SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 1, Special Branch Shanghai, //
REPORT
Date January 12, 19 37
File No. ............

Subject Communication dated 6-1-37 from the "Council of the United Russian
Public Organization of Shanghai" (SORO) concerning Mrs L. BARD.
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by [Signature]

Mrs Lia Ruvimovna BARD, Russian of Jewish origin, was
born on December 15, 1888 at Sebastopol, Russia. She first ar-
rived in Shanghai from Harbin on February 23, 1936 in the S.S.
"Dairen Maru". and has since been residing in this city with
the exception of the period from July to August 31, 1936 when
she was absent to Harbin.

From the Alien Passport Declaration Form she filled up
prior to disembarking it appears that she was in possession of
emigrant's passport No 145 issued on 12-2-36 at Harbin. In
Shanghai she registered with the Public Safety Bureau through the
medium of the "Council of the United Russian Public Organization "
(SORO) on the date of her arrival.

It is reported that Mrs Bard's husband, M. Bard, a merchant,
passed through Shanghai early in 1936 en route from Harbin to Ar-
gentine. She has two sons: Leo M. Bard, proprietor of the Bard & Co,
Opticians, 1159 Buboling Well Road, and Solomon M. Bard, 20, who
is reported to be in Honkong at present, where he continues his
education. Mrs Bard's brother, D.trumson, a musician, has been
employed with the S.M.C. Orchestra for the past four years.

Nothing detrimental is known in this office regarding
the Bard family either politically or criminally.

D. Prokopiew
D. S. I.

D.C. ( Special Branch )

事由：1937年1月6日来自“上海俄侨公共联合会”（SORO）关于 L. BARD 夫人的公函。
呈报人：侦探副督察 Prokofiev。 转呈人：[签名]

莉亚·鲁维莫夫娜·巴德（Lia Ruvimovna BARD）夫人，俄籍犹太人，1888年12月15日出生于俄罗斯塞瓦斯托波尔。她于1936年2月23日首次从哈尔滨乘“大连丸”（Dairen Maru）轮抵达上海，此后一直居住在本市，惟1936年7月至8月31日期间曾前往哈尔滨，不在此列。

从其下船前填写的外侨护照申报表中可知，她持有1936年2月12日在哈尔滨签发的第145号移民护照。抵达上海当日，她通过“上海俄侨公共联合会”（SORO）向公共安全局进行了登记。

据报，巴德夫人的丈夫 M. Bard 先生是一名商人，于1936年初从哈尔滨前往阿根廷途中经过上海。她有两个儿子：利奥·M·巴德（Leo M. Bard），卜罗林路（Buboling Well Road）1159号巴德眼镜行（Bard & Co, Opticians）店主；以及所罗门·M·巴德（Solomon M. Bard），20岁，据报目前在香港继续学业。巴德夫人的兄弟 D.trumson（音译）是一名音乐家，过去四年受雇于工部局乐队。

本处所知，巴德家族在政治或刑事方面均无不良记录。

D. Prokopiew
侦探副督察

助理处长（特务科）

de la
República Argentina.

Kobe, October 31st 1936.

Bard & Co.,
1159 Bubblig Well Road.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir:
        We are in reciept of yours dated on the 21st, Oct.,
inquiring the way to enter in Argentina.
        As I just been appointed here I am not yet well
informed about if your family is registred in this General
Consulate but any how, when your mother will come here we will
do our best for her.

        Your certificate issued by Harbin Police is not good
now as it is already cancel because is dated on the 17th.
February 1936, so is got more than six months old; any one of
yours wants to travel to Argentina needs NEW CERTIFICATE FROM
THE POLICE.

Yours very truly.
Enrique Ross
Argentine Consul.

FB/st.

神户，1936年10月31日。

巴德公司（Bard & Co.），
上海，卜布利格威尔路（Bubblig Well Road）1159号。

尊敬的先生：

我方已收到您10月21日的来信，询问进入阿根廷的途径。
由于我刚刚在此就任，尚不完全清楚您的家人是否在本总领事馆登记，但无论如何，当您母亲来到这里时，我们将尽力为她提供帮助。

您持有的由哈尔滨警方签发的证明书目前已无效，因其已被注销，且签发日期为1936年2月17日，已超过六个月；任何欲前往阿根廷的人士均需新的警方证明书。

此致
最诚挚的问候。

恩里克·罗斯（Enrique Ross）
阿根廷领事。

FB/st.

ROYAL DANISH CONSULATE-GENERAL
SHANGHAI.

Shanghai 18. February 1937

J. No. 35 N 1
No. S ____ . ____ . ____
Date ____ . ____ . ____
〔此处转录不清〕

Sir,

A Danish subject, Mr. Wilfred Madsen, born the
25th March 1895 at Shanghai, has applied for my assistance
to obtain a certificate from the Shanghai Police, certi-
fying his good conduct during the last five years of his
stay here.

Mr. Wilfred Madsen has stated to me that he left
Shanghai for Japan in May 1935 and has only returned a few
days ago. His present address is: 36 G Brenan Road, Park
View Apartments, and the period to be covered by the cer-
tificate should be the five years before his departure for
Japan in 1935. At that time his address was: 395/8 Route
Frelupt.

I may add that nothing unfavourable has been
brought to the knowledge of this Consulate General about
Mr. Wilfred Madsen's conduct.

I should be much obliged to receive the certif-
icate in duplicate.

At the same time I have addressed a similar let-
ter to the Director of the French Municipal Police.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

〔签名〕
Consul General.

The Commissioner,
The Shanghai Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

先生，

一名丹麦籍公民威尔弗雷德·马森先生，1895年3月25日出生于上海，已申请我方协助，以获取上海警方出具的一份证明，证实其在此居住期间过去五年的良好行为。

威尔弗雷德·马森先生向我陈述，他于1935年5月离开上海前往日本，并于数日前刚刚返回。他目前的地址是：公园景公寓（Park View Apartments），格伦南路（Brenan Road）36号G室；证明书所涵盖的时期应为其1935年赴日之前五年。当时他的地址是：法雷普路（Route Frelupt）395/8号。

我可以补充说明，本总领事馆未获悉任何关于威尔弗雷德·马森先生行为的不利情况。

如能收到两份该证明书，我将不胜感激。

同时，我也已向法国市政警察局局长致函类似信件。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，

〔签名〕
总领事。

致总监，
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。

Vol. C. 6067 /
Date 22/ 3 / 37

REGISTRY
No. S. G. D. 8264/25
Date ____

The Commissioner of Police,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sir,
re: CHARLES HEINRICH EMIL PLATOW.

The above gentleman arrived in the Union of South Africa in October, 1934, under contract of employment to us for a period of two years, on the termination of which it was renewed by both parties.

Upon arrival in the Union of South Africa the Immigration authorities here refused to admit him as an immigrant under the Quota Act, in view of his birth place being Warsaw he is classified as a Polish citizen, although he is of German parentage, and holds a German passport.

To conform to the regulations of the Union Immigration Act it was necessary to obtain certain documents which include a Police Certificate in duplicate which we attach hereto certifying to his conduct at the last place of residence.

These Certificates were duly forwarded by us to the German Consulate General at Shanghai early in 1935 in reply to which we received the attached letter marked "Exhibit 1." We also attach hereto copy of a letter received from his employers during the time he was in Shanghai, namely, Messrs. Kofa American Drug Co., which is marked "Exhibit B."

Mr. Platow has been allowed temporary permits which have been extended from time to time during the past two and a half years, and his present permit expires on the 30th June of this year. The Government of the Union of South Africa have recently passed a new Immigration Act whereby it is necessary for all intending immigrants, holding permits, to apply for admission, and failing such admission being accepted by the Board of Control

日期 ____

致上海警务处处长，
上海。

尊敬的先生：
事由：查尔斯·海因里希·埃米尔·普拉托夫（CHARLES HEINRICH EMIL PLATOW）。

上述先生于1934年10月抵达南非联邦，根据与我们签订的为期两年的雇佣合同受聘于此，合同期满后双方又予以续签。

抵达南非联邦后，此地的移民当局依据《配额法》拒绝接纳其为移民。鉴于其出生地为华沙，他被归类为波兰公民，尽管他拥有德国血统并持有德国护照。

为了符合南非联邦移民法的规定，必须获取某些文件，其中包括两份警方证明书，兹随函附上，以证明其在最后居住地的行为表现。

这些证明书已由我方于1935年初正式转交至驻上海的德国总领事馆，作为回复，我们收到了附后的标记为“证据1”的信件。我们还随函附上他在上海期间从其雇主处收到的一封信的副本，即科发美国药房（Messrs. Kofa American Drug Co.），标记为“证据B”。

在过去两年半的时间里，普拉托夫先生获准持有临时许可证，并多次延期，其当前许可证将于今年6月30日到期。南非联邦政府最近通过了一项新的移民法，据此，所有持许可证的意向移民必须申请入境许可，如果管制委员会（Board of Control）

2/ ____

pages.en:
- 2 -
D8204/25
The Commissioner of Police, Shanghai. 24.2.37

appointed by the Union Government they will be compelled to leave
the Union upon the expiration of their permit.

Mr. Platow's conduct while he has been with us has been ex-
emplary, and you will notice the same applies during his residence
in Shanghai, save and except that he had the misfortune to have a
motor accident on the Hangchow Road to which unfortunately there
were no witnesses. The question as to whether he was to blame
has never been proved, and he asserts that he did everything poss-
ible to avoid the accident in that he swerved to the right with
almost fatal results to himself. In seeking to ascertain why he
did not remain in Shanghai and stand his trial he states that he
left the country on the advice of the German Consulate together
with that of his former employers, Messrs. Kofa American Drug Co.,
and the advice of his attorneys who stated that in all probability
as there were no witnesses he would have been convicted.

We have endeavoured in the aforegoing to set out the case as
clearly as possible, and request if it is at all possible that
you will complete the attached Certificates and return them to us
in order that we may conform to the Union Immigration Act.

Any further information you may require we shall be only too
glad to furnish.

Yours faithfully,
STINNES AGENCIES (PTY.) LTD.

〔此处为手写签名〕
DIRECTOR.

SFR/AM

P.S. You will note that the Police Report certifies that the
party has not been convicted of any crime or misdemeanour, and
as Mr. Platow has not been convicted of any crime, we shall be
glad if you will kindly sign the report.

〔此处为手写签名〕

不接受此类入境申请，他们将在许可证期满时被强制离开
南非联邦。

普拉托夫先生在我们这里工作期间的行为堪称模范，
您会注意到，他在上海居住期间也是如此，除了
他不幸在杭州路发生了一起车祸，不幸的是当时没有
目击者。关于他是否负有责任的问题从未得到证实，
他声称自己已尽一切可能避免事故，即向右急转弯，
结果几乎导致自己丧命。在试图查明他为何不留在上海
接受审判时，他表示，他是根据德国领事馆的建议，
以及其前雇主科发美国药房（Messrs. Kofa American Drug Co.）
和他的律师的建议离开该国的，律师指出，由于没有
目击者，他很可能会被定罪。

我们在上文中力求尽可能清楚地陈述案情，并请求
您在可能的情况下填写所附证明书并退还给我们，以便
我们遵守南非联邦移民法。

如您需要任何进一步的信息，我们将非常乐意提供。

此致，
施廷内斯代理有限公司（STINNES AGENCIES (PTY.) LTD.）

〔此处为手写签名〕
董事。

Dear Sirs,

In reply to your letter SFF/CB. of the 21st
of May I regret to inform you that I cannot procure a
Certificate of Conduct from the local Police Authorities
for Mr. H.C.R. P l a t o w for the following reason.
While motoring from Hangchow to Shanghai in November 1933
this gentleman had the misfortune to run an old Chinese
farmer down with fatal results. The criminal action
following this incident in the Chinese Law Court of Shanghai
was avoided by Mr. Platow who in consequence left China
without further notice for Germany. As the suit against
him is still pending and will be taken up immediately in case
Mr. Platow should ever return to China, there is no
possibility to get the required certificate from the Shanghai
Municipal Police.

The question whether Mr. Platow is to blame for
negligent driving or whether the accident has been caused
by circumstances beyond his control has never been
established. No doubt Mr. Platow will be in a position
to give you all the details of the case himself. Otherwise
nothing unfavourable is known about him at this Consulate
General.

Yours faithfully,

.........
CONSUL GENERAL FOR GERMANY.

中国法院引发的刑事诉讼被普拉托夫先生规避，他因此
在未作进一步通知的情况下离开中国前往德国。由于针对
他的诉讼仍未结案，一旦普拉托夫先生返回中国，该案将
立即重启，因此不可能从上海公共租界工部局警务处获得

普拉托夫先生能够亲自向你们提供该案的所有细节。否则，

Dear Sirs:

This acknowledges receipt of your letter of 4th
January last, addressed to our Manager, Mr. W. Pflug, inform-
ing us that the Union Immigration Authorities require certain
formalities before Mr. H. Platow, now in your employ, may be
permanently admitted into the Union of South Africa and that
in addition to the deposition made by your goodselves, a
certificate from the Police Authorities certifying Mr. Platow's
character, will be needed.

In reply thereto we beg to inform you that we would
be only too glad to comply with your request, but are unable
to do so as the Police of the Shanghai Settlements does not
keep a record of Foreigners and Chinese residents. As Mr.
Platow can confirm the Shanghai Concession is divided into
The International Settlement and French Settlement, apart from
the Native City, (Shanghai, Greater Shanghai.) The Inter-
national Settlement of Shanghai, wherein our offices and most
of the Foreign and Chinese Business Hongs are situated, is
governed by the Municipal Council Administration, elected
yearly by the Foreign Ratepayers and consisting of 5 British,
2 American, 2 Japanese and 5 Chinese Councillors, while the
adjoining French Concession is governed on similar lines, but
under supreme control of the French Consul General. Neither
the Police of the International, nor of the French Settlement
are keeping a register of Foreigners or Chinese residing therein
and for said reason are not in a position to issue a certificate
as to the character and well behaviour of the many hundred of
thousands of residents.

As already certified in Mr. Platow's testimonial
issued by this company, Mr. Platow has been employed in a
responsible and trustworthy position from the 1st January, 1928,

你们自身的证词外，还需要一份由警察当局出具的证明普拉托夫
先生品行的证书。

对此，我们谨告知，我们非常乐意满足你们的请求，但无法做到，
因为上海租界的警察并不保存外国人和中国居民的记录。正如
普拉托夫先生可以证实的那样，上海租界除华界（上海、大上海）
外，分为公共租界和法租界。我们的办事处以及大多数外商和华商
字号所在的上海公共租界，由工部局行政管理，该局由外籍纳税人
每年选举产生，由5名英国人、2名美国人、2名日本人和5名中国人
组成；而相邻的法租界也按类似方式管理，但在法国总领事的最高
管辖之下。无论是公共租界还是法租界的警察，都不保存居住在其中
的外国人或中国人的登记册，因此出于上述原因，无法就数十万居民
的品行和良好行为出具证明书。

先生自1928年1月1日起担任负责任且值得信赖的职位，

The Commissioner of Police,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sir,
re: CHARLES HEINRICH EMIL PLATOW.

The above gentleman arrived in the Union of South Africa in October, 1934, under contract of employment to us for a period of two years, on the termination of which it was renewed by both parties.

Upon arrival in the Union of South Africa the Immigration authorities here refused to admit him as an immigrant under the Quota Act, in view of his birth place being Warsaw he is classified as a Polish citizen, although he is of German parentage, and holds a German passport.

To conform to the regulations of the Union Immigration Act it was necessary to obtain certain documents which include a Police Certificate in duplicate which we attach hereto certifying to his conduct at the last place of residence.

These Certificates were duly forwarded by us to the German Consulate General at Shanghai early in 1935 in reply to which we received the attached letter marked "Exhibit 1." We also attach hereto copy of a letter received from his employers during the time he was in Shanghai, namely, Messrs. Kofa American Drug Co., which is marked "Exhibit B."

Mr. Platow has been allowed temporary permits which have been extended from time to time during the past two and a half years, and his present permit expires on the 30th June of this year. The Government of the Union of South Africa have recently passed a new Immigration Act whereby it is necessary for all intending immigrants, holding permits, to apply for admission, and failing such admission being accepted by the Board of Control

事由：查尔斯·海因里希·埃米尔·普拉托夫（CHARLES HEINRICH EMIL PLATOW）。

上述先生于1934年10月抵达南非联邦，根据与我们签订的为期两年的雇佣合同受聘于此，合同期满后双方又予以续签。

抵达南非联邦后，此地的移民当局依据《配额法》拒绝接纳其为移民。鉴于其出生地为华沙，他被归类为波兰公民，尽管他拥有德国血统并持有德国护照。

为了符合南非联邦移民法的规定，必须获取某些文件，其中包括两份警方证明书，兹随函附上，以证明其在最后居住地的行为表现。

这些证明书已由我方于1935年初正式转交至驻上海的德国总领事馆，作为回复，我们收到了附后的标记为“证据1”的信件。我们还随函附上他在上海期间从其雇主处收到的一封信的副本，即科发美国药房（Messrs. Kofa American Drug Co.），标记为“证据B。”

普拉托夫先生获准持有临时许可证，并在过去两年半的时间里多次延期，其当前许可证将于今年6月30日到期。南非联邦政府最近通过了一项新的移民法，据此，所有持许可证的意向移民必须申请入境许可，如果管制委员会（Board of Control）

Mr. Platow's conduct while he has been with us has been ex-
emplary, and you will notice the same applies during his residence
in Shanghai, save and except that he had the misfortune to have a
motor accident on the Hangchow Road to which unfortunately there
were no witnesses. The question as to whether he was to blame
has never been proved, and he asserts that he did everything poss-
ible to avoid the accident in that he swerved to the right with
almost fatal results to himself. In seeking to ascertain why he
did not remain in Shanghai and stand his trial he states that he
left the country on the advice of the German Consulate together
with that of his former employers, Messrs. Kofa American Drug Co.,
and the advice of his attorneys who stated that in all probability
as there were no witnesses he would have been convicted.

We have endeavoured in the aforegoing to set out the case as
clearly as possible, and request if it is at all possible that
you will complete the attached Certificates and return them to us
in order that we may conform to the Union Immigration Act.

Any further information you may require we shall be only too
glad to furnish.

Yours faithfully,
STINNES AGENCIES (PTY.) LTD.

Date March 24, 1937.

Subject N.J. Boxer, applicant for letter of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by J. Boyne

Enquiries show that Naum (Nahem) Jacob BOXER is a
Russian of Jewish origin who was born on May 27, 1910
in Herson Province, South Russia. He arrived in Shanghai
from Harbin on January 10, 1936 in the s.s. "Tsingtao
Maru". On 23/1/36 he registered with the Public Safety
Bureau as a Russian emigrant on the strength of residential
permit No.29349/6886 issued by the Harbin authorities on
30/8/35.

During the period of his sojourn in Shanghai Boxer,
who claims to be a railway engineer, has been unemployed.
He resides at 1191 Bubbling Well Road (Apt. 4-A) together
with his sister, Mrs. A. Shpiro, divorcee, proprietress of
the "Ann's Medical Cosmetic Institute & Laboratory" at
that address, whom he assists in her business. His
parents are reported to be residing in Harbin.

On 23/2/37 Boxer registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, to which he was recommended
by Mr. M. Marderfeld, 458 Szechuen Road, merchant and an
old resident of Shanghai.

While in Shanghai Boxer did not come to the notice
of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities
of an undesirable character.

G. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

C.P.
D.C. (Special Branch). No objection in regard to character
so far as known to Police.

24 MAR. 1937
DEPUTY COMMISSIONER
(SPECIAL BRANCH)

经查，Naum (Nahem) Jacob BOXER 系犹太裔俄国人，1910年5月27日出生于俄国南部赫尔松省 (Herson Province)。他于1936年1月10日乘坐“青岛丸”号轮船 (s.s. "Tsingtao Maru") 从哈尔滨抵达上海。1936年1月23日，他凭哈尔滨当局于1935年8月30日签发的第29349/6886号居住证，以俄国移民身份在公共安全局登记。

Boxer 自称铁路工程师，但在沪期间一直失业。他与姐姐 A. Shpiro 夫人（离异）同住于静安寺路1191号（4-A室）。Shpiro 夫人在该地址经营“Ann's Medical Cosmetic Institute & Laboratory”（安氏医学美容研究所及实验室），Boxer 协助其业务。据报，其父母居住在哈尔滨。

1937年2月23日，Boxer 在四川路458号商人、上海老居民 M. Marderfeld 先生的推荐下，向莫尔尼姆路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记。

Boxer 在沪期间，未因任何不良行为引起工部局警务处的注意。

G. Prokofiev

REPORT . Date May 12, 1937.

Subject Miss Eva LIPKOVSKY - Application for certificate of character.

Made by D.S. Larby Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

With reference to the attached letter dated 1-5-37, from
one M. LIPKOVSKY, Municipal Police records contain nothing of
detriment to the name of Miss Eva LIPKOVSKY.

Miss LIPKOVSKY, who, it is learned, has been residing in
the U.S.A. for the past 15 months, had in her possession a
Chinese Passport (Russian Emigrant's) which has now expired
and which the Chinese Consular Authorities in New York refuse
to renew.

Faced with the prospect of having to leave the U.S.A. -
the U.S. Bureau of Immigration have allowed her an extension of
6 months' stay - Miss LIPKOVSKY is endeavouring to become a
citizen of the U.S.A., and it is to satisfy the U.S.Government
Authorities that nothing of a disparaging nature is associated
with her name, that the above mentioned certificate is
required.

Her father, M.LIPKOVSKY, Manager of "Cathay Jewellery,"
2 Kiangse Road, has been the subject of a number of police
reports in connection with the smuggling of narcotics and
jewellery, and other dealings of a fraudulent nature. He has
not, however, any actual criminal record, insofar as the S.M.P.
are concerned.

The above paragraph may be of interest in view of the
fact that LIPKOVSKY, himself, states that the presence of his
daughter in the U.S.A. has been of assistance to him in the
settlement of a number of transactions relating to the
purchasing and selling of jewellery.

D. S. Larby
D. S.

呈报人：副巡长 Larby (D.S. Larby) 转呈人：**〔此处转录不清〕**

关于所附1937年5月1日来信，发信人为 M. LIPKOVSKY，警方档案中无任何不利于 Eva LIPKOVSKY 小姐名声的记录。

据悉，Lipkovsky 小姐过去15个月居住在美国，她持有一本已过期的中国护照（俄国移民类），纽约的中国领事当局拒绝为其续期。

鉴于必须离开美国的局面——美国移民局已允许其延期停留6个月——Lipkovsky 小姐正努力成为美国公民。上述证明书之所需，旨在向美国政府当局证明其名声无任何贬损之处。

其父 M. LIPKOVSKY，江西路2号“Cathay Jewellery”（华懋首饰店）经理，曾因走私毒品和珠宝及其他欺诈性质交易而多次成为警方报告的对象。然而，就工部局警务处而言，他并无任何实际犯罪记录。

鉴于 Lipkovsky 本人声称，其女儿在美国的存在有助于他解决多项珠宝买卖交易，上述段落可能具有参考价值。

In accordance with the instructions of the Deputy
Commissioner (Special Branch), the attached file was shown to
the United States Marshal, Mr. Edward L. Faupel, on the 14th
May, 1937.
Mr. Faupel expressed the view that the U.S. authorities
would have no objection to the Municipal Police issuing a
certificate as requested; he further stated that in the event of
the S.M.P. so doing, and in view of Mr. Lipkovsky's reputation
and his recent assertion anent his daughter's usefulness to him
in his jewellery transactions, he would at once inform the U.S.
authorities in Washington (D.C.), who would be able to make any
arrangements necessary for the checking of the movements of
Miss Lipkovsky.
The present address of Miss Lipkovsky is as follows :-
Apartment 2d,

New York City, U.S.A.

D. S.

Subject Re Albert Michael Raskin. 800 / 22.
23 / 7 / 37
Made by D.S.I. Rhind Forwarded by Supt. MacDermott.

Sir,
Albert Michael Raskin, age about 37, came to Shanghai
in 1914 from Manchuria accompanied by his parents for the purpose
of continuing his education. He became a pupil of the Thomas
Hanbury School for boys which he left in 1919 to join the firm
of Messrs. Edward Evans & Sons Ltd, then situated at 30 Szechuen
Road. Later, in partnership with his brother, he established
an Import and Export business which operated on a very small scale
and which finally failed. He then went to London where he
obtained employment with a firm known as Messrs. W.J.Richard
and Sons as a travelling salesman in the Malay States & Java.
Leaving this firm in 1926, he obtained a position with Messrs
Kornetzer & Bros. Diamond Merchants, Singapore, which went into
liquidation a few months afterwards and then he entered another
（印：RECEIVED M.SICKLEFF 21 SEP 1937 (C.A.)）firm of diamond merchants known as Buchenholz & Company,
acting as their agent until October, 1926, when he returned to
Shanghai. Before leaving Singapore, however, he made a
report to the local police of the loss of 900 small loose diamonds
valued about $8,000.00, the property of his firm. The Singapore
Police regarded the circumstances of the alleged loss as very
suspicious and his firm held him liable for 50 per cent of the
value of the diamonds. On his arrival in Shanghai, he went
to live with his parents at their boarding house at 34 Haskell
Road. At present he is employed with The China Engineers Ltd
with whom he has served for the past 3½ years.

Raskin's parents are said to be a respectable Russian
Jewish family. So far as can be ascertained nothing is known
to his detriment locally apart from the fact that the Singapore
Police expressed the opinion that the circumstances in which he
allegedly lost the diamonds in 1926 were very suspicious.

S.I.
D.B.

先生，
阿尔伯特·迈克尔·拉斯金，年龄约37岁，于1914年随父母从满洲来到上海，目的是继续学业。他成为汤玛斯·汉伯里男校（Thomas Hanbury School for boys）的学生，1919年离校后加入当时位于四川路30的爱德华·埃文斯父子有限公司（Messrs. Edward Evans & Sons Ltd）。后来，他与兄弟合伙经营一家进出口商行，规模很小，最终倒闭。随后他前往伦敦，在一家名为 W.J.理查德父子公司（Messrs. W.J.Richard and Sons）的企业任职，担任马来亚邦和爪哇地区的旅行推销员。1926年离开该公司后，他在新加坡的科内策尔兄弟钻石商（Messrs Kornetzer & Bros. Diamond Merchants, Singapore）获得职位，但该公司几个月后便进入清算程序，之后他又进入另一家
（印：1937年9月21日 M.SICKLEFF 收讫 (C.A.)）名为布肯霍尔茨公司（Buchenholz & Company）的钻石商行，担任其代理人，直至1926年10月返回上海。然而，在离开新加坡之前，他曾向当地警方报告丢失了属于其公司的900颗散装小钻石，价值约8,000.00美元。新加坡警方认为所谓丢失的情况非常可疑，其公司要求他承担钻石价值50%的责任。抵达上海后，他与其父母同住，地址为赫斯克尔路34号的寄宿公寓。目前，他受雇于中国工程师有限公司（The China Engineers Ltd），已为其服务过去3年半。

据称，拉斯金的父母是一个受人尊敬的俄罗斯犹太家庭。据查，除了新加坡警方曾表示意见，认为他1926年所谓丢失钻石的情况非常可疑外，本地方面并未发现对他不利的记录。

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev    Forwarded by C. Crawford

with reference to the endorsement of the D.C.
(Crime & Special Branches) on the attached report dated 17-9-37
I have to state that Albert Mihailovich ( Abram Haimovich)
MASKIN, Russian of Jewish origin, at present residing at 461
Avenue Joffre, apt. 53, did not come to the notice of this office
in connection with activities of a political nature.
He is registered at the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau as a Russian emigrant ( Reg. 4412 of 3-9-1932),
but during the past five years did not apply for renewal of his
registration.
His father, M.G. ( A. G. ) Maskin, who died about
three months ago in Shanghai at the age of 75 years, is mentioned
in Intelligence Report dated 17-1-1927 as " a well known local
Russian communist whose boarding house at No. 37 Haskell Road
is frequented by Soviet agents". It appears, however, that this
statement was based solely on the fact that his boarding house
was patronized by Soviet employees in 1925-1929. As a matter
of fact it is known that he furnished to members of the Municipal
Police information regarding the inmates of his boarding house.

A. Prokofiev
D.S.I.

Special Branch - Station,
REPORT
Date October 8, 19 37.

Subject Communication from Mr. Benjamin SHMULEVSKY requesting a
certificate of character.

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by

With reference to the contents of the attached letter
addressed to the Commissioner of Police I have to report that
Veniamin Voulfovoch SHMULEVSKY, or as he is now known
Benjamin SHMULEVSKY, is a Russian of Jewish extraction born
on October 10, 1892 at Nerchinsk, Siberia. His parents
were wealthy people who were able to give him an extensive
technical education. From 1913 until 1918 he studied phar-
maceutical chemistry at Tomsk University and succeeded in
obtaining the Government degree of 'assistant chemist.'
With the incidence of the Russian Revolution, SHMULEVSKY
was forced to abandon his studies, and as a result came to China,
arriving in Shanghai in May 1919. Shortly after arrival here,
he was employed as a dispensing chemist with Messrs. Allen &
Hanbury's Ltd., a post which he vacated after some nine months
in order to join Messrs. The American Drug Co. (KOFA), with
which concern he remained for approximately six years. Both
these companies speak highly of their ex-employee's character,
ability and honesty.
In 1925 SHMULEVSKY established THE STAR PHARMACY at
837 Avenue Joffre. This concern is well known locally as
high-class dispensing chemists and druggists and as such
enjoys an excellent reputation. SHMULEVSKY, the owner, is
the chief chemist, and is well spoken of in many well-to-do
circles in Shanghai. Financially, he is well off and
has no debts or commitments beyond his monthly accounts with
wholesalers.
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee,
and as far as can be ascertained evinces not the slightest
interest in politics of any kind.

（左侧手写批注：）
I have
usual
reply.
Sy.

事由：本杰明·什穆列夫斯基（Benjamin SHMULEVSKY）先生请求开具品行证明的信函。

由警司皮茨（D.S. Pitts）制作，由____转呈

参照致警务总监的附件信函内容，本人须报告如下：韦尼亚明·沃尔福维奇·什穆列夫斯基（Veniamin Voulfovoch SHMULEVSKY），即现在所称的本杰明·什穆列夫斯基（Benjamin SHMULEVSKY），系犹太裔俄罗斯人，1892年10月10日出生于西伯利亚涅尔琴斯克。其父母家境富裕，能够为他提供广泛的技术教育。1913年至1918年，他在托木斯克大学学习药物化学，并成功获得政府颁发的“助理化学师”学位。随着俄国革命的爆发，什穆列夫斯基被迫放弃学业，因此来到中国，于1919年5月抵达上海。抵沪后不久，他受雇于艾伦与汉伯里有限公司（Messrs. Allen & Hanbury's Ltd.）担任配药化学师，约九个月后离职，加入美国大药房（KOFA）（Messrs. The American Drug Co. (KOFA)），在该机构工作约六年。这两家公司对其前雇员的品行、能力和诚实度均给予高度评价。
1925年，什穆列夫斯基在霞飞路837号创办了“明星药房”（THE STAR PHARMACY）。该机构在当地以高档配药化学师和药剂师闻名，享有极佳的声誉。业主什穆列夫斯基是首席化学师，在上海许多富裕阶层中口碑良好。经济上，他生活宽裕，除每月与批发商的账目往来外，无其他债务或负担。
他在俄罗斯流亡者委员会注册，据查，他对任何政治都毫无兴趣。

（左侧手写批注：）
我已
常规
回复。
Sy.

Married in November 1919 SHMULEVSKY has a daughter
aged 17 years and a son of 14, who both have excellent
school records, and it is believed that it is an effort
to give his offspring a better chance in life as the children
of a father with nationality, that he has applied to the
American authorities for permission to enter America, where
he hopes event l'' to acquire naturalisation. At present
he has the usual passport issued to Russian Emigrants by
the Chinese authorities, and which describes him as being
of 'no nationality.' He has a number of relatives
in the United States, all of whom have promised him
assistance - not financial -in commencing business there.
A resident of Shanghai for some 18 years, SHMULEVSKY
is of good character, a respectable member of the community,
and has never been convicted of any criminal or political
offence, or committed to any institution for crime or
incompetence.

什穆列夫斯基于1919年11月结婚，育有一女17岁，一子14岁，两人学业成绩优异。据信，他为了让子女作为有国籍父亲的子女获得更好的人生机会，已向美国当局申请入境许可，希望最终在美国获得归化入籍。目前，他持有中国当局发给俄罗斯流亡者的通常护照，上面注明其为“无国籍”。他在美国有多位亲属，均承诺在他那里开始经商时提供协助——非金钱援助。

如蒙惠赐签发上述证明书，以便将其连同我的其他文件及入境申请一并寄往澳大利亚，我将不胜感激。

此致，

V. Gavriloff

Mihail Ivanovich YOUHOTSKY, Russian, was born on
October 9, 1900, at Irkutsk, Siberia. He is reported to
have left Russia for China in 1922 and to have subsequently
resided in Harbin where he studied at the Polytechnic
Institute. Upon graduating he continued his education in
America for about one year. Returning to Harbin in 1929
he was attached to the Polytechnic Institute for about two
years and was also employed with the Harbin branch of
Andersen, Meyer & Co., Ltd.

In October, 1932, Youhotsky arrived in Shanghai
from Harbin. Here he was employed for various periods
with A. Corrit, 278 Kiangsi Road, Davies, Brooke & Gran,
81 Jinkee Road, Credit Foncier d'Extreme Orient and Leonard,
Veyssyere & Kruze, 461 Avenue Joffre. In July, 1935, he
left for Sianfu, Shensi Province, together with another
Russian engineer named G.A. Shestakoff. Both were employed
at the construction of a governmental building (College for
Agriculture ?) at Wukung, about forty miles from Sianfu.
Youhotsky returned in Shanghai in July, 1936 and from
September of the same year has been employed with Andersen,
Meyer & Co., 21/43 Yuen Ming Yuen Road.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee. His wife, Mrs. O.A. Youhotsky, and their two
daughters reside at Tsingtao together with his parents.
Mrs. Youhotsky is reported to conduct a beauty parlour in
that city.

While in Shanghai he did not come to the notice of
the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an
undesirable character.

A. Prokojiev

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by [签名]

Vladimir Alexandrovich GAVRILOFF, Russian, was born
on July 3, 1893, in Kazan District, Russia. He is reported
to have arrived in Shanghai from Russia in 1918. After a
short stay in this city he proceeded to Hankow where he
subsequently was employed for several years with the Municipal
Council of the Ex-Russian Concession as an assistant secretary.

In September, 1927, he came to Shanghai. It is reported
that his departure from Hankow was very sudden and that it was
due to the discovery of certain irregularities of a fraudulent
nature in the account books for which Gavriloff was responsible.
No charge was preferred against Gavriloff in connection with
this matter, but his superannuation fund is reported to have
been confiscated by the Municipality in order to cover the
damages resulting from the irregularities referred to above.

In Shanghai Gavriloff was employed with the Public
Works Department, Shanghai Municipal Council, as an assistant
Clerk of Works from 1930 to 1936 when his services were
dispensed with owing to a reduction in staff. His next employ-
ment was with the Unit Furniture Co., 213-A Route Cardinal
Mercier, and at present he is reported to be temporarily
employed with the Shanghai Power Company.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee
and at present resides at 26 Temple Lane, Apt. 15 together
with his wife, Mrs. O. A. Gavriloff, and their daughter 18 years
of age.

While in Shanghai he did not come to the notice of the
Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an
undesirable character.

1927年9月，他来到上海。据报他离开汉口非常突然，原因是发现了他负责的账簿中存在某些欺诈性质的违规行为。此事未对 Gavriloff 提出指控，但据报他的退休金已被工部局没收，以弥补上述违规行为造成的损失。

在上海，Gavriloff 于1930年至1936年间受雇于上海工部局工务处，担任助理监工员，后因裁员而被解雇。他的下一份工作是受雇于麦赛尔福脱路213-A号的 Unit Furniture Co.，据报目前他暂时受雇于上海电力公司。

他已在俄国侨民委员会登记，目前与妻子 O. A. Gavriloff 夫人及他们18岁的女儿一同居住在庙街26弄15号。

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I

Enquiries show that Joseph Samuilovich ZALMANOFF
is a Soviet citizen of Jewish origin who was born on October 20,
1915 at Harbin. He is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin on November 9, 1935. When registering with the Shanghai
City Government Police Bureau he produced Passport No 9538 issued
on 24-10-35 by the Soviet Consulate-General in Harbin and Residen-
tial Certificate No 40462 issued on 18-7-35 by the Harbin Police.
On 15-11-35 he was issued by the S.C.G. Police Bureau with Certi-
ficate of Registration No 17042.

In summer, 1936 Zalmanoff obtained from the local
American Consulate-General a visa to enable him to proceed to Ca-
lifornia, U.S.A., in order to continue his education and on July 5
1936 he left for San Francisco in the s.s. "Asama Maru."

While in Shanghai he was unemployed and resided
first at 7/3 Rue Paul Henry and later at 651 Weihaiwei Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
against this person.

经查，约瑟夫·萨穆伊洛维奇·扎尔马诺夫（Joseph Samuilovich ZALMANOFF）系犹太裔苏联公民，1915年10月20日出生于哈尔滨。据报他于1935年11月9日从哈尔滨抵达上海。在向上海市政府警察局登记时，他出示了由苏联驻哈尔滨总领事馆于1935年10月24日签发的第9538号护照，以及由哈尔滨警察机关于1935年7月18日签发的第40462号居住证。1935年11月15日，上海市政府警察局向他签发了第17042号登记证。

Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by C Crawford

With reference to the contents of the attached
communication dated November 22, 1937, I have to report
that Miss Stella LEVY, British Jewess, desires to secure
a Certificate of Character in order to complete her
arrangements for entering the United States of America
under the immigration quota.
Born in Hongkong 27 years ago, Miss Levy has been a
resident of Shanghai, on and off, for the past ten years.
She is known to be a woman of irreproachable character
and has never come to the notice of the Municipal Police
in an unfavourable light. She has never been convicted
of any crime here nor committed to any institution for
incompetence.
By profession a stenographer, Miss Levy's last post
was with Messrs. Manufacturers Life Insurance Company,
Hamilton House, Foochow Road. She left this concern
on September 30, 1937, retiring voluntarily, after having
served the company for over two years. She is highly
spoken of in this organisation.

由副巡官皮茨（D.S. Pitts）撰写。由克劳福德（C Crawford）转呈

鉴于所附1937年11月22日来函的内容，我必须报告，英国籍犹太女子斯特拉·莱维（Stella LEVY）小姐希望获得一份品行证明书，以完成其根据移民配额进入美利坚合众国的安排。
莱维小姐27年前出生于香港，在过去十年中断断续续居住在上海。众所周知，她是一位品行无可指责的女性，从未在工部局警务处留下不良记录。她在此地从未因任何罪行被定罪，也从未因精神失常被送入任何机构。
莱维小姐的职业是速记员，她最后的职位是在福州路汉密尔顿大厦（Hamilton House）的制造商人寿保险公司（Messrs. Manufacturers Life Insurance Company）。她在该公司服务两年多后，于1937年9月30日自愿离职。她在这家机构中备受赞誉。

贾·皮茨
副巡官。

（左侧批注：29.11.）
副警务总监（特务科）。

Subject E.F. Nevessky - application for a letter of character.

Made by D.S. Tcheremstansky    Forwarded by C. Garsia

Ilia (Elias) Franzevich Nevessky, Russian, was born
on August 2, 1895 at Jitomir, South Russia and is a son of
a farmer. He attended a school in Jitomir for four years
after which from 1912 to 1916 he was employed as a clerk in
the Police Department in that city. In 1916 he was called
for military service as a conscript and was attached to the
reserve battalion of the Novocherkassky Regiment, Petrograd.
After 6 months service he was sent as a workman to Putilov's
Metal Works in that city, which manufactured arms etc. for
the army. Following the revolution Nevessky returned to Jitomir
in 1918 and in December of the same year was engaged as a
fireman on board the Russian Mercantile Fleet steamer s.s.
"Saratov". In 1920 he arrived in Constantinople with the
remnants of the Russian White Army and refugees and remained
in that port for two years. In 1922 Nevessky was discharged
from his ship and joined the crew of British salvage steamer
"La Luna." In 1923 he resigned and proceeded to France, where
he subsequently worked in an iron factory for a period, after
which he left for Mexico. He was employed in the oil fields
in Tampico until 1924, after which he returned to the U.S.S.R.
where he stayed for two years. He then proceeded to Manchuria
where he was engaged in Vinocuroff's Lumber Co. Harbin. In
1927 he visited Shanghai for a short period and returned again
in November 1929 and stayed here obtaining employment as a
bodyguard to Mr. Yuing Sung-chiang, 338 Burkill Road from
27.1.30 to September 1937 when he was discharged with an
excellent character. While employed as bodyguard, he was granted
6 months leave in January 1935 during which period he visited
Mexico where he took part in wrestling bouts.

伊利亚（埃利亚斯）·弗兰泽维奇·涅韦斯基，俄罗斯人，1895年8月2日出生于南俄日托米尔（Jitomir），系农民之子。他在日托米尔的一所学校就读四年，随后于1912年至1916年间在该市警察局担任职员。1916年，他作为应征入伍者服兵役，被编入彼得格勒新切尔卡斯克团（Novocherkassky Regiment）的后备营。服役6个月后，他被派往该市的普季洛夫金属工厂（Putilov's Metal Works）当工人，该厂为军队制造武器等。革命后，涅韦斯基于1918年返回日托米尔，并于同年12月在俄罗斯商船队“萨拉托夫”号（s.s. "Saratov"）轮船上担任司炉。1920年，他随俄国白军残部和难民抵达君士坦丁堡，并在该港口停留了两年。1922年，涅韦斯基从船上退役，加入了英国打捞蒸汽船“拉卢纳”号（"La Luna."）的船员队伍。1923年他辞职前往法国，随后在一家铁工厂工作了一段时间，之后前往墨西哥。他在坦皮科（Tampico）的油田工作至1924年，之后返回苏联，在那里停留了两年。随后他前往满洲，在哈尔滨的维诺库罗夫木材公司（Vinocuroff's Lumber Co. Harbin）任职。1927年他曾短暂访问上海，又于1929年11月再次返回并在此停留，自1930年1月27日至1937年9月受雇为伯基尔路338号余松江（Yuing Sung-chiang，音译）先生的保镖，离职时品行优良。在担任保镖期间，他于1935年1月获准休假6个月，期间他访问了墨西哥并参加了摔跤比赛。

Subject Mrs. Z.M. Markinin applicant for letter of character.

Made by D.S.I. Irokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S

Inquiries show that Mrs Zina Mikhailovna MARKININ, Russian, was born on June 18, 1890 at Kokchetav, Altai Province, Siberia. She arrived in Shanghai from Russia in 1926 in order to join her husband, an ex-colonel of the Siberian Cossack Troops, who was the Commander of the 2nd Company of the Russian Regiment, S.V.C. from 1927 to the time of his death in July, 1937.

George M. Markinin was born on 17-8-1909 at Djarkent, Semirechensk Province, Siberia. He arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok via Genzan in 1922 together with the Omsk Military Cadet School. In 1924 he left for Serbia with a group of cadets of the said school. Returning to Shanghai in October, 1930 he joined the Russian Regiment with which he is still serving.

Mihail M. Markinin was born on 14-2-1911 at Semipalatinsk, Siberia. He arrived in Shanghai from Russia in 1926 together with his mother. From 1926 to 1930 he attended the Russian Orthodox Confraternity's School, after which he joined a local garage as an apprentice. For the past five or six years he has been employed as a mechanic and driver with Bills Motors, Avenue Foch.

Nothing detrimental is known by this office regarding Mrs Markinin and her sons.

经查，Zina Mikhailovna MARKININ 夫人，俄国人，1890年6月18日出生于西伯利亚阿尔泰省科克切塔夫。她于1926年从俄罗斯抵达上海，与其丈夫团聚。其丈夫系前西伯利亚哥萨克部队上校，1927年至1937年7月去世期间，担任上海万国商团俄国队第二连连长。

George M. Markinin 于1909年8月17日出生于西伯利亚谢米列奇耶省贾尔肯特。他于1922年随鄂木斯克军事士官学校从海参崴经元山抵达上海。1924年，他随该校一批士官生前往塞尔维亚。1930年10月返回上海后，他加入俄国队，至今仍在该队服役。

Mihail M. Markinin 于1911年2月14日出生于西伯利亚塞米巴拉金斯克。他于1926年随母亲从俄罗斯抵达上海。1926年至1930年，他就读于东正教兄弟会学校，之后在当地一家车库当学徒。过去五六年间，他在霞飞路比尔汽车行（Bills Motors）受雇为机械师和司机。

REPORT
Date December 16 1937

Subject V. V. Razsadin, applicant for letter of character.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky    Forwarded by C. Crawford A.S

Vassily Vassilievich Razsadin, Russian, was born on
April 7, 1897, in Samara Province. His father was a
railway employee. Razsadin was educated at Buzuluk
Forestry School and subsequently attended the Normal
School at Melekes, Samara Province. Upon leaving school
in 1915 he was employed as a forester until 1916 when he
was called for military service as a conscript. He saw
active service during the Great War, and from July 1918 to
1922 served in the ranks of Admiral Koltchak's Army in
Siberia. In 1922 he left Vladivostok for Genzan, Korea,
together with the remnants of the White Army. In 1923-
1924 he resided in Harbin, after which he joined the
Russian Detachment of Marshal Chang Chung Chang's Army in
Shantung. Following the disbandment of this army in
1927, Razsadin arrived in Shanghai. Here he was employed
with the Modern Farm Dairy, 8 Tifeng Road, for a short
period, after which he joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.,
leaving the regiment on his own accord in 1930. He was
then employed as bank-escort with Clarke's Inquiry and
Protection Agency, 88 Nanking Road, until February, 1934,
when he was engaged as a body guard by a Chinese named
Sung Kyih Ching, residing at 418 Myburgh Road.
On November 15, 1937 his services were dispensed with
owing to the present situation in Shanghai. He received
a good testimonial from his employer.
At present Razsadin is without a fixed employment.

Vassily Vassilievich Razsadin，俄国人，1897年4月7日出生于萨马拉省。其父为铁路雇员。Razsadin 曾在布祖卢克林业学校受教育，随后就读于萨马拉省梅列克斯师范学校。1915年离校后，他担任护林员直至1916年应征入伍。他在第一次世界大战期间服役，1918年7月至1922年间在西伯利亚科尔恰克海军上将的军队中服役。1922年，他随白军残部从海参崴前往朝鲜元山。1923-1924年他居住在哈尔滨，之后加入山东张宗昌元帅军队的俄国分队。该军队于1927年解散后，Razsadin 抵达上海。在此，他曾在提丰路8号现代农场乳品厂短暂工作，随后加入上海万国商团俄国队，并于1930年自愿离队。此后，他在南京路88号克拉克调查保护社担任银行押运员，直至1934年2月，受雇于一位名叫宋吉清（Sung Kyih Ching，音译）的中国人担任保镖，此人居住于迈尔堡路418号。
1937年11月15日，由于上海目前的局势，他被解雇。他获得了雇主的良好推荐信。
目前 Razsadin 没有固定工作。

Date December 20, 19 37
Subject Wilhelm Rubensohn - applicant for a certificate of good conduct
from the Shanghai Municipal Police.
Made by D.S. Larby Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.

Wilhelm Rubensohn, German Jew, was born in Leipzig,
Germany, on January 14, 1906 and is the holder of a German
passport No. 103/37 issued in Shanghai on April 22, 1937.
On the completion of his general education, Rubensohn
became apprenticed to a firm of fur merchants operating in
Leipzig and in 1925 obtained a position in the Hamburg office
of C. Holstein & Company, fur merchants. Subsequently,
in January 1926, Rubensohn was transferred to the Kobe office
of the aforementioned firm in which he continued to serve
until April 15, 1927 when he resigned as a result of the
decision of the company to recall him to Germany.
After resigning, Rubensohn then proceeded to Tientsin
and in May, 1927, was engaged by Carlowitz & Company in
the capacity of a furs and hides expert. In May, 1932, as
a result of a retrenchment scheme put into operation by the
company, Rubensohn resigned his position and returned to
Germany where he remained until September, 1932 when he
left Germany and returned to China, arriving in Shanghai
during October of the same year.
After his arrival in Shanghai, Rubensohn endeavoured
to operate his own import and export business but owing
to lack of capital he met with little success. Consequently,
in March, 1933, he wound up his business and joined the
radio sales staff of Siemens China Company by which concern
he has since been continuously employed to the present
time.
In view of the present conditions in Shanghai and
the poor prospects of advancement in his present occupation,
Rubensohn has decided to emigrate to Australia where

威廉·鲁本索恩，德籍犹太人，1906年1月14日出生于德国莱比锡，持有1937年4月22日在上海签发的德国护照，号码为103/37。
在完成普通教育后，鲁本索恩在莱比锡一家皮草商行当学徒，并于1925年在皮草商C. Holstein & Company的汉堡办事处获得职位。随后，1926年1月，鲁本索恩被调往上述公司的神户办事处，他一直在此任职，直到1927年4月15日，因公司决定将其召回德国而辞职。
辞职后，鲁本索恩前往天津，并于1927年5月受雇于礼和洋行（Carlowitz & Company），担任皮草与皮革专家。1932年5月，由于公司实施裁员计划，鲁本索恩辞去职务返回德国，他在德国停留至1932年9月，随后离开德国回到中国，于同年10月抵达上海。
抵达上海后，鲁本索恩试图经营自己的进出口业务，但因缺乏资金，收效甚微。因此，1933年3月，他结束了业务，加入西门子中国公司（Siemens China Company）的无线电销售部门，并一直受雇于该公司至今。
鉴于上海目前的局势以及其当前职业晋升前景不佳，鲁本索恩已决定移民澳大利亚，在那里

Eugene Spiridonovich BLENSKY, Russian, was born on
September 21,1909 at Vissenskaya Station, Ussoury Railway, Mari-
time Province, Russia. According to his own statement, he re-
sided together with his parents in various places of the Chinese
Eastern Railway Zone from 1910 and in 1932 graduated from the
Harbin Polytechnic Institute.
He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in September,1932
and from March,1934 has been employed with Anderson,Meyer & Co.,
21/43 Yuen Ming Yuen Road ( Structural Department ).
It appears that on account of the present uncertain
political and economic situation in Shanghai he intends to mig-
rate to Iran and that he has been corresponding for some time
with a certain A.J. Treskinsky,Russian engineer residing at
25 Khiaban Diba, Teheran,with the assistance of whom he hopes
to obtain a visa for Iran and subsequently an employment in that
country.
Blensky is a member of the Russian Technical Society
in Shanghai. For about four years he has been residing at 730
Avenue Foch,House 93 together with his parents,Mr.& Mrs S.A.
Blensky aged 55 and 51 years,respectively.Mr. S.A. Blensky,for-
merly a school teacher in Harbin, is at present unemployed. Mr.
and Mrs Blensky intend to accompany their son to Iran.
The Blensky family are registered with the Russian Emi-
grants' Committee,113/1 Noulmeir Road.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office regarding
them.
G. Prokopiev
D. S. I.
D. C. ( Special Branch).

叶夫根尼·斯皮里多诺维奇·布连斯基（Eugene Spiridonovich BLENSKY），俄罗斯人，1909年9月21日出生于俄罗斯滨海省乌苏里铁路维森斯卡亚站（Vissenskaya Station）。据其自述，他从1910年起与父母一起居住在中东铁路区的各个地方，并于1932年毕业于哈尔滨工业大学。
他于1932年9月从哈尔滨抵达上海，并从1934年3月起受雇于安美洋行（Anderson, Meyer & Co.），地址为圆明园路21/43号（结构部）。
看来，由于上海目前政治和经济局势的不确定性，他打算移民伊朗，并且一段时间以来一直与居住在德黑兰迪巴街25号（Khiaban Diba）的俄罗斯工程师A.J. Treskinsky通信，希望在他的帮助下获得伊朗签证，随后在该国就业。
布连斯基是上海俄罗斯技术学会的成员。大约四年来，他一直与父母S.A.布连斯基夫妇（年龄分别为55岁和51岁）居住在霞飞路730号93室。S.A.布连斯基先生曾是哈尔滨的一名学校教师，目前失业。布连斯基夫妇打算陪同他们的儿子前往伊朗。
布连斯基一家已在诺尔梅尔路113/1号的俄罗斯难民委员会登记。
本处未掌握关于他们的任何不利记录。
G. Prokopiev
D. S. I.
D. C. (特别处)。

With regard to the attached communication dated
November 24, 1937 from Dr. Frederick REISS, asking for a
certificate of conduct in duplicate affecting his stay in
Shanghai, I have to report that in the October, 1929 issue
of 'True Detective Mysteries' (pages 45-52) an article
entitled "D.O.P. - Scourge of the Underworld" appeared, in
which a letter from Dr. Reiss addressed to Messrs. W.H.R. &
Co., Budapest, introducing one "...... r. J.S. Dolan, who
is interested in my mind, in the products of your factory...
...." is reproduced. James Stephen DOLAN, American, is
a convicted criminal, having been fined 5,000 marks or 500
days' imprisonment in Hamburg in June 1928 for smuggling
large quantities of heroin. At the time of his arrest
the above mentioned letter was found in Dolan's possession,
but a thorough investigation failed to prove that Reiss was
actively connected in any way with the smuggling activities
of Dolan.

A copy of this article was forwarded to the Municipal
Police on October 19, 1929 with a covering letter which was
signed by the following Shanghai doctors:-
A. von Fiorini, T. Toll,
. Piza, F. Bxtolar,
A. Renner, A. Baflaender,
M. Morec, A. Tuzlag.

Investigations conducted in October 1929 showed that
although Reiss had written the letter of introduction at
Dolan's request, it had been done as a friendly gesture, as
Dolan, in 1929, had proposed him for membership in a
Masonic Lodge in Shanghai. From that time Reiss saw little

J.S. Dolan，他对贵厂的产品很感兴趣____”。詹姆斯·斯蒂芬·多兰（James Stephen DOLAN），美国人，是一名有定罪记录的罪犯，曾于1928年6月在汉堡因走私大量海洛因而被处以5,000马克罚款或500天监禁。在他被捕时，上述信件在多兰身上被发现，但经过彻底调查，未能证明赖斯以任何方式积极参与了多兰的走私活动。

until 1928 when Dolan approached him, intimated that he was
shortly proceeding to Budapest on business and since Dr.
Reiss was a Hungarian, requested certain letters of introduction
to business organisations there. Messrs. Byer & Co., the
concern to which the letter found on Dolan was addressed,
dealt in chemical products and it was naturally suspected
by the Military Police that Reiss had written the communication
with a motive that was not one of introducing Dolan from a
viewpoint of friendship.
The motive of the above party of doctors in despatching
the copy of the article was not so much in the interests of
justice as it was from professional jealousy, for Reiss, at
the time the letter was sent to the Police, was rather proud
of the fact that he was a member of the Shanghai Medical
Association and refused to have anything to do with the
signatories, and on his own admission was responsible for
preventing any of them attempting to join the Association
through fear of being blackballed by the influence which Dr.
Reiss wielded among members of the local British medical
fraternity.
Dr. Reiss, M.D. (Budapest, 1914), arrived in Shanghai
in January 1922 from Budapest and for many years has had
consulting rooms at 142 Museum Road. For several years he
was the official physician to the Italian Consulate-General
here, to the Italian Navy, and among his many clients are
numerous employees of the Municipal Council. A specialist
in skin diseases, Dr. Reiss is Assistant Professor of
Dermatology of the National Medical College and since 1930

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Crawford. L. S.

G. A. Schavinsky, applicant for a certificate of character,
applied for a certificate on December 21, 1937, which was
issued on 27.12.37, but now states that he requires another
one as the previous one was either lost or mislaid when
transferred by post to Australia ( see letter attached). Since
he was issued with this certificate he has not come to the
notice of the Municipal Police except for the fact that when
leaving his former residence at 591/178 Bubbling Well Road
in January 1938 he left an unpaid account of $33.00 which
still remains unsettled.

Fanny Yakovlevna SCHAVINSKY, nee Polk, Latvian by birth,
was born in Valk, Latvia, on November 29, 1901.

She is reported to have left Russia in 1919 and subsequently
resided in Harbin, Peking and Tientsin. She arrived in
Shanghai from Tientsin in 1925. Here she met and later
cohabited with her present husband G. A. Schavinsky to whom in
1931 she was legally married.

The applicant is a professional dancer and singer and has
been appearing in that capacity in various theatres in Shanghai.
She is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1
Moulmein Road, on the strength of passport No. 308, issued by
the Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government on July 2,
1937.

While in Shanghai the applicant did not come to the notice
of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of
an undesirable nature.

G. A. Schavinsky，品行证明书申请人，曾于1937年12月21日申请证明书，该证明书于1937年12月27日签发，但他现在表示需要另一份，因为前一份在邮寄至澳大利亚时丢失或放错地方（见附件信函）。自从获得该证明书以来，除了一件事外，他未引起工部局警务处的注意，即他在1938年1月离开原住所静安寺路591/178号时，留下了一笔33.00美元的未付账目，至今仍未结清。

范妮·雅科夫列夫娜·沙文斯基（Fanny Yakovlevna SCHAVINSKY），娘家姓波尔克（Polk），拉脱维亚人，1901年11月29日出生于拉脱维亚瓦尔卡（Valk）。

据报道，她于1919年离开俄罗斯，随后居住在哈尔滨、北京和天津。她于1925年从天津抵达上海。在这里，她结识了现在的丈夫 G. A. Schavinsky 并与之同居，两人于1931年正式结婚。

申请人是一名职业舞蹈家和歌手，曾以上述身份在上海各大剧院演出。她凭上海市政府警察局于1937年7月2日签发的第308号护照，在莫尔尼姆路118/1号俄罗斯侨民委员会登记注册。

在上海期间，申请人未因任何不良性质的活动引起工部局警务处的注意。

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by C. Crawford, A.J.

Georgy Alexandrovich Schavinsky, Russian, was
born on April 23, 1894, at Sebastopol, Crimea. Son of
a structural engineer, he was educated at the Sebastopol
Normal School, graduating in 1912. In 1914 he entered
the Odessa Military Officers School and subsequently
took part in the Great War until 1918. Following the
demobilization of the Russian Army he returned to
Sebastopol. According to his own statement, he later
joined the "White Army" in South Russia, was shell
shocked and invalided, after which he resided in various
towns in Russia until 1924 when he left for Manchuria.
For about one year he worked at the Lumber Concession
at Shatouedzi, Chinese Eastern Railway, after which he
proceeded to Shanghai arriving here in June, 1925. Here
he worked for 8 months as a sailor on board one of the
Asiatic Petroleum Company steamers during the strike.
From February, 1927 to July 1927, he served in the Russian
Detachment, S.V.C. He resigned on his own accord and
from 1927 to 1931 was employed as a Police watchman with
Fook Yuen Bank, 64 Ningpo Road. Later he worked as a
dental technician with Mrs. T.D. Belitsky, local dental
surgeon.

In 1933 he went for Harbin where he studied in the
2nd Harbin Dentistry School graduating in November, 1934. He
then returned to Shanghai and has since been working as
a dental surgeon with an office at 51 Chusan Road.
Following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities
in Shanghai he removed his office to Lane 591, Bubbling
Well Road, House 178, Room 263.

Georgy Alexandrovich Schavinsky，俄罗斯人，1894年4月23日出生于克里米亚塞瓦斯托波尔。他是结构工程师之子，就读于塞瓦斯托波尔师范学校，1912年毕业。1914年进入敖德萨军官学校，随后参加第一次世界大战直至1918年。俄罗斯军队复员后，他返回塞瓦斯托波尔。据其自述，后来他加入了南俄的“白军”，因炮击休克而退役，此后居住在俄罗斯各个城镇，直到1924年前往满洲。他在中东铁路沙陀子木材特许区工作了约一年，之后前往上海，于1925年6月抵达此地。罢工期间，他在亚细亚火油公司的一艘轮船上做了8个月的水手。从1927年2月到1927年7月，他在上海万国商团俄罗斯分队服役。他自愿辞职，1927年至1931年间受雇于宁波路64号福源银行担任警卫视卫。后来他在本地牙科医生 T.D. Belitsky 夫人处担任牙科技师。

1933年他前往哈尔滨，在哈尔滨第二牙科学校学习，于1934年11月毕业。随后他返回上海，此后一直在中山路51号开设诊所从事牙科手术工作。
随着上海中日敌对行动的爆发，他将诊所迁至静安寺路591弄178号263室。

Subject. M.K. Karpoff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Garsia

Maxim Karpovich KARPOFF, Russian, born on January 14,
1899 in Perm Province, Russia. Former soldier of Admiral Kol-
chak's army in Siberia he is reported to have left Vladivostok
for China in 1922 together with the remnants of the "White" ar-
my. From 1922 to 1925 he was employed at Kovalsky's timber con-
cession, Mianpo Station, Chinese Eastern Railway after which he
proceeded to Shanghai arriving here in October, 1925.

In Shanghai he was without a fixed employment until
8-2-27 when he joined the Russian Detachment, S.V.C. Leaving the
service on his own wish on 31-3-33. he worked as a chauffeur for
Bloch Manufacturing & Lumber Co from May to October, 1933 and
for the Frenchine Trading Co, 19 Rue Stanislas Chevalier, from
11-10-33 to January, 1934 and from February, 1934 has been employ-
ed as a bodyguard to Ye Cho Sung, Chinese Manager of the Engineer-
ing Department, Arnhold & Co., residing at 454 Burkill Road.

It appears that he intends to migrate to Australia and
that in this matter he relies upon the assistance of a local Bri-
tish resident.

Karpoff is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Com-
mittee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, He has good testimonials from his
previous employers.

Nothing detrimental is known by this office regarding
him.

D. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

D. C. (Special Branch)

马克西姆·卡尔波维奇·卡尔波夫（Maxim Karpovich KARPOFF），俄罗斯人，1899年1月14日出生于俄罗斯彼尔姆省。据报他曾是西伯利亚高尔察克海军上将军队的士兵，于1922年随“白”军残部离开符拉迪沃斯托克前往中国。1922年至1925年间，他在中东铁路面坡站（Mianpo Station）的科瓦尔斯基（Kovalsky）木材特许专营区受雇，随后前往上海，于1925年10月抵达此地。

在上海，他一直无固定职业，直到1927年2月8日加入上海万国商团俄籍分队。1933年3月31日，他自愿离职。1933年5月至10月，他在布洛克制造与木材公司（Bloch Manufacturing & Lumber Co）担任司机；1933年10月11日至1934年1月，他在斯坦尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路19号（19 Rue Stanislas Chevalier）的法兰信贸易公司（Frenchine Trading Co）任职；自1934年2月起，他受雇担任安诺德洋行（Arnhold & Co.）工程部华籍经理叶卓成（Ye Cho Sung，音译）的保镖，叶氏居住于伯基尔路454号。

看来他打算移居澳大利亚，在此事上他依赖一位当地英国居民的协助。

卡尔波夫已在莫尔美因路118/1号的俄罗斯侨民委员会登记。他拥有前雇主提供的良好推荐信。

本局未掌握任何对他不利的记录。

D. Prokofiev
副督察

副 commissioner （特别支部）

Mihail Vassilievich Ossipoff, Russian, was born on
8.10.1889 at Irkutsk, Siberia. Formerly an employee of the
Russo-Asiatic Bank at Irkutsk he served in the ranks of the
Russian Army from 1916 to 1918. In 1920 he left Russia for
China and arrived in Shanghai via Mongolia and Tientsin.
In May 1922 he joined the Shanghai branch of the Russo-Asiatic
Bank and in September of the same year was transferred to
the Harbin branch of this bank. Following the liquidation
of the bank in question in 1925, Ossipoff in partnership with
S.M. Krieger, A.A. Petroff, Gubonin and Makaroff, ex-employees
of the Russo-Asiatic Bank, and one E.S. Kaufman established
the Thriftcor Bank in Harbin. Ossipoff was appointed one
of the directors. This bank held a charter issued by the
State of Nevada, U.S.A., but was not an American bank and
was not incorporated under U.S. Banking Law. In 1935 in
connection with the liquidation of the bank, Ossipoff and
another director of the bank, named A.A. Petroff, were
arrested by the Japanese authorities in Harbin. They were
released in March 1935, after over one month detention, having
explained to the satisfaction of the authorities the reasons
why the bank went into voluntary liquidation.

In August 1936, Ossipoff arrived to Shanghai from
Harbin together with his family. From February 1937, he has
been employed with the Discount Saving Bank (S.I.Djamgarian
& T.A. Bahmani), 465/467 Avenue Joffre. It was rumoured that
this bank has business connections with local Soviet commercial
institutions.

Ossipoff is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee. When in Harbin he was a member of the Rotary

米哈伊尔·瓦西里耶维奇·奥西波夫（Mihail Vassilievich Ossipoff），俄罗斯人，1889年10月8日出生于西伯利亚伊尔库茨克。他曾是伊尔库茨克俄亚银行（Russo-Asiatic Bank）的职员，1916年至1918年在俄国军队中服役。1920年，他离开俄罗斯前往中国，经蒙古和天津抵达上海。1922年5月，他加入俄亚银行上海分行，同年9月调任该银行哈尔滨分行。在该银行于1925年清算后，奥西波夫与俄亚银行前雇员 S.M. Krieger、A.A. Petroff、Gubonin 和 Makaroff，以及一位 E.S. Kaufman 合伙在哈尔滨成立了节俭银行（Thriftcor Bank）。奥西波夫被任命为董事之一。该银行持有美国内华达州颁发的执照，但并非美国银行，也未根据美国银行法注册。1935年，随着该银行的清算，奥西波夫和另一位名为 A.A. Petroff 的银行董事被日本当局在哈尔滨逮捕。他们在拘留一个多月后，于1935年3月获释，因为他们向当局满意地解释了银行自愿清算的原因。

1936年8月，奥西波夫携家人从哈尔滨抵达上海。自1937年2月起，他受雇于折扣储蓄银行（Discount Saving Bank，S.I. Djamgarian & T.A. Bahmani），地址为霞飞路465/467号。有传言称该银行与当地苏联商业机构有业务往来。

奥西波夫已在俄罗斯侨民委员会登记。在哈尔滨期间，他是扶轮社成员

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............

REPORT    Special Branch Station,
Date August 20, 1938.

Subject C.P. OSSORGIN - applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S. Pitts.    Forwarded by [Signature]

The Australian Trade Commissioner was interviewed during
the morning of August 20, 1938 in regard to OSSORGIN'S
application for a certificate of character, which is required
before he can enter Australia.

The Commissioner stated that he had already been approached
by Ossorgin and in view of the fact that he had been favourably
impressed by his demeanour, he had reviewed the details
relating to the application and had come to the following
conclusions:

1) It would be in order for the Police to issue Ossorgin
a certificate on which, however, particulars should be
recorded as to his past offences. Failure to comply
might create a dangerous precedent which could result
in unwittingly involving several persons in considerable
trouble.

2) He would be obliged if a copy of the police report dated
January 10, 1938 giving information relating to Ossorgin's
antecedents be forwarded to him.

3) Ossorgin is to be requested to call on the Trade Commissioner
in due course with his certificate, when the Commissioner
will make arrangements to supply him with a letter to the
Secretary of the Interior of the Australian Government,
explaining that the offences he committed in Shanghai
were such not to brand him as a hardened character.

D.S. Pitts
D. S.

1938年8月20日上午，就 OSSORGIN 申请品行证明书一事采访了澳大利亚贸易专员，该证明书是他进入澳大利亚之前所必需的。

专员表示，Ossorgin 此前已与他接触过，鉴于他对 Ossorgin 的举止印象良好，他审查了与该申请有关的细节，并得出以下结论：

1) 警方可以向 Ossorgin 颁发证明书，但在证明书上应记录其过去的罪行。如果不这样做，可能会开创一个危险的先例，导致在不知情的情况下使数人陷入相当大的麻烦。

2) 如果将1938年1月10日提供的关于 Ossorgin 背景的警方报告副本转发给他，他将不胜感激。

3) 将要求 Ossorgin 在适当时候持证明书拜访贸易专员，届时专员将安排向他提供一封致澳大利亚政府内政部长的信，解释他在上海所犯的罪行并不足以将他标记为顽固不化的罪犯。

On January 19, 1938 Mr. C.P. Ossorgin called at this
office. He stated that in connection with his application for
a visa to enter Australia a certificate was necessary from the
local Police to the effect that he has no criminal record.
Although he was convicted of two offences (1/ Drunk and dis-
orderly and 2/ Assault on Police) on 27.2.34, he hopes that
it is perfectly clear from the circumstances of the case that
he got into a trouble while being under the influence of
alcohol and that he cannot be regarded as a criminal.

Branch) on the attached report dated January 10, 1938 Mr.
Ossorgin was advised to put his case before the Australian
Trade Commissioner. He said that he would postpone this matter
until Mr. Bowden's return to Shanghai from Australia.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford. I. S.

Constantin Pavlovich OSSORGIN, Russian, was born on
July 29, 1896 at Mentone, France. He claims to have been graduated
from a Military Cadets Corps in Russia in 1915 and to have at-
tended the Vladivostok Polytechnic Institute in 1920-1922.
Immediately prior to the occupation of Vladivostok
by the "reds" in November, 1922 he left that city for Genzan,
Korea, and later proceeded to Shanghai arriving here in Septem-
ber, 1923 in the s.s. "Eldorado".
In Shanghai he was employed with the Shanghai Tele-
phone Company for several years, being discharged in 1931 owing
to a reduction in staff; he was employed as a residence manager,
Hamilton House, from 1932 to February, 1934. For the following
two years he was connected with Haskins & Sells, Certified Public
Accountants, 320 Szechuen Road, and with Allman, Davies & Tops,
local lawyers, 206 Hamilton House. During the summer seasons
in 1936 and 1937 he was employed as manager of the Edgewater
Mansions, Tsingtao. At present he is reported to be connected
with the China Motors, 702 Bubbling Well Road, as a salesman on
a commission basis.
He was a member of the S.M.Police ( Specials ) from
1930 to February, 1934.
Ossorgin forms the subject of criminal record F.1947,
the particulars of which are as follows:-
I/ In October, 1931 a charge of Misappropriation was
brought against him at the 1-st S.S.D.Court. He was acquitted of
this charge on 30-1-32.
II/ On 22-1-34 he was arrested and charged at the same
court with, 1) Assault on Police and, 2) Drunk and disorderly.
He was sentenced to 30 days' detention on the first and was

January 10, 1938.

C.P. Ossorgin, applicant for a certificate of character

Constantin Pavlovich OSSORGIN, Russian, was
born on July 29, 1896 at Mentone, France. He claims
to have graduated from a Military Cadet Corps in
Russia in 1915 and to have attended the Vladivostok
Polytechnic Institute in 1920-1922.

Immediately prior to the occupation of
Vladivostok by the "reds" in November, 1922 he left
that city for Genzan, Korea, and later proceeded to
Shanghai arriving here in September, 1923 in the
s.s. "Eldorado."

In Shanghai he was employed with the Shanghai
Telephone Company for several years, being discharged
in 1931 owing to a reduction in staff; he was employed
as a residence manager at Hamilton House from 1932 to
February 1934. For the following two years he was
connected with Haskins & Sells, Certified Public
Accountants, 320 Szechuen Road, and with Allman,
Davies & Kops, local lawyers, 208 Hamilton House.
During the summer seasons in 1936 and 1937 he was
employed as manager of the Edgewater Mansions, Tsingtao.
At present he is reported to be connected with the China
Motors, 702 Bubbling Well Road, as a salesman on a
commission basis.

He was a member of the Shanghai Municipal Police
(Specials) from 1930 to February 1934.

Ossorgin forms the subject of criminal record
F.1947, particulars of which are as follows :-

Date February 23, 1938

Subject M.K. Epport, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by C Crawford. A.J.

Michail Michailovich Epport, Russian of Jewish
origin, born on May 4, 1896 at Ivanovka, Ekaterinoslav
Province, South Russia. According to his own statement,
he graduated from a middle school in Harkov in 1919, after
which he studied in the local Polytechnic Institute
(Industrial-Economical Faculty) for two years. From 1924
to 1927 he was employed for various periods with the Soviet
lumber export concern "Exportles" in Harkov, Moscow and
Habarovsk, after which he was sent to Harbin as the "Exportles"
representative for China. Until 1930 he resided in Tientsin
and during that period frequently made business trips to
Harbin and Shanghai.

In December 1930, following his refusal to comply
with an order to return to the U.S.S.R., he severed his
connections with the "Exportles" and took out an emigrant's
passport in Tientsin. In March 1931 he arrived in Shanghai
and for the following three years was engaged here in co-
mercial activities, having established his own firm under
the style of the "Shanghai Equitable Trading Corporation
with an office at 24 The Bund. At the same time he was
connected with Ling Kee Timber Co., 44 Canton Road. On
12.12.33 he left for Europe in the s.s. "Conte Rosso" on
a business trip with a view to the establishing connections
with various woolen piece goods firms. Having visited Italy,
Austria, Czechoslovakia and Germany he returned to Shanghai
about June 1934 and, in partnership with one I.M.Baumzweiger,
Russian Jew, opened the piece goods department of his firm.
In summer 1934 he made an application for a visa to Samarinda

米哈伊尔·米哈伊洛维奇·埃波特 (Michail Michailovich Epport)，俄籍犹太人，1896年5月4日出生于南俄罗斯叶卡捷琳诺斯拉夫省 (Ekaterinoslav Province) 的伊万诺夫卡 (Ivanovka)。据其自述，他于1919年毕业于哈尔科夫 (Harkov) 的一所中学，随后在当地理工学院（工业经济系）学习了两年。1924年至1927年间，他在哈尔科夫、莫斯科和哈巴罗夫斯克 (Habarovsk) 的苏联木材出口企业“Exportles”断续受雇，之后被派往哈尔滨担任“Exportles”驻华代表。直至1930年，他居住在天津，期间频繁前往哈尔滨和上海出差。

1930年12月，因拒绝服从返回苏联的命令，他切断了与“Exportles”的联系，并在天津申领了移民护照。1931年3月他抵达上海，随后的三年里在此从事商业活动，以“上海公平贸易公司” (Shanghai Equitable Trading Corporation) 的名义成立了自己的公司，办事处设在外滩24号。同时，他与广东路44号的 Ling Kee Timber Co. 有业务联系。1933年12月12日，他乘坐“Conte Rosso”号轮船前往欧洲进行商务旅行，旨在与多家毛呢匹头商行建立联系。在访问了意大利、奥地利、捷克斯洛伐克和德国后，他于1934年6月左右返回上海，并与俄籍犹太人 I.M. Baumzweiger 合伙，开设了他公司的匹头部。1934年夏，他申请前往三马林达 (Samarinda) 的签证

（左侧手写批注：Put up used Certificate f cf. sig.）

REPORT
Date February 25 1938
Subject M. Lewenszpil, applicant for a certificate of character.
Made by D.S. Tcheremshanaky Forwarded by [Signature] DS/

Mojzes (Moses) LEWENSZPIL alias LEVENSPIEL, alias
LEVENSPHIEL, Polish citizen, was born on September 14,
1892 at Warsaw, Poland, and is the son of a merchant.
He received his education in a commercial school in Warsaw.
Later he was employed as a piece goods salesman in that
city. In 1914 he went to London, where he remained
until 1918 working as a salesman. In 1919 he arrived
in Shanghai from England via Archangel and Siberia. Here
he was employed in the piece goods department of Weeks
& Company, Nanking Road, from 1919 to 1929. From
1930 to 1936 he was employed as a salesman and mechanic
with the Auto Palace and Overland Motors, 694 Bubbling
Well Road. From September, 1936 to September, 1937 he
worked in the same capacity with Bills Motors, Avenue
Foch. He left this firm owing to a cut of staff resulting
from business depression and was given a good testimonial.
For the last few months he has been employed with Renault
Motors, 627 Avenue Foch.
Lewenszpil resides at 1205 Bubbling Well Road with
his wife, Mrs. Clara Lewenszpil. He is registered with
the local Polish Consulate-General. His father, two
brothers and three sisters are residing at Paris.
His cousin, one A. Levenspiel, residing at 320
Kiangse Road, a merchant by profession, is known as a person
of a doubtful reputation with strong socialist tendencies
and is in sympathy with the bolshevic regime. Like the
applicant he resided in London prior to 1918.
There is nothing in Municipal Police records against
M. Lewenszpil.
D.C. (Special Br.)
[Signature]
D. S.

Mojzes (Moses) LEWENSZPIL，别名 LEVENSPIEL，别名 LEVENSPHIEL，波兰公民，1892年9月14日出生于波兰华沙，系商人之子。他在华沙的一所商业学校接受教育。后来在该市担任匹头销售员。1914年他前往伦敦，直到1918年一直在那里担任销售员。1919年，他经阿尔汉格尔斯克 (Archangel) 和西伯利亚从英国抵达上海。1919年至1929年间，他在南京路的 Weeks & Company 匹头部工作。1930年至1936年，他在静安寺路69号的 Auto Palace 和 Overland Motors 担任销售员和机械师。1936年9月至1937年9月，他在霞飞路 (Avenue Foch) 的 Bills Motors 担任相同职务。由于商业萧条导致裁员，他离开了该公司，并获得了良好的推荐信。最近几个月，他在霞飞路627号的雷诺汽车公司 (Renault Motors) 工作。
Lewenszpil 与妻子 Clara Lewenszpil 夫人居住在静安寺路1205号。他已在当地波兰总领事馆登记。他的父亲、两个兄弟和三个姐妹居住在巴黎。
他的表亲 A. Levenspiel，居住在江西路320号，职业为商人，被认为声誉可疑，有强烈的社会主义倾向，并同情布尔什维克政权。与申请人一样，他在1918年之前也居住在伦敦。
工部局警务处档案中无任何针对 M. Lewenszpil 的不利记录。

Subject V.V. Ankudinoff - applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by J.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford A.J.

Vasiley Vasilievitch Ankudinoff, Russian, born on
December 24, 1903 at Imianpo Station, Chinese Eastern Railway.
Former student of the Habarovsk Military Cadets School he arrived
in Shanghai from Vladivostok in November, 1922 together with the
school. After graduating in 1923 he was without a fixed employ-
ment and resided with his late uncle until 1928, when he was en-
gaged as a body-guard by a Chinese. After 2½ years work in this
capacity he joined the firm Palmer & Turner as an assistant clerk
of works. On 31-5-35 he was discharged owing to a reduction in
staff. From October, 1936 to July, 1937 he was employed as a build-
ing supervisor with A. Corrit, 27c Kiangsi Road. Leaving this posi-
tion on his own wish he worked in a similar capacity with E.D.

Made by D.S. Tcheremahansky Forwarded by C. Caserta 2.3.

Valery Alexandrovich Shostakovich, Russian, was born
on February 21, 1902 at Irkutsk, Siberia. His father was
formerly an employee of the Russo-Asiatic Bank in Russia
and at present resides at Harbin. Applicant was educated
at the commercial school in Chita, graduating in 1918.
From 1918 to 1922 he served in the "White" Russian Army
in Siberia, after which he left Russia for China with the
remnants of the army. After several months stay in a con-
centration camp at Kirin, he proceeded to Harbin where he
was employed with the Chinese Eastern Railway until 1929
as a boy-scout instructor and at the same time was for
various periods employed with different printing offices.
In 1929, during the Sino-Soviet conflict in Manchuria, he
was in charge of Railway Guards attached to the Chinese
Eastern Railway Workshops in Harbin. On 2.2.30 he arrived
in Shanghai from Harbin and from July 1930 to August 1936
was employed with the Acme Foundry Ltd., 120 Robison Road.
Later he worked in the printing office of the Russian news-
paper "Novy Put" for about 6 months and subsequently with
the "Novosti Dnia" for two months. In summer 1937 Shostakovich
left for Tsingtao where he was employed as a tutor at a
Russian Children's Camp.

Shostakovich was a member of the 3rd Russian Volunteer
Company, S.V.C. from 23.1.34 to December 1937. From November
26 to January 2, 1938 he served in the Russian Detachment,
S.V.C., attached to the French Police. He was discharged
following his arrest on 2.1.38 for "Gambling" of which charge
he was subsequently acquitted by the 1st Shanghai Special

REPORT
Date March 2, 19 38.

Subject D.P. Shmygin, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by C Crawford Z. S.

Dmitry Petrovich Shmygin, Russian, was born on
October 26, 1893 at Tomsk, Siberia and is the son of a
farmer who at present resides in the U.S.S.R. He received
his education in a primary school. He saw active service
during the Great War and subsequently served in the White
Army in Siberia in Ataman Annenkoff's detachment. Follow-
ing the defeat of the "Whites" in 1919 he made his way to
Urumchi, Chinese Turkestan and in 1920 proceeded to Tientsin
via Peking. In Tientsin he was employed for over three
years with the mechanical workshops of Messrs Nevsky and
Kremarevsky. On January 25, 1925 he arrived in Shanghai
from Tientsin and for about three months was employed on a
steamer of China Navigation Co., plying between Shanghai and
Hankow. Later he was employed for a short period at the
restaurant "Russky Ugolok," North Szechuen Road, and sub-
sequently with a British missioner Mr. Wilson as a house-
keeper. In 1936 Shmygin left for Kuling where he was employed
at a Mission Hospital etc. until October 1936 when he returned
to Shanghai. Since April 1937 he has been employed with
Henningsen Produce Co. Fed. Inc. U.S.A., 250 West Saking
Road.

Shmygin is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee. He resides at House 6, Lane 135 Avenue Haig
with his wife Mrs. Z.P. Shmygin and two children 11 and 8
years respectively.

Nothing detrimental is known by this office against
the applicant.

D.C. (Special Branch).

g Tcheremshansky.
D.S.

2/3.

Dmitry Petrovich Shmygin，俄国人，1893年
10月26日出生于西伯利亚托木斯克，是一位农民的儿子，
其父现居苏联。他受过小学教育。他在第一次世界
大战期间服过现役，随后在西伯利亚白军的 Ataman Annenkoff
分队服役。1919年“白军”战败后，他前往中国新疆
乌鲁木齐，并于1920年经北京前往天津。在天津，他在
Nevsky 和 Kremarevsky 先生的机械车间受雇三年多。
1925年1月25日，他从天津抵达上海，并在往返于上海和
汉口之间的中国轮船公司（China Navigation Co.）的一艘轮船上
工作了约三个月。后来他在北四川路的“Russky Ugolok”
餐厅短暂工作，随后在英国传教士 Wilson 先生处担任管家。
1936年，Shmygin 前往牯岭（Kuling），在那里的一家教会医院
等地工作，直到1936年10月返回上海。自1937年4月以来，
他一直受雇于美国 Henningsen Produce Co. Fed. Inc.，地址为
西萨金路250号。

Shmygin 已在俄国侨民委员会注册。他与妻子
Z.P. Shmygin 夫人及两个分别为11岁和8岁的孩子
居住在海格路135弄6号。

本局未发现对申请人不利的记录。

REPORT
Date March 16, 1938

Subject Mrs. I.I. Leiboshetz - applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by J.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

Mrs Ida Efraimovna LEIBOSHETZ, Russian of Jewish
extraction, born on September 7, 1897 at Odessa, South Russia.
In 1923 she graduated from the Medical Faculty of the Universi-
ty of Prague and soon afterwards left for Palestine where she re-
mained for about one year, after which she proceeded to Shanghai
arriving in this city in 1926. Here she established herself as
a medical practitioner. She is registered with the Public Health
Department, S.M.C., and at present has her office at 770 Bubbling
Well Road, Flat 35.

According to her own statement, she was married to
a certain Mr. I.H. Ignatoff, Bulgarian subject, and was divorced
in December, 1935 at the 1-st S.S.J. Court.

She was registered with the S.C.G. Police Bureau as
a Russian emigrant until 1932 when she obtained a "certificate of
nationality" from the Lithuanian Consul at Harbin. In 1936, fol-
lowing an investigation carried out in the Far East by a repre-
sentative of the Lithuanian Government, the majority of "certi-
ficates of nationality" issued by the Harbin consul were cancel-
led. Mrs Leiboshetz then re-registered with the S.C.G. Police
Bureau as a Russian emigrant through the medium of the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118 Boulmein Road.

Nothing detrimental is known by this office regard-
ing this person.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

DBR
3
D. C. ( Special Branch ).

由 J.S.I. Prokofiev 撰写。由 C. Crawford 转呈。副督察。

Ida Efraimovna LEIBOSHETZ 夫人，俄籍犹太人，1897年9月7日出生于南俄罗斯敖德萨。
1923年，她毕业于布拉格大学医学院，随后不久前往巴勒斯坦，在那里停留了约一年，之后前往上海，于1926年抵达本市。在此，她成为一名执业医生。她在工部局公共卫生处注册，目前诊所位于静安寺路770号35室。

据其自述，她曾嫁给一位名为 I.H. Ignatoff 的先生（保加利亚籍），并于1935年12月在第一特区地方法院离婚。

她在上海公共租界警务处登记为俄国难民，直至1932年从哈尔滨立陶宛领事馆获得“国籍证明书”。1936年，经立陶宛政府代表在远东进行调查后，哈尔滨领事签发的多数“国籍证明书”被注销。随后，Leiboshetz 夫人通过莫尔尼路118号俄国难民委员会，再次在上海公共租界警务处登记为俄国难民。

本局未发现有关此人的不利记录。

A. Prokofiev

Subject Mr. and Mrs. A.P. Berlinsky, applicants for certificate of good
character.

Made by D.P.S. Rogovenko Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

Alecsander Pavlovich Berlinsky, Russian Jew, was
born on 16.9.1896 in Irkutsk, Siberia. He attended a high
school in Irkutsk, from which he did not graduate. He left
school at the age of 16, in order to go into the cinema-
tograph business, remaining in that line till 1918, when
the revolution broke out. He escaped to Manchuli, Manchuria,
where he remained for a year and conducted a similar trade.
Following his marriage, which took place in Manchuli, he
and his wife proceeded to Harbin, arriving there in 1920.
He opened a small watch-repairing shop and was taught that
trade by an expert who was employed by him. As conditions
improved, he enlarged his business and also took up the
jewellery line. However, when the Soviets took over the
Chinese Eastern Railway, trade got bad, as most of his clients
were employees of the Chinese Eastern Railway and have been
purchasing his wares on credit, for which he was not reimbursed.
He departed from Harbin and arrived locally in 1929. Here
he was employed for about one year by Wirth, jewellers, then
conducting business at 51 Nanking Road. Resigning from Wirth,
he opened his own, jewellery and watch-repairing business,
and has been conducting it since 1930. It is reported that
in 1934 two Hai Alai players, Chatto and Rafael of Spanish
nationality assisted Berlinsky financially. Following which
he was able to expand the business and removed his shop to
better premises at 787 Avenue Joffre, at present known as
the "Ural Jewellery Store."

His father was a private in the former Russian
Imperial Army and is now residing in the U.S.S.R. He has

Alecsander Pavlovich Berlinsky，俄籍犹太人，1896年9月16日出生于西伯利亚伊尔库茨克。他就读于伊尔库茨克的一所中学，但未毕业。他16岁辍学，进入电影行业，一直从事该行业直到1918年革命爆发。他逃至满洲里，在那里停留了一年并经营类似业务。婚后（婚礼在满洲里举行），他和妻子前往哈尔滨，于1920年抵达那里。他开了一家小型钟表修理店，并由一名受雇于他的专家教授该行手艺。随着情况好转，他扩大了业务，并涉足珠宝行业。然而，当苏联接管中东铁路时，生意变得糟糕，因为他的大多数客户是中东铁路的员工，且赊购他的商品，这些款项并未得到偿还。他离开哈尔滨，于1929年抵达本地。在这里，他为位于南京路51号的珠宝商 Wirth 工作了约一年。辞去 Wirth 的工作后，他开设了自己的珠宝和钟表修理业务，并自1930年以来一直经营至今。据悉，1934年，两名西班牙籍的海莱（Hai Alai，音译）球员 Chatto 和 Rafael 在资金上协助了 Berlinsky。此后，他得以扩大业务，并将店铺迁至霞飞路787号更佳的 premises，即现在的“乌拉尔珠宝店”。

他的父亲曾是前俄罗斯帝国军队的一名列兵，目前居住在苏联。他

no idea what his father may be doing, as he absolutely lost

His wife Elizoveta Vasilevna, was born on 24.9.1900
in Perm, Russia. She was educated and remained in Perm
till the Revolution, when she left and escaped over the
border into Manchuli. There her marriage took place. She
is the daughter of a merchant, who also was the owner of
a shipping company, running passenger boats on the River
Kama, between Perm and Kazan. It is believed he is still
residing in Russia.
They have two children, a son, Vadim and a daughter,
Ludmilla, both were born in Harbin on the 30.5.1923 and
28.10.1924 respectively.
The son is attending the Public School for Boys and
the daughter the Sacred Heart Convent.
Owing to unsettled conditions, Mr. Berlinsky desires
to leave Shanghai with his family and take up permanent
residence in Australia.
He was arraigned before the French Mixed Court on
August 5, 1929 for "Fraud." However, he was released as
the complainant dropped the charge and the matter was settled
amicably between them, (See Special Branch File D-401).
On June 26, 1936 he was fined $50 by the French
Police for "Receiving Stolen Property," (See Special Branch
File D-7827).
Apart from the above nothing detrimental is known by
this office against him.
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee.

完全不知道父亲可能在做什么，因为他已经有很长一段时间彻底失去了与父亲的联系。
他的妻子 Elizoveta Vasilevna，1900年9月24日出生于俄罗斯彼尔姆。她接受过教育，并留在彼尔姆直到革命爆发，当时她离开并越境逃至满洲里。在那里举行了婚礼。她是一位商人的女儿，该商人还拥有一家航运公司，经营往返于彼尔姆和喀山之间卡马河上的客船。据信他仍居住在俄罗斯。
他们有两个孩子，儿子 Vadim 和女儿 Ludmilla，分别于1923年5月30日和1924年10月28日出生于哈尔滨。
儿子就读于男童公学，女儿就读于圣心女修院。
由于局势动荡，Berlinsky 先生希望携家人离开上海，在澳大利亚永久定居。
他曾于1929年8月5日因“欺诈”罪在法国混合法庭被提审。然而，由于原告撤诉，且双方友好解决了此事，他被释放，（参见特务科档案 D-401）。
1936年6月26日，他因“收受赃物”被法国警察罚款50美元，（参见特务科档案 D-7827）。
除上述情况外，本局未发现对他不利的记录。
他在俄国难民委员会登记。

1937 for minor breaches of local traffic regulations
(ranking during prohibited hours, obstruction, waiting in
"No Waiting" areas, etc.), and has been fined from $2 to
$10 in connection therewith.

Maurice TUTTELMAN, a Jew of Egyptian extraction,
was born in Shanghai on October 1, 1905, and until
approximately 1930 enjoyed British protection and all
those facilities offered by such protection. In that
year, however, his British passport having expired and
Egypt having become a self-governing unit, he became
a person "without nationality" since there was no official
Egyptian representative in Shanghai and since British
protection as previously afforded Egyptians had been
withdrawn. He is now in possession of Passport No. 4578
issued on July 10, 1937 by the Commissioner of Police of
the former City Government of Greater Shanghai. In this
document he is described as being without nationality.

TUTTELMAN has been married twice, his first wife
having been Grace HAIMOVICH, from whom he secured a divorce
in the Shanghai Special District Court in October 1934 on
the grounds of incompatibility. He was given the

REPORT
Date March 29, 19 38.

Subject Mrs. Martha Camincian, applicant for a certificate of good
character.
Made by D.P.S. Rogovenko Forwarded by C. Crawford A.J.

Martha Camincian, Rumanian, was born on 27.7.1892. She
has been a resident of Shanghai as far back as 1910 and also
spent several years in Tientsin. She once made a trip to
the U.S.A. with her husband. By profession she is a beauty
expert and managed her own business at her residence, earning
between $150 to $200 per month. At one time her husband,
G.S.Camincian, deserted her and kept company with a woman
known as "Vera," who posed as Mrs. Camincian. They have
since been reconciled.

She left Shanghai on 31.8.37 for Hongkong and later
for Bangkok where she joined her husband. Mr. A.L.Brandt,
Secretary of Brandt & Rodgers, Ltd., has known her for a
period of three years and confirms the above.

Her husband was employed for two years by the Reyer
Construction Corps., Inc., in their electrical department.
Subsequently he opened his own electrical installation,
heating and plumbing concern on Museum Road. Same he
liquidated prior to his departure from this city about a
year ago.

The Camincians are unknown to the local Rumanian
Association. However, this association does not issue passports
to Rumanian citizens, same being issued by the Rumanian
Legation at Tokio.

Nothing detrimental is known by this office against them.

D.P.S.
**〔签名：Rogovenko〕**

D.C.(Special Branch)

**〔左侧手写批注：2/3 3/3〕**
