由 D.P.S. Rogovenko 呈报 经 C. Crawford A.J. 转呈

玛莎·卡明西安，罗马尼亚人，出生于1892年7月27日。她自1910年起即为上海居民，并在天津居住过数年。她曾与丈夫一同前往美国旅行。她的职业是美容专家，在住所经营自己的生意，月收入在150至200美元之间。有一段时间，她的丈夫G.S.卡明西安抛弃了她，并与一名自称“卡明西安夫人”的名叫“薇拉”的女子在一起。此后两人已和解。

她于1937年8月31日离开上海前往香港，随后前往曼谷与丈夫团聚。百兰罗德有限公司（Brandt & Rodgers, Ltd.）秘书A.L.布兰特（A.L. Brandt）先生认识她已有三年，并证实了上述情况。

她的丈夫曾在雷耶建筑公司（Reyer Construction Corps., Inc.）电气部门工作两年。随后他在博物馆路开设了自己的电气安装、供暖和管道工程公司。大约在一年前离开本市之前，他将该公司清算关闭。

本地罗马尼亚协会对卡明西安夫妇并不了解。然而，该协会不向罗马尼亚公民签发护照，护照由驻东京的罗马尼亚公使馆签发。

本处室未掌握任何对他们不利的信息。

D.P.S.
**〔签名：Rogovenko〕**

副督察长（特科）

**〔左侧手写批注：2/3 3/3〕**

Dear Sir,

at 1220 Avenue Road and who on account of events
in Shanghai has left that city on August 31-st
1937 for Hong Kong and later for Bangkok where
she has joined her husband, Mr. G.S.Camincian.

She is a Rumanian by marriage (German by birth)
born in 1892 July 27. The certificate is to the
effect that she was not implicated in any crime
and was a bonafide citizen of that city.

Your kind help will be greatly appreciated,
and the above document need to be attached to the
application; the rule is that the certificate must
be issued in the place where the applicant has spent
the last five years.

Any expenses connected with this certificate
will be remitted immediately upon your request.

Yours truly
Martha Camincian

REPORT
Date April 1, 1938.

Subject I.R. Cohen - Application for a certificate of
good character from the Municipal Police

Made by D.S. Larby Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. S

Isaac Ramon (alias Raymond) Cohen, Iraqian, was
born in Shanghai on February 14, 1909, his parents being
Baghdad Jews.

After completing his education at the Shanghai
Jewish School, Cohen secured employment as a shop
assistant with the firm of Boyes, Bassett Ltd.
Subsequently, he has been employed as a salesman of
refrigerating machinery by the firms of Andersen,
Meyer and Company Ltd., and Mustard and Company Ltd.,
respectively.

Although no charges have been preferred against
Cohen, he is mentioned in the records of the Boarding
House Section as having failed to settle his account
with the proprietor of a boarding house wherein he
resided during June, 1933. While there is no further
information regarding this individual in the records
of either the Municipal Police or of the French Police,
enquiries show that Cohen possesses an unsavory reputation
in Shanghai and is generally regarded as an over-sexed,
plausible and unscrupulous rogue and gigolo with a great
liking for pretentious display.

D.C. (Special Branch).

（左侧手写批注：D.Bk. 1/4）
（右下签名：B.J. Hanley. D. S.）

Isaac Ramon（又名 Raymond）Cohen，伊拉克人，1909年2月14日出生于上海，其父母为巴格达犹太人。

Cohen 在上海犹太学校完成学业后，受雇于 Boyes, Bassett Ltd. 公司担任店员。随后，他分别受雇于 Andersen, Meyer and Company Ltd. 公司和 Mustard and Company Ltd. 公司，担任制冷机械推销员。

虽然未对 Cohen 提出任何指控，但在寄宿公寓组的记录中提及，他未能结清1933年6月期间居住的一家寄宿公寓业主的账目。尽管在工部局警务处或法租界警务处的记录中均无关于此人的进一步信息，但调查显示，Cohen 在上海名声不佳，普遍被视为一个好色、能言善辩且肆无忌惮的流氓和男妓，酷爱虚荣炫耀。

D.C.（特务科）。

Made by D.P.S. Rogovenko Forwarded by C. Caspari S.

Leo Isaac Jack Kosloff, Russian Jew, was born on
12.10.12 at Harbin, Manchuria. He left for Tientsin in
1922 with his grand-father. There he attended the Tientsin
Grammar School from 1922 to 1928. Subsequently he was
employed by Beiner & Co., till his arrival in Shanghai on
3.12.30. Since 1.1.31 he has been employed as a constable
in the Chinese Maritime Customs River Police.
His father was killed in the Great War and his
mother is residing in Buenos Aires, Argentine.
He will be proceeding on long leave next April and
will visit his mother.
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against him.

D.P.S. Rogovenko
D.P.S.

D.C. (Special Branch)

Leo Isaac Jack Kosloff，俄罗斯犹太人，1912年10月12日出生于满洲哈尔滨。1922年随祖父前往天津。1922年至1928年间，他就读于天津文法学校。随后受雇于 Beiner & Co. 公司，直至1930年12月3日抵达上海。自1931年1月1日起，他受雇于中国海关水警队担任巡捕。
其父在第一次世界大战中阵亡，其母现居阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯。
他将于明年四月休长假并探望其母。

SHANGHAI, March 30th, 1936.

To The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Police.

Sir,

I, the undersigned, arrived in Shanghai on
December 3rd, 1930, and since January 1st, 1931, have
been employed with the Chinese Maritime Customs River
Police.

At present I am due to proceed on long leave and
contemplate visiting Chile and the Argentine. As the
Consuls of these two countries require a letter of
good conduct to be issued by the Shanghai Municipal Police
prior to issuing a visa, could you kindly oblige me with
same. For references, Mr. Wm. C. Woodfield, Chief of the
River Police, will be glad to speak on my behalf if called
upon to do so.

Yours faithfully,

L. S. Todoroff
pages.zh:
上海，1936年3月30日。

致警务总监，
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

先生：

本人于1930年12月3日抵达上海，自1931年1月1日起受雇于中国海关水警队。

目前本人拟休长假，计划前往智利和阿根廷。由于这两国领事馆在签发签证前要求出具由上海公共租界工部局警务处签发的品行良好证明信，恳请阁下惠予办理。如需证明人，水警队队长 Wm. C. Woodfield 先生乐意在需要时为我作证。

此致，
敬礼

L. S. Todoroff

April 8, 38

B.L. Mamysh - applicant for a certificate of character.

D.S.I. Prokofiev.

Veniamin ( Benjamin ) Leontievich Mamysh, Russian of
Jewish extraction, born on January 13,1395 at Rostov-on-Don, South
Russia. He is reported to have left the U.S.S.R. for China in
1918 and subsequently to have resided at Harbin until 1920 after
which he proceeded to Shanghai. Here he is reported to have been
employed as an architectural assistant with Palmer & Turner from
1924 to 1929,after which he has been working in the same capacity
in the Public Works Department of the Shanghai Municipal Council.
His service will terminate on April 30,1938 on account of the re-
cent reorganization of the Public Works Department which resulted
in a reduction in staff.

Mr. Mamysh intends to leave for Argentina in order to
join his brother, Mr. M.Mamysh residing at Alsino 3117, Buenos
Aires.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants'Committee,
118/1 Moulmein Road and at present resides at the Clements Apart-
ments, Rue Lafayette, Apt. 25.

While in Shanghai he did not come to the notice of the
Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an undesi-
rable character.

D. S. I.

D. C. ( Special Branch).

As I am leaving my services with the Shanghai Municipal
Council at the end of this month,I decided to go to Buenos Aires,Ar
Argentina (South America),to join my brother and his family there.
To obtain a visa from the Agrentinian Minister to Tokyo,Japan-
(The only representative on the Far East) - a Police certificate
of good behavior is required.
Therefore I would be very much obliged if you would kindly
issue such a certificate to me. I am herewith pleased to attach a
certificate from the Russian Emigrants' and Relief Association in
Shanghai,dated Marsh II,1938.
Thanking you in anticipation.I am
faithfully yours,
B.Mamysh

Made by D.P.S. Rogovenko Forwarded by C. Crawford L.S.

Boris Rafailovich Rabinovitch, Russian Jew, was
born on December 13, 1896 at Vilna, Poland. He was
educated at a commercial school in Vladivostok, following
which he took a two year course at the Kyoto Imperial
University, Kyoto, Japan. On completion, he proceeded
to Harbin during 1920. There he obtained a position with
Schusterovitch & Co., importers and exporters. He was
connected with same for four years. Leaving Harbin he
arrived in Shanghai on April 15, 1924. Locally he was
employed by S. Behr & Mathew, Ltd., from 1924 to June
1937. At present he conducts a small egg business.

He has been divorced from his wife six years ago
and his son is in her custody. About a year ago he was
remarried to Dr. Ida Leiboshetz. She obtained a certificate
of good character previously (see S.B. File D.8264/67).

In Vladivostok, his father was the proprietor of
a mineral water plant. Both his parents are not living,
their death took place in Vladivostok.

He is not registered with any of the Russian
associations and has in his possession an expired
passport issued by the former Bureau of Public Safety.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against him.

D. P. S.
D.C. (Special Branch).

Boris Rafailovich Rabinovitch，俄罗斯犹太人，1896年12月13日出生于波兰维尔纳。他在海参崴的一所商业学校接受教育，随后在日本京都帝国大学修读两年课程。毕业后，他于1920年前往哈尔滨。在那里，他在进出口商 Schusterovitch & Co. 公司获得职位。他与该公司保持了四年的联系。离开哈尔滨后，他于1924年4月15日抵达上海。在本地，他于1924年至1937年6月受雇于 S. Behr & Mathew, Ltd. 公司。目前他经营一家小型鸡蛋商行。

他于六年前与妻子离婚，儿子由女方抚养。大约一年前，他与 Ida Leiboshetz 博士再婚。她此前已获得过品行良好证明书（参见特务科档案 D.8264/67）。

在海参崴，其父拥有一家矿泉水厂。双亲均已去世，逝世地点均为海参崴。

他未在任何一个俄罗斯协会登记，持有一张由前公安局签发的过期护照。本处未发现对其不利的记录。

D. P. S.
D.C.（特务科）。

Subject A.V. Liapin - applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by J.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by C Crawford

Alexey Vassilievich LIAPIN, Russian, born on February 11,
1894 in the Orenburg Province, Russia. Former junior officer of
the Orenburg Cossack Troops; he is reported to have left Russia
for Sinkiang, China, in 1920, together with a detachment of the
"white" army in Siberia and subsequently to have made his way to
Peking where he resided for about two years, after which he pro-
ceeded to Hankow. In the latter town he was employed in the Mu-
nicipal Police of the Russian Concession from 15-2-23 to 2-3-25
when the concession was taken over by the Chinese Government.
From 20-10-25 to 30-6-29 he was employed with the Hankow branch
of Goerz & Diener, Ltd. first as an overseer and later as a super-
intendent of their casing factory. Following the closing down of
the factory he was employed as a superintendent of the Leather
factory of Messrs Ivanoff & Co. in the same town from 1-9-29 to
1-9-30 when the factory was closed. In October, 1930 he arrived in
Shanghai. Here he was employed in a similar capacity with Siemssen
& Krohn for three years. Leaving this position owing to a reduc-
tion in staff he established the "International Casing Co." in
Chapei in partnership with a certain Mr. Black, ex-employee of the
Chinese Maritime Customs. The business proved to be a failure and
was closed in 1934, following which Liapin was without fixed em-
ployment until 1936, when he was engaged by Roland Commercial Co.,
8 Dixwell Road, in which he worked for about 6 months. At present
he is employed in the Casing & Feather Department of Henningsen
Produce Co., 250 Dawgin Road.

Liapin is married and has one daughter aged 6 years. Ac-
cording to his own statement, he instituted divorce proceedings re-
cently, after the completion of which he intends to marry Mrs T.I.

（左侧边缘印章内容：ITALIAN CONSULATE GENERAL SHANGHAI 11 APR 1938）

Alexey Vassilievich LIAPIN，俄国人，1894年2月11日出生于俄罗斯奥伦堡省。前奥伦堡哥萨克部队下级军官；据报他于1920年随西伯利亚“白”军的一支分队离开俄罗斯前往中国新疆，随后辗转至北平，在那里居住了约两年，之后前往汉口。在汉口，他于1923年2月15日至1925年3月2日期间受雇于俄国租界工部局警务处，直至该租界被中国政府收回。从1925年10月20日至1929年6月30日，他就职于 Goerz & Diener, Ltd. 的汉口分行，起初担任监工，后来担任其肠衣厂的主管。在该工厂关闭后，他于1929年9月1日至1930年9月1日期间，在同一城市受雇于 Ivanoff & Co. 先生的皮革厂担任主管，直至该厂关闭。1930年10月，他抵达上海。在此地，他在 Siemssen & Krohn 公司以类似职位工作了三年。后因裁员离开该职位，他与一位前中国海关雇员 Black 先生在闸北合伙成立了“国际肠衣公司”（International Casing Co.）。该生意证明是失败的，并于1934年关闭，此后 Liapin 一直无固定职业，直到1936年受雇于狄思威路8号的 Roland Commercial Co.，在那里工作了约6个月。目前，他受雇于 Dawgin 路250号 Henningsen Produce Co. 公司的肠衣与羽毛部。

Liapin 已婚，育有一名6岁的女儿。据他自己陈述，他最近启动了离婚程序，完成后打算与 T.I.

（左侧边缘印章内容：意大利驻上海总领事馆 1938年4月11日）

In accordance with the instructions of D.C.
(Special Branch) on memo. dated 25.4.38, in reference to
the attached letter addressed to the Commissioner of
Police by Mr. C.J. Ordus, of U.S.S. Memphis, San Diego,
California, U.S.A. requesting that he be furnished with
a letter stating whether his wife, namely, Emelia Garcia
has a criminal record in Shanghai, and explaining that
she resided in Shanghai at various times between 1928 and
1937, enquiries at the Finger Print Bureau and other
registries of the S.M.P., failed to reveal any record of
the woman in question having been mentioned in connection
with any criminal activities.

The records of the Boarding House Section,
however, show that at various times between 1932 and
1937, she resided in different boarding houses in the
International Settlement together with the writer of the
attached letter, when she always gave her name as Mrs.
Amelie Ordus, but variously described herself as being
of Mexican, Spanish and American nationality.

Mr. L. D. Pease, Vice Consul, Passport Office,
U.S.A. Consulate-General, who was interviewed, stated that
it was not necessary to obtain any particulars concerning
the woman in question, other than her criminal record if any,
consequently details of her marriage were not verified.

Logan
D. S. I.

D. C. (Special Branch)

Made by D.P.S. Rogovenko Forwarded by C. Crawford.

Cyril Cyrillievitch Chernosvitoff, Jnr., Russian, was
born on 15.11.15 at Petrograd, Russia. Leaving his birthplace,
he arrived in Shanghai with his parents and sister in 1916.
During the same year he left Shanghai for various places in
China, including Hankow, Tientsin, Newchwang, Tsingtao and Harbin.
He attended school at the above places. He returned to Shanghai
in July 1930 and was a pupil of the Thomas Hanbury School for
two years. On the 10.3.32, he enlisted in the Russian Detach-
ment, S.V.C., and now holds the rank of corporal.
His different moves in China may be explained by the fact,
that his father was formerly a manager of the Russian Asiatic
Bank, and in that role was subject to transfers to the various
branches of the Bank. At present, he is connected with the
Russian Mutual Credit Corp.
His mother resides at Christchurch, New Zealand, and has
been conducting a chicken farm for the past eleven years. She
has been divorced from her husband since 1916, the divorce
took place in Hankow.
The applicant wishes to proceed to New Zealand in order
to join his mother.
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against him.

D.B.R.
29/4

D.C. (Special Branch)

D. P. S. Rogovenko

Cyril Cyrillievitch Chernosvitoff, Jnr.，俄国人，1915年11月15日出生于俄罗斯彼得格勒。离开出生地后，他于1916年随父母和姐姐抵达上海。同年，他离开上海前往中国各地，包括汉口、天津、牛庄、青岛和哈尔滨。他在上述地方上学。他于1930年7月返回上海，并在汉璧礼学校就读两年。1932年3月10日，他加入上海万国商团俄国分队，目前军衔为下士。
他在中国各地的迁徙可以解释为：他的父亲曾是俄亚银行经理，因职务关系需调往该银行的各个分行。目前，他与俄国互助信贷公司有关联。
他的母亲居住在新西兰基督城，过去十一年一直经营着一个养鸡场。她自1916年起与丈夫离婚，离婚手续在汉口办理。
申请人希望前往新西兰与母亲团聚。
他已在俄国侨民委员会登记。
本处未掌握任何关于他的不利记录。

D.B.R.
29/4

D.C. (特科)

Special Branch
May 5, 1938.

Memorandum concerning the firm of BERAHA & STETTEN

The following information regarding the Beraha family
and the firm of Beraha & Stetten has been collected.
Although having managed to avoid police action the Berahas
are reported to have been involved in a number of questionable
deals and reference to certain of these is contained in the
following paragraphs.

Shortly after the termination of the Great War MATTEO
BERAHA came to Shanghai from Salonika and established a
company for the purpose of conducting trade in jewels.
Beraha is about 55 years of age and claims that he is of
Spanish-Jewish origin. He has never lived in Spain but
states that his family emigrated to Salonika at the end of
the 18th century.

In Shanghai Matheo Beraha's business prospered and large
profits were made, it is said, through purchases of stolen
uncut diamonds. A similar business was established in Tientsin
and was operated by his two sons.

In 1926 Dario and Alberto Beraha, nephews of Matheo,
arrived in Shanghai and were taken into the firm. About
this time both the Shanghai and Tientsin offices claimed that
they suffered loss by theft and suspicions were entertained
that the claims were bogus, had been made in order to defraud the
Insurance Company.

In 1929 Matheo formed a company known as Filmos Ltd. for
the distribution of cinema films. In this venture he became
associated with S. Skenazi, a Turk, and a Spanish Jew named
Ramos. It became known that the above-mentioned trio were
responsible for the bribing of the local representative of
Fox Films and were thus able to acquire films at below market
rates. In connection with his film business Matheo Beraha built
pages.zh:
特科
1938年5月5日。

关于 BERAHA & STETTEN 商行的备忘录

以下有关 Beraha 家族及 Beraha & Stetten 商行的信息已收集完毕。
尽管 Beraha 家族成功避免了警方的行动，但据报道他们卷入了一些可疑的交易，下文段落中提及了其中某些交易。

大战结束后不久，MATTEO BERAHA 从萨洛尼卡来到上海，成立了一家公司，旨在开展珠宝贸易。Beraha 现年约55岁，自称具有西班牙犹太血统。他从未在西班牙生活过，但声称其家族于18世纪末移民至萨洛尼卡。

据说，Matheo Beraha 在上海的生意兴隆，通过购买被盗的原石钻石赚取了巨额利润。他的两个儿子在天津也建立了类似的生意并加以经营。

1926年，Matheo 的侄子 Dario 和 Alberto Beraha 抵达上海并加入该行。大约在此时，上海和天津的办事处均声称因盗窃遭受损失，有人怀疑这些索赔是虚假的，旨在欺骗保险公司。

1929年，Matheo 成立了一家名为 Filmos Ltd. 的公司，用于发行电影。在此项目中，他与土耳其人 S. Skenazi 和一位名叫 Ramos 的西班牙犹太人合作。众所周知，上述三人负责贿赂福克斯电影公司（Fox Films）的当地代表，从而能够以低于市场的价格获取影片。与其电影业务相关，Matheo Beraha 建造了

pages.en:
- 2 -

the Hongkew, Chekiang, Lafayette and Broadway Cinemas.

Beraha's Company became known as Beraha & Stetten in
1930 when M.R.D. and F. Stetten, Germans, joined the firm.
Both the Stettens reside in Paris.

In September, 1932, the Customs authorities are reported
to have received information that the firm of Beraha and Stetten
were in possession of certain cases containing smuggled jewelry.
A search warrant was obtained from the Spanish Consulate but
as a result of delay by the Consular authorities Beraha had time
to remove the cases in question.

In 1933 Beraha obtained the local agency for INTORGRINO
(U.S.S.R. films) and also negotiated with Centrosojus for
jewel mining concessions in Borma, Siberia.

Beraha and Stetten since 1933 have continued in the jewel
trade and suspicions are still entertained that traffic in
uncut diamonds, the ownership of which is doubtful, is carried
on. The agency for Soviet films has been discontinued but
the Skenaze - Beraha Cinema Combination still exists. Alberto
Beraha acts as representative in China for "L'Illustration,"
a French paper published in Paris which has printed some
fairly strong anti-Japanese propaganda.

At the time of the overthrow of the Spanish Monarchy,
the Berahas in common with many other Spanish emigres, register-
ed with the Spanish Consulate in Shanghai. Dario Beraha has,
however, subsequently acquired French nationality and is re-
gistered at the French Consulate.

At present D. Beraha is stated to be in the U.S.A., M.
Beraha in Hongkong and A. Beraha in Shanghai.
pages.zh:

虹口、浙江、拉斐特和百老汇电影院。

1930年，当德国人 M.R.D. 和 F. Stetten 加入该行后，Beraha 的公司更名为 Beraha & Stetten。两位 Stetten 均居住在巴黎。

据报道，1932年9月，海关当局收到情报，称 Beraha and Stetten 商行拥有若干装有走私珠宝的箱子。虽从西班牙领事馆获得了搜查令，但由于领事当局延误，Beraha 有时间移走涉案箱子。

1933年，Beraha 获得了 INTORGRINO（苏联电影）的本地代理权，并与 Centrosojus 就西伯利亚 Borma 地区的珠宝开采特许权进行谈判。

自1933年以来，Beraha and Stetten 继续从事珠宝贸易，人们仍怀疑其进行所有权存疑的原石钻石交易。苏联电影的代理权已终止，但 Skenaze - Beraha 影院联合体仍然存在。Alberto Beraha 担任在巴黎出版的法国报纸《画报》（"L'Illustration"）在华代表，该报刊登了一些相当强烈的反日宣传内容。

在西班牙君主制被推翻时，Beraha 家族与许多其他西班牙流亡者一样，在上海西班牙领事馆进行了登记。然而，Dario Beraha 随后获得了法国国籍，并在法国领事馆登记。

目前，据称 D. Beraha 在美国，M. Beraha 在香港，A. Beraha 在上海。

Made by D.P.S. Rogovenko Forwarded by 〔此处转录不清〕

Leonid Bustaff, Russian, was born on 11.10.12 at Hankow,
China. His father was formerly connected with the Russian
Municipal Council, Russian Concession, Hankow. At the
outbreak of the Great War, he enlisted in the army and has
been missing since.

He arrived in Shanghai when he was a young boy and as
an orphan, he was placed in the custody of the Marist Brothers.
He commenced his education at the St. Francis Xavier's
College, Shanghai. On reaching the higher grades in 1927,
he was sent to Turin, Italy, to complete his education at a
seminary and to join the holy order of the Marist Brothers.
He returned to Shanghai in 1930 as he did not wish to remain
an ecclesiastic. He was made an assistant master in the
St. Francis Xavier's College and taught the preparatory class
for about a year. From 1931 to January 1932 he was employed
by the Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury in their editorial
office. He also worked for several months at Studio d'Art,
now defunct. At present he is the accountant of Messrs
"Ucometal," Ltd., metal importers, and has been connected with
them in that capacity since March 1933.

He was a member of the American Company, U.V.C., from
September 1931 to September 1932. During the 1937 hostilities
he served in the S.M.P. Specials.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against the applicant.

列昂尼德·布斯塔夫（Leonid Bustaff），俄国人，1912年10月11日出生于中国汉口。其父曾任汉口俄租界俄国市议会职员。大战爆发时，他应征入伍，此后下落不明。

他幼年时抵达上海，身为孤儿，被交由玛利斯特兄弟会（Marist Brothers）监护。他在上海圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Francis Xavier's College）开始接受教育。1927年升入高年级后，他被送往意大利都灵，在一所神学院完成学业并加入玛利斯特兄弟会神圣修会。1930年他返回上海，因为他不愿继续担任神职人员。他受聘为圣方济各沙勿略学院的助理教员，教授预科班约一年。1931年至1932年1月，他就职于《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury）编辑部。他还曾在现已停业的“艺术工作室”（Studio d'Art）工作数月。目前他是金属进口商“Ucometal”有限公司的会计，自1933年3月起一直以此身份任职。

1931年9月至1932年9月期间，他是美国公司 U.V.C. 的成员。在1937年的战事期间，他在工部局警务处特别队服役。

他已在俄国侨民委员会登记。本局未发现对该申请人不利的记录。

Alexius Zaharovich Dimoff, Russian, was born on
March 10, 1899 at Nerchensk, Siberia. He attended a
village school for a few years, then worked for his
parents on their farm. During the civil war he served
under General Gleboff in the White Army. The remnants
of this army retreated from Vladivostock to Genzan, Korea
and subsequently arrived in Shanghai during 1923 in several
transports. He lived on one of these transports for
about two years, which at that time were anchored off
Woosung.

During 1925 he was employed by the B.A.T. for about
four months, then worked as a groom for Mr. M.C. Springfield,
former Deputy Commissioner, S.M.P., for one year. He
served in the Russian Detachment, S.V.C. from September 1,
1927 to September 30, 1929. Since January 1930 he has
been employed as a watchman by Andersen, Meyer & Co., Ltd.
He married Elizabeth Ivonovna Molyakina on November 3, 1937.

Elizabeth Ivonovna Dimoff, Russian, wife of the
above was born on September 1, 1892 at Perm, Russia.
After completing her education, she left for Harbin in
1911, where she conducted her own dressmaking business
till her departure from Harbin. She arrived in Shanghai
on April 23, 1932, here she was occupied with a similar
business but on a smaller scale, which she suspended after
her marriage.

Mr. and Mrs. Dimoff are registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee. Nothing detrimental is known by
this office against them.

D.C. (Special Branch).
D. P. S. **〔签名〕**

**〔左侧手写批注〕**

阿列克谢·扎哈罗维奇·迪莫夫（Alexius Zaharovich Dimoff），俄国人，1899年3月10日出生于西伯利亚涅尔琴斯克。他在村校就读数年，随后在父母的农场劳作。内战期间，他在格列博夫将军（General Gleboff）麾下的白军服役。这支军队的残部从符拉迪沃斯托克撤退至朝鲜元山，随后于1923年分几批运输船抵达上海。他在其中一艘运输船上生活了约两年，这些船当时锚泊在吴淞口外。

1925年期间，他受雇于英美烟草公司（B.A.T.）约四个月，随后为前工部局警务处副巡捕长 M.C. Springfield 先生担任马夫一年。1927年9月1日至1929年9月30日，他在工部局义勇队俄国分队服役。自1930年1月起，他受雇于安得生·梅耶有限公司（Andersen, Meyer & Co., Ltd.）担任看守。他于1937年11月3日与伊丽莎白·伊万诺芙娜·莫利亚金娜（Elizabeth Ivonovna Molyakina）结婚。

伊丽莎白·伊万诺芙娜·迪莫娃（Elizabeth Ivonovna Dimoff），俄国人，上述人士之妻，1892年9月1日出生于俄国彼尔姆。完成学业后，她于1911年前往哈尔滨，在那里经营自己的裁缝生意直至离开哈尔滨。她于1932年4月23日抵达上海，在此从事类似但规模较小的生意，婚后停止经营。

迪莫夫夫妇已在俄国侨民委员会登记。本局未发现对他们不利的记录。

D.C. (特别股)。

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford.

Sergey Evgenievich KIRILOFF, Russian, born on
August 9, 1888 at Mitava, Latvia ( formerly a part of Russia).
A graduate of the Polytechnic Institute ( Architectural Depart-
ment ) in Riga, he is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from
Vladivostok in 1925. Here he was employed in his professional
capacity first with L.A. Hudec and later with A.Juenson & Co.,
Ltd, local architects, until 1926 when he left for Canada.
Following his return to Shanghai in April, 1933 he was employed
as a draughtsman with the Asia Realty Company until 15-8-34
and with J.H.Gonda, architect, from 1-11-34 to 15-4-36, after
which he was without fixed employment for a period. From
March, 1937 he has been conducting the Pacific Stamp Company,
957 Buboling Well Road.

He resides at 204/14 Yu Yuen Road, together with
his wife, Mrs Inna I. Kiriloff, 44, and their son Leo, 22 years

谢尔盖·叶夫根尼耶维奇·基里洛夫（Sergey Evgenievich KIRILOFF），俄国人，1888年8月9日出生于拉脱维亚米塔瓦（原属俄国）。他是里加理工学院（建筑系）毕业生，据报于1925年从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海。在此地，他先受雇于 L.A. Hudec，后受雇于本地建筑师 A.Juenson & Co., Ltd.，从事专业工作，直至1926年前往加拿大。1933年4月返回上海后，他受雇于亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）担任绘图员，直至1934年8月15日；随后于1934年11月1日至1936年4月15日期间受雇于建筑师 J.H.Gonda，此后有一段时间无固定职业。自1937年3月起，他经营太平洋邮票公司（Pacific Stamp Company），地址为卜罗林井路957号。

他居住在愚园路204/14号，与其妻因娜·I·基里洛娃（Inna I. Kiriloff）夫人（44岁）及22岁的儿子利奥（Leo）同住。

基里洛夫已在摩尔门路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会以及上海市政府警察局（注册号 12748）登记。他持有上海市政府警察局于1936年8月12日签发的第15522号护照。

Sir,
    I have the honour of asking you to deliver me a certificate

    A certificate of character, which I have sent to Australia
has been delivered to me in June 1938. The certificate I am now
applying for will enable me to prolong my stay in the United States.

    In June 1938 I gave to Mr. Prokofieff of the Shanghai
Municipal Police all information concerning myself:-
Basil Sourochnikoff, born 22nd July 1908 in Samara, Russia,
arrived in Shanghai in 1921. Graduated from the French Municipal
School in 1924, from the "Universite d'Aurore" in 1929 (Civil
Engineering Course), employed by the French Municipal Council,
Shanghai, since the 1st July 1929, have never been in prison
or in a mental ward.

to remain
                                Your obediently

Shanghai for the United States in March, 1938 together with her
two daughters. He also has two sisters in Shanghai one of whom
is employed with the Fonciere et Immobiliere de Chine, and the
other with the International Savings Society.

Vadim Vassilievich SENTIANIN, Russian, born on February 21, 1898, at Cheliabinsk, Russia. According to his own statement, he left Russia for China in 1921 and subsequently resided in Harbin. In 1933 he graduated from the Polytechnic Institute (Electro-mechanical Department) in that city. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in June, 1935. Here he is reported to have been employed with Bills Motors as a foreman from September, 1935 to October, 1936, after which he joined the Compagnie Francaise de Tramways et d'Eclairage Electriques de Shanghai, his present employment.

He is registered with the Council of United Russian Public Organization (CURD) and the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau ( Reg. No. 16389 of 10-7-36 ). At present he resides at 40 Rue Pere Robert together with his wife, Mrs Raisia L. Sentianin nee Beloozeroff, 33, and their son aged 14 years.

While in Shanghai he did not come to the notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an undesirable character.

C. Gafarov
D. S. I.

REPORT
Date June 21, 1938.
Subject Communication dated May 4, 1938 from Mr. Harry Walter LENT
requesting a Certificate of Character.
Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by C. **〔此处转录不清〕**

Harry Walter LENT, British, was born in Shanghai on
June 26, 1917. He was educated locally at Gonzaga College
and for a short period in the United Kingdom. From 1932
until 1935 he served a course of apprenticeship as an
engineer with Messrs. Auto Palace and The Far Eastern
Aviation Company. On completion of his apprenticeship
he made his way to sea as a deck-hand on the s.s. "Gertrude
Maersk" plying between this port and New York. In the
summer of 1937 he secured a position with the Furness
Bermuda Line and had not since returned to Shanghai.

Nothing is known by the Municipal Police to the applicant's
detriment from a criminal, political or moral point of view.
He is, or rather was, on good terms with several local
persons of good standing, including Dr. W.E. O'Hara, who
signed and forwarded the attached reference to Mr. Lent
some three months ago at the latter's request. It is
learned from Mr. Lent's brother. Mr. R.C. Lent, that the
Certificate of Character is required by the American
authorites to complete the filing of his application for
naturalization as an American citizen. Similar information
secured from the local American Consulate-General reveals
that a Certificate of Character testifying that the applicant
has no Police Record in Shanghai will be required before
Lent can complete the necessary application.

D.C. (Special Branch).

Ja. Pitts
D. S.

哈里·沃尔特·伦特（Harry Walter LENT），英国籍，1917年6月26日出生于上海。他在本地冈萨加学院（Gonzaga College）接受教育，并在英国短期就读。从1932年至1935年，他在 Auto Palace 公司和远东航空公司（The Far Eastern Aviation Company）作为工程师学徒服役。学徒期满后，他在往返于本港与纽约之间的“格特鲁德·马士基”号（s.s. "Gertrude Maersk"）轮船上担任甲板水手出海。1937年夏，他在弗内斯百慕大航线公司（Furness Bermuda Line）获得职位，此后未再返回上海。

从刑事、政治或道德角度来看，公共租界警务处未发现任何不利于申请人的记录。他与其几位当地有声望的人士关系良好，或者说曾经关系良好，其中包括 W.E. 奥哈拉博士（Dr. W.E. O'Hara），后者应伦特先生的请求，约三个月前签署并转交了附上的推荐信。据伦特先生的兄弟、工部局公共卫生处的 R.C. 伦特（R.C. Lent）先生称，美国当局要求提供品行证明书，以完成其归化为美国公民的申请备案。从美国驻当地总领事馆获得的类似信息显示，在伦特完成必要申请之前，需要提供一份证明申请人在上海无警方记录的品行证明书。

D.C.（特务科）。

Ja. 皮茨（Pitts）
D. S.

Shanghai,

Dear Sir,

As I am at present living in New York
and intend to take out American Papers, it
will be necessary for me to have a certifi-
cate from you advising that I have no Police
Record in Shanghai.

I am a British subject, born in Shang-
hai and have been a resident in Shanghai
until the begining of 1937, when I left for
New York - I enclose a letter addressed to
you by Dr. O'Hara certifying that I have
been a resident in your city.

Will you kindly issue the necessary
certificate and hand the same to the bearer
of this letter, Mr. Robert C. Lent of the
Shanghai Municipal Council, Health Department
for transmission to me.

I appreciate any assistance you can
give me in this matter, and remain.

Yours truly,

H. Walter Lent

上海，

亲爱的先生：

由于我目前居住在纽约，并打算办理美国国籍文件，因此需要您出具一份证明，表明我在上海没有警方记录。

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by C. Crawford i.d

Ivan Stepanovich CHIJOFF, Russian, born on January 27,
1890, at Hvalynsk, Saratov Province, Russia. He is reported
to have arrived in Shanghai from Japan in 1930. A confection-
er by occupation, he was employed with G. Tchakalian's
Bakery, Range Road, from November, 1930, to September, 1933,
after which from 1934 he has been conducting his own
confectionery at 133 Avenue Haig.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee,
118/1 Moulmein Road, and with the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau ( Reg. No. 4660 of 27.6.36). At present he
holds passport No. 17390 issued by the latter Bureau on
17.6.37. He resides at the above address together with
his wife, Mrs. Irene A. Chijoff, 29, nee Alalin, and their
children aged 7 and 6 years, respectively.

According to his own statement, Chijoff, prior to his
coming to Shanghai, resided in Harbin from 1920 to 1921; in
Tientsin from 1921 to 1928; in Mukden from 1928 to 1930 and
in Tokyo in 1930.

While in Shanghai he did not come to the notice of the
Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an
undesirable character.

（批：Prokofiev.）

Subject Y.J. KALOUSEK, applicant for a certificate of good character.

Made by D.S. Rogovenko Forwarded by C. Crawford S.S.

Yaroslav John Kalousek, Czechoslovakian, was born on
15/3/10 at Harbin, Manchuria. He accompanied his parents
to Peking and Tientsin and arrived in Shanghai during the
latter part of 1915. He commenced his education in 1916
at the St. Francis Xavier's College and completed same in
December, 1925. Subsequently he was employed as an
apprentice by Mark L. Moody, Ltd. Inc., for two years
(1926-7). Having completed his apprenticeship, he joined
H.S. Honigsberg in January 1928 in the capacity of workshop
supervisor. He left them in January 1929 in order to take
up a similar position with Hartzenbusch Motors, with whom
he remained till June 1930, when he resigned and joined Mills
Motors, Ltd. Inc., as assistant motor engineer. In November,
1930 he obtained a better position with the China General
Omnibus Co., Ltd., in their engineering department as engineer
in charge of the night staff. He followed this line of work
till December 1931 when he had to resign as the continuous
night work began to impair his health.
Since April 1932 he has been connected with G.E. Marden
& Co., Ltd., as engineer in charge of their workshop.
He was married on 31/10/34 to Luba (nee Napoloff), a
Harbin educated girl and whose father is a merchant, trading
in Harbin and Dairen. Their son, George, was born on
11/7/37 at Shanghai.

雅罗斯拉夫·约翰·卡卢塞克（Yaroslav John Kalousek），捷克斯洛伐克籍，1910年3月15日出生于满洲哈尔滨。他随父母前往北京和天津，并于1915年下半年抵达上海。他于1916年开始在圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Francis Xavier's College）接受教育，并于1925年12月完成学业。随后，他在 Mark L. Moody, Ltd. Inc. 当了两年学徒（1926-27年）。学徒期满后，他于1928年1月加入 H.S. Honigsberg，担任车间主管。他于1929年1月离开该公司，以便在 Hartzenbusch Motors 担任类似职位，他一直工作到1930年6月，当时他辞职并加入 Mills Motors, Ltd. Inc.，担任助理汽车工程师。1930年11月，他在中国通用巴士有限公司（China General Omnibus Co., Ltd.）工程部获得了更好的职位，担任夜班人员主管工程师。他从事这项工作直到1931年12月，由于持续的夜班工作开始损害他的健康，他不得不辞职。
自1932年4月以来，他一直受雇于 G.E. Marden & Co., Ltd.，担任车间主管工程师。
他于1934年10月31日与卢巴（Luba，娘家姓 Napoloff）结婚，卢巴是在哈尔滨受教育的女孩，其父亲是在哈尔滨和大连经商的商人。他们的儿子乔治（George）于1937年7月11日出生于上海。

Baron Daniel Alexandrovich FITTINGHOF-SHELL, Russian
of German origin, born on December 28, 1906 at Ekaterinburg, Russia.
He is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Hankow some time
towards the end of 1934. A motor car mechanic by occupation, he
was employed here with Hartzenbush Motors for about 6 months,
after which he was connected with the Auto-Palace Co., Ltd, Nan-
king branch, for about 2 years. In June, 1937 he returned to Shang-
hai and soon afterwards joined Bills Motors, Avenue Joffre. Until
November, 1937 he was attached to their Nanking branch. Shortly
prior to the occupation of Nanking by the Japanese troops he left
that city for Shanghai via Hankow and Hongkong. At present he is
employed in the tire department of the firm in Shanghai.

According to his own statement, prior to his coming
to Shanghai he resided in Urga (1911-1920), Peking ( 1920-1922)
Tientsin ( 1922-1928 ) and Hankow ( 1928-1934 ). In the latter
town he was employed with Arnhold Co.

The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and with the Shanghai City Govern-
ment Police Bureau ( Reg. No 16273 of 25-12-36). He resides at
295 Route Cohen, House 10, Apt. 1 together with his wife, Baroness
Eugenie P. Fittinghof-Shell nee Kozoolin, 24 ( S.C.G. Police Bureau
Reg. No. 10706 of 6-7-36).

While in Shanghai they did not come to the notice of
the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an un-
desirable character.

A. Prokofiev

CONFIDENTIAL

MEMORANDUM FOR: Director, Central Intelligence
SUBJECT: Soviet Reaction to Certain U.S. Courses of Action on Cuba

1. The paper at the enclosure hereto presents an estimate of probable Soviet reactions to certain courses of action which the US might take with respect to Cuba. It was prepared by the Office of National Estimates in coordination with all other components of the intelligence community and has been concurred in by the United States Intelligence Board.

2. In preparing this estimate, the intelligence community has drawn upon all available information. Nevertheless, because of the paucity of reliable evidence regarding Soviet intentions and decision-making processes, the conclusions reached must be regarded as tentative and subject to revision as new information becomes available.

3. The estimate considers three broad categories of US action: (a) diplomatic and economic measures short of military force; (b) limited military actions such as air strikes against selected targets; and (c) full-scale invasion and occupation of Cuba. For each category, it assesses the likelihood of various Soviet responses ranging from verbal protests to direct military confrontation.

4. With respect to diplomatic and economic measures, the Soviets are likely to respond with strong verbal condemnation and increased aid to Cuba, but will probably avoid direct military involvement unless they perceive a threat to their own security or prestige. They may also seek to exploit the situation for propaganda purposes and to strengthen ties with other Latin American countries.

5. In the event of limited military actions, the Soviets would almost certainly protest vigorously and might take some retaliatory measures, such as increasing military aid to Cuba or conducting naval exercises near US shores. However, they would be unlikely to initiate direct military conflict unless they believed that the US was preparing for a full-scale invasion.

6. A full-scale invasion and occupation of Cuba would pose the greatest risk of Soviet military response. The Soviets might view such an action as a direct challenge to their influence in the Western Hemisphere and could respond with measures ranging from increased military aid to Cuba to direct military intervention. The likelihood of such a response would depend on a number of factors, including the perceived threat to Soviet interests, the level of US commitment, and the international political climate.

7. It should be noted that the Soviet leadership is not monolithic and that there may be differences of opinion within the Kremlin regarding the appropriate response to US actions on Cuba. Some hardliners may advocate a more aggressive stance, while others may favor a more cautious approach. The ultimate decision will likely reflect a compromise between these competing viewpoints.

8. In conclusion, while the Soviets are likely to respond strongly to any US action on Cuba, the nature and extent of their response will depend on a variety of factors. The US should carefully consider the potential consequences of its actions and be prepared to adjust its strategy as the situation evolves.

Enclosure:
Estimate of Probable Soviet Reactions to Certain US Courses of Action on Cuba

事由：苏联对美国在古巴某些行动方针的反应

1. 随函附上的文件评估了美国可能针对古巴采取的某些行动方针所引发的苏联可能的反应。该文件由国家评估办公室（Office of National Estimates）编制，并与情报界的所有其他部门协调完成，且已获得美国情报委员会（United States Intelligence Board）的认可。

2. 在编制本评估报告时，情报界利用了所有可获得的信息。然而，由于有关苏联意图和决策过程的可靠证据匮乏，所得出的结论必须被视为暂时性的，并需随着新信息的出现而进行修订。

3. 本评估考虑了三大类美国行动：(a) 未达到使用武力程度的外交和经济措施；(b) 有限的军事行动，例如对选定目标进行空袭；以及 (c) 对古巴进行全面入侵和占领。对于每一类行动，报告评估了从口头抗议到直接军事对抗等各种苏联反应的可能性。

4. 关于外交和经济措施，苏联可能会以强烈的口头谴责和增加对古巴的援助作为回应，但除非他们认为自身的安全或威望受到威胁，否则可能会避免直接的军事介入。他们还可能寻求利用这一局势进行宣传，并加强与其他拉丁美洲国家的联系。

5. 如果发生有限的军事行动，苏联几乎肯定会提出强烈抗议，并可能采取一些报复性措施，例如增加对古巴的军事援助或在美国海岸附近举行海军演习。然而，除非他们认为美国正准备进行全面入侵，否则他们不太可能发起直接的军事冲突。

6. 对古巴进行全面入侵和占领将带来苏联做出军事反应的最大风险。苏联可能会将此类行动视为对其在西半球影响力的直接挑战，并可能采取从增加对古巴的军事援助到直接军事干预等一系列措施。此类反应的可能性取决于多种因素，包括对苏联利益构成的感知威胁、美国的投入程度以及国际政治气候。

7. 需要注意的是，苏联领导层并非铁板一块，克里姆林宫内部对于如何适当回应美国在古巴的行动可能存在意见分歧。一些强硬派可能主张采取更具侵略性的立场，而其他人则可能倾向于更为谨慎的做法。最终的决定很可能反映了这些相互竞争观点之间的妥协。

8. 总之，虽然苏联可能会对任何美国在古巴的行动做出强烈反应，但其反应的性质和程度将取决于各种因素。美国应仔细考虑其行动的潜在后果，并准备随着局势的发展调整其战略。

Date July 19, 1938.

Subject A.L. GOSTINOPOLSKY, the applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

Andrey Leonidovitch GOSTINOPOLSKY, Russian, was born in Vladivostok on February 9, 1912. It is reported that he together with his mother left Vladivostok for Japan in 1921. He first arrived in Shanghai in the beginning of 1923. Here he attended the Hanbury School for boys until 1926 when he left for Tientsin, where from January 1927 to December 1928 he attended the Tientsin Grammar School. Upon leaving the school he was without any fixed employment until the end of 1929 when he obtained a position with the Chihli Motors Limited where he remained till November 1930.

He returned to Shanghai in November 1930 and in December of the same year obtained a position as a time keeper with the Bills' Motors. He resigned on his own accord in November 1934 and in December of the same year joined the Auto Palace, 100 Route Cardinal Mercier, in which firm he at present holds the post of manager of the Spare Parts Department.

The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, on the strength of passport No.4800 issued by the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau on May 25, 1937.

At present he resides with his mother at 1562, Avenue Joffre, Apartment E7.

While in Shanghai he did not come to the notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an undesirable nature.

Subject John A. Dzedzulia - Applicant for Police Certificate
of Good Character.

Made by D.S. Henchman Forwarded by C. Gasona [签名]

J.A. Dzedzulia, Russian, born in Harbin 5th January,
1911, arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in 1927.

In Shanghai Dzedzulia joined the Russian Regiment
of the S.V.C. with which unit he served until his voluntary
resignation on 3rd December, 1930.

Following his military service, he was employed
in a hair-dressing establishment and subsequently opened
his own beauty-parlour at 113 Love Lane. In 1933 he married
K.P. Koltsoff and has a son aged 3 years.

Late in August, 1937, Dzedzulia went to Nanking
where he obtained employment as a barber. On 6th September,
shortly after his arrival, he was arrested together with
his mother, A.A. Dzedzulia, on the suspicion of the Chinese
Authorities that they were engaged in espionage on behalf
of the Japanese. They were imprisoned and subsequently sent
from Nanking to Shanghai where they arrived on 15th September
and were handed over to the Chinese Police at the Zi Ka Wei
Sub-Station. On 18th September, their identities having
been established by the Russian Emigrants' Committee, they
were released.

For the past six months, Dzedzulia has operated
the Aureole Beauty Parlour at 936 Bubbling Well Road.

There is nothing in Police records detrimental
to the character of either Dzedzulia or his mother.

D.S. Henchman [签名]
D. S.

J.A. Dzedzulia，俄国人，1911年1月5日出生于哈尔滨，1927年从哈尔滨抵达上海。

在上海，Dzedzulia 加入了上海义勇队（S.V.C.）的俄国团，并在该部队服役直至1930年12月3日自愿辞职。

退役后，他在一家理发店工作，随后在爱多亚路（Love Lane）113号开设了自己的美容厅。1933年，他与 K.P. Koltsoff 结婚，育有一子，现年3岁。

1937年8月下旬，Dzedzulia 前往南京，在那里受雇为理发师。9月6日，即抵达后不久，他和他的母亲 A.A. Dzedzulia 因涉嫌为中国当局怀疑从事亲日间谍活动而被捕。他们被监禁，随后从南京被押送至上海，于9月15日抵达，并被移交给徐家汇分巡捕房的中国警察。9月18日，在俄国侨民委员会确认其身份后，他们获释。

在过去六个月里，Dzedzulia 经营着位于静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）936号的 Aureole 美容厅。

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

Veniamin Maksimilianovitch PRIGOROVSKY, Russian was born in Chita Transbaikal Province, Siberia on October 26, 1920.

It is reported that he together with his parents left the U.S.S.R. for Manchuria in 1921 and subsequently resided in Imianpo Station, Chinese Eastern Railway. He arrived in Shanghai together with his parents in the end of 1931. Here he attended the St. Joan D'Arc College for one year then Ecole Remi for one year and for the past four years has been studying in the Commercial School of the Russian Orthodox Confraternity.

His father, M. Prigorovsky has been employed with the S.M.C. for the past six and half years in the capacity of a Police Watchman No. 101, and his mother L.P. Prigorovsky for the past six years has been employed as a teacher in the Commercial School of the Russian Orthodox Confraternity.

Applicant is the God-son of Mr. G.E. Radionoff, formerly a Sub-Inspector in the S.M.Police, who is in Australia at present and who is assisting the applicant in the matter of obtaining an immigration visa to that country.

While in Shanghai the applicant did not come to the notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an undesirable nature.

（签名）

Nicolai Arhipovitch Pamfiloff, Russian, was born in Blagoveshchensk, Siberia on December 19, 1919.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and at present resides at 833/21, Avenue Joffre.

Arcadi Ivanovitch Somnitelnoff, Russian was born
in Samara, Russia on March 18, 1913.

It is reported that he together with his family
left the U.S.S.R. for Manchuria in 1922 and subsequently
resided in Harbin and Chan-chun.

He arrived in Shanghai in the end of 1932 and on
January 1, 1933 he joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C. from
where on February 1, 1933 he resigned on his own accord. He
rejoined the Regiment on August 21, 1933 and completion of a
7 months contract he again resigned on March 21, 1934. Then
on July 21, 1934 he joined the China General Omnibus Co. as
a driver from which position he resigned on March 23, 1935.
Upon leaving the China General Omnibus Co. he began to work
as an engraver and electro-plater for Messr. A. Zaushkin -
Jewellery and Watch Store at 647, Avenue Joffre.

The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee , 118/1 Moulmein Road on the strength of
pass-port No. 19250 issued by the Police Bureau of the City
Government of Shanghai on 20.9.35.

While in Shanghai the applicant did not come to
the notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any
activities of an undesirable nature.

Subject M.P. OMELINA, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Crawford. W.S.

Natia Pavlovna Omelina, Russian was born in Ijevsk,
Russia on June 20, 1898.

According to her own statement she left Russia
for Manchuria together with her family in 1902, and subse-
quently resided in Harbin, where her father was employed with the
Chinese Eastern Railway.

She arrived in Shanghai in the end of 1931 and
resided at 7-A Miller Road together with her common law
husband P.L. Zvetkoff, employee of the Shanghai Water Works
Co. at that time. After the death of P.L. Zvetkoff in
February 17, 1937 she obtained a position as a nurse in the
Hospital of the Russian Orthodox Confraternity, from where
she resigned on her own accord on March 30, 1938. On April 1,
1938 she took up her present employment as a governess in Mr.
L. Holpers' house.

Mr. L. Holper and family are intending to proceed
to Australia in near future and are willing to take the
applicant with them.

M.P. Omelina is registered with the Council of the
United Russian Public Organizations (Soro).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
against either the applicant or her late common law husband
P.L. Zvetkoff.

D.C. (Special Branch)

d.a. Pavloff -
D.P.S.

她于 1931 年底抵达上海，与其事实丈夫 P.L. Zvetkoff 同住于米勒路 7-A 号，P.L. Zvetkoff 当时是上海自来水公司的雇员。1937 年 2 月 17 日 P.L. Zvetkoff 去世后，她在东正教兄弟会医院获得了一份护士职位，并于 1938 年 3 月 30 日自愿辞职。1938 年 4 月 1 日，她开始在 L. Holpers 先生家中担任家庭女教师，即目前的职务。

L. Holper 先生及其家人打算在不久的将来前往澳大利亚，并愿意带申请人同行。

M.P. Omelina 已在俄罗斯公共组织联合会（Soro）理事会登记。

Alexandre Zaharovitch Rodkin, Polish Jew, was
born in Poltavskaya Province, Russia on February 2, 1899.
According to his own statement he left Russia for Poland in
1918 and resided there until 1929, during which period he
became a naturalized Polish subject. He arrived in Shanghai
in the end of 1929 and took over the post of the manager of
the Polish-Chinese Trading Corp. The above firm was liquidat-
ed in the end of 1936 and since December 23, 1936 he is a repre-
sentative of John Butt & Co. (London) Limited. During his
stay in Shanghai he was connected with the Polish Chamber of
Commerce, the member of which he still remains at present.
He is in possession of the Polish passport No. 61/35 issued by
the local Polish Consulate General on May 18, 1938.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to the character of the applicant.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Gausden. S.I.

Alexandre Constantinovitch ILKOFF, Russian, born in
Zabaikalskaya Province, Russia on March 17, 1890. According
to his own statement he left the U.S.S.R. in 1920 and subse-
quently resided in Tientsin. There he was employed as
Drawing teacher with Saint Louis College and in the same
time connected with Wilson & Co. and Robert Smith & Co. where
he was engaged in the capacity of a wool expert. He arrived
in Shanghai in 1932 and between November 1933 and June 1934
was employed as a night porter with Metropol Hotel. In the
begining of 1935 he obtained his present position as a teacher
with the Commercial School of the Russian Orthodox Confraternity.

Nadejda Pavlovna Ilkoff, nee Farafontova, Russian, born
in Blagoveshchensk, on October 24, 1891. She is reported
to have resided in Harbin ever since her childhood as her
father was connected with the Chinese Eastern Railway. On
completion of her education in Harbin she obtained a position
with the same concern. In 1923 while visiting her sister in
Tientsin she have met and later married A.C. Ilkoff.

The applicants are registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road on the strength of passport No.
13897, issued by the Police Bureau of the City Government of
Shanghai on May 13, 1937.

While in Shanghai the applicants did not come to the
notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any
activities of an undesirable nature.

Alexandre Constantinovitch ILKOFF，俄国人，1890年3月17日出生于俄国外贝加尔省（Zabaikalskaya Province）。据其自称，他于1920年离开苏联，随后居住在天津。在那里，他在圣路易斯学院（Saint Louis College）担任绘画教师，同时与 Wilson & Co. 和 Robert Smith & Co. 有联系，担任羊毛专家。他于1932年抵达上海，1933年11月至1934年6月期间，在大都会酒店（Metropol Hotel）担任夜班门房。1935年初，他获得现任职位，在俄罗斯东正教兄弟会商业学校（Commercial School of the Russian Orthodox Confraternity）担任教师。

Nadejda Pavlovna Ilkoff，婚前姓 Farafontova，俄国人，1891年10月24日出生于布拉戈维申斯克（Blagoveshchensk）。据报她自幼居住在哈尔滨，因为其父与中东铁路有关联。在哈尔滨完成学业后，她在同一家机构任职。1923年，她在天津探望姐姐时结识了 A.C. Ilkoff，随后与其结婚。

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by [手写签名]

Gregory Alexandrovich GITOFF, Soviet citizen, born on October 14,1886 at Brest-Litovsk,Russia. According to his own statement, he left Russia for China in 1920 together with his family and subsequently resided in Harbin,where he was employed as a teacher of chemistry in the Harbin Polytechnic Institute from 1920 to 1935, after which he proceeded to Shanghai arriving in this city in August of the same year. Here he worked in an experimental laboratory at Kiangwan owned by Mr. M.A. Joffe, proprietor of the Sine-Pharmacy,14 Broadway, and adviser and superviser of manufacturing at the Sine Laboratory Co.,Ld,20 Rue Massenet, from February,1936 until the outbreak of the hostilities in Shanghai in 1937. At present he is reported to be employed in the Farimex Distilling Works,751 Avenue du Roi Albert.

In 1926 ,while at Harbin, he became a Soviet citizen and at present holds passport No 075942 issued by the Soviet Consulate-General at Shanghai on 31-3-36. He is one of the prominent members of the local Soviet Citizens' Club.

The applicant's wife, Mrs Lydia Yakovlevna Gitoff nee Zander,Russian, born on 1-5-1899 at St.Petersburg,Russia, is a music teacher by profession. She arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in September,1934 travelling on Soviet passport No 23354 issued on 28/9/26 at Harbin . In 1935 she renounced her Soviet citizenship and registered with the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau as an emigrant ( Reg. No 11174 ).

Their son, Alexis Gitoff,born on 20-12-1920 at Harbin at present attends the Public & Thomas Hanbury Public School for Boys in Shanghai.

Mrs. Gitoff's daughter by her first husband was married in 1937 to Mr. H.L. Jones,formerly of the S.M.Police.

格里戈里·亚历山德罗维奇·吉托夫（Gregory Alexandrovich GITOFF），苏联公民，1886年10月14日出生于俄罗斯布列斯特-立托夫斯克（Brest-Litovsk）。据其自述，他于1920年与家人离开俄罗斯前往中国，随后居住在哈尔滨，1920年至1935年间在哈尔滨工业大学担任化学教师，之后前往上海，于同年8月抵达本市。在此期间，他在江湾的一家实验实验室工作，该实验室属于百老汇路14号“信谊药房”（Sine-Pharmacy）业主M.A. Joffe先生；同时他还担任马思南路20号信谊实验室有限公司（Sine Laboratory Co., Ltd）的制造顾问及主管，任职时间从1936年2月至1937年上海战事爆发。据悉，他目前受雇于阿尔伯特王路751号法美酿酒厂（Farimex Distilling Works）。

1926年在哈尔滨期间，他成为苏联公民，目前持有苏联驻上海总领事馆于1936年3月31日签发的第075942号护照。他是当地苏联公民俱乐部的知名成员之一。

申请人的妻子，莉迪亚·雅科夫列夫娜·吉托夫夫人（Mrs Lydia Yakovlevna Gitoff，娘家姓赞德 Zander），俄罗斯人，1899年5月1日出生于俄罗斯圣彼得堡，职业为音乐教师。她于1934年9月从哈尔滨抵达上海，持1926年9月28日在哈尔滨签发的第23354号苏联护照旅行。1935年，她放弃苏联国籍，并在上海市政府警察局登记为难民（登记号11174）。

他们的儿子，阿列克谢·吉托夫（Alexis Gitoff），1920年12月20日出生于哈尔滨，目前就读于上海的公立暨汤玛斯·汉伯理男校（Public & Thomas Hanbury Public School for Boys）。

吉托夫夫人与其前夫所生的女儿于1937年嫁给了H.L.琼斯先生，后者曾任工部局警务处警员。

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by W Legan A.I.

Nicolai Nicolaevitch BRUDASTOFF, naturalized
Chinese citizen of Russian origin, was born in Kostroma,
Russia on November 22, 1892.
He attended the Technological Institute in St.
Petersburg and graduated from the same in 1918 with a
Diploma of a Chemical Engineer. From the period of 1918
to 1921 he was a teacher of Chemistry in the Vladivostok
Polytechnic School. He left Vladivostok for Manchuria
in the end of 1921 and subsequently resided in Harbin. In
June 1922 he obtained employment with the Chinese Eastern
Railway from where in July 1931 he resigned on his own
accord. He arrived in Shanghai in December 1931. In
October 1932 he joined as a Chief Chemist with S.J.E. Jensen
Chemical Laboratories, at that time situated at No. 6, The
Bund. Since 1934 the above firm is known as United Laboratories
of Shanghai, 114 Nanking Road and the applicant is still
connected with that firm.

Maria Gavrilovna BRUDASTOVA, widow of G. Zafataeff,
nee Loubinia, naturalized Chinese citizen of Russian origin,
was born in Odessa, Russia on September 28, 1898.
She was married to G. Zafataeff, an Officer of the
Imperial Russian Army who was killed during the Civil War in
Russia. She met N.N. Brudastoff in Vladivostok and became
his common law wife. She proceeded with him to Harbin,
where in September 1924 they were legally married. From her
first husband she had a son who, it is believed, was adopted
by N.N. Brudastoff, as at present he is known under the name
of Brudastoff and not Zafataeff.

尼古拉·尼古拉耶维奇·布鲁达斯托夫（Nicolai Nicolaevitch BRUDASTOFF），俄裔归化中国公民，1892年11月22日出生于俄罗斯科斯特罗马（Kostroma）。他就读于圣彼得堡理工学院，并于1918年毕业，获得化学工程师文凭。1918年至1921年间，他在符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）理工学校担任化学教师。1921年底，他离开符拉迪沃斯托克前往满洲，随后居住在哈尔滨。1922年6月，他在中东铁路找到工作，并于1931年7月自愿辞职。他于1931年12月抵达上海。1932年10月，他加入位于外滩6号的S.J.E. Jensen化学实验室，担任首席化学师。自1934年起，上述公司更名为上海联合实验室（United Laboratories of Shanghai），地址为南京路114号，申请人至今仍与该公司保持雇佣关系。

玛丽亚·加夫里洛夫娜·布鲁达斯托娃（Maria Gavrilovna BRUDASTOVA），G. Zafataeff之遗孀，娘家姓卢比尼亚（Loubinia），俄裔归化中国公民，1898年9月28日出生于俄罗斯敖德萨。她曾嫁给沙皇俄国陆军军官G. Zafataeff，后者在俄国内战期间阵亡。她在符拉迪沃斯托克结识N.N. Brudastoff并成为其事实婚姻妻子。她随同Brudastoff前往哈尔滨，两人于1924年9月在那里正式结婚。她与第一任丈夫育有一子，据信该子已被N.N. Brudastoff收养，因为他目前使用Brudastoff姓氏而非Zafataeff。

尤韦纳利·加夫里洛维奇·布鲁达斯托夫（Yuvenaly Gavrilovitch BRUDASTOFF），俄裔归化中国公民，1916年2月6日出生于西伯利亚哈巴罗夫斯克（Habarovsk）。1921年，他随母亲离开俄罗斯，随后居住在满洲哈尔滨。1929年，他离开哈尔滨前往天津，并在那里就读于圣路易斯学院（St. Louis' College）直至1932年。他于1932年初抵达上海，1933年进入公立暨汤玛斯·汉伯理男校就读，于1934年10月离校。此后他一直无固定职业。

玛丽亚·阿列克谢耶夫娜·布鲁达斯托夫（Maria Alexeevna BRUDASTOFF），俄罗斯人，申请人之母，1866年3月1日出生于俄罗斯科斯特罗马省。据申请人陈述，其母在该省居住至1924年，随后离开苏联前往满洲，并与儿子居住在哈尔滨。她于1936年抵达上海，目前与申请人一同居住在阿尔伯特王路310号。

N.N. Brudastoff及其家人已在俄罗斯难民委员会登记。

Date August 27, 19 38.

Subject George S. Radbill, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by W Logan 8/8

Enquiries show that George Semenovich RADBILL
is a Russian of Jewish origin who was born on May 6, 1917
at Moscow. He is reported to have left Russia for China
together with his parents in 1920 and subsequently resided
in Harbin where he attended a commercial school. In
September, 1931 he arrived in Shanghai from Harbin. Here
he continued his education in the Public and Thomas Hanbury
School for boys. Upon graduating from the latter school
in 1934 he was employed with the Overland Motors Ltd., 993
Bubbling Well Road, from 1-9-35 to 31-8-37 as an office
clerk. His next employment was in the capacity of a
truck driver with the Shanghai Coal Company, 715 Yu Yuen
Road, from 26-11-37 to 31-1-38, after which he worked for
short periods first in Albert Motors, 65/67 Avenue du Roi
Albert and later at Jessfield Club, Yu Yuen Road as a
cashier. From 20-8-38 he has been employed as a driver of
a motor car of Major-General Telfer-Smollett, Commander of
the British Forces in Shanghai.

The applicant's father, Mr. S.M. Radbill, 47, has
been residing in Shanghai since December 1931. Immediately
upon arrival here he called at the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118 Moulmein Road, and declared that he wished to
renounce his Soviet citizenship and to register as an
emigrant. On that occasion he stated that being in the
employ of the Chinese Eastern Railway in Harbin he had to
become a Soviet citizen in 1927 in order to keep his
employment, but that he always had been against the principles

由特别调查员普罗科菲耶夫（Prokofiev）撰写。经 W Logan 8/8 转呈

调查显示，George Semenovich RADBILL 是一位犹太裔俄罗斯人，1917年5月6日出生于莫斯科。据悉，他于1920年随父母离开俄罗斯前往中国，随后居住在哈尔滨，并在那里就读于一所商业学校。1931年9月，他从哈尔滨抵达上海。在此之后，他继续在公立暨汤玛斯·汉伯理男校接受教育。1934年从该校毕业后，他于1935年9月1日至1937年8月31日期间受雇于静安寺路99号大陆汽车公司（Overland Motors Ltd.），担任办公室职员。他的下一份工作是在愚园路715号上海煤炭公司（Shanghai Coal Company）担任卡车司机，时间为1937年11月26日至1938年1月31日，之后他先后在阿尔伯特王路65/67号的Albert Motors和愚园路极司菲尔路俱乐部（Jessfield Club）短暂工作，担任出纳。自1938年8月20日起，他受雇为驻沪英军司令Telfer-Smollett少将的汽车司机。

申请人的父亲S.M. Radbill先生，47岁，自1931年12月起居住于上海。抵达此地后，他立即前往莫尔尼姆路118号的俄罗斯难民委员会，声明希望放弃苏联国籍并登记为难民。当时他表示，由于在哈尔滨受雇于中东铁路，他不得不于1927年成为苏联公民以保住工作，但他一直反对该原则

Subject E.A. Shestakoff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by W. Logan A.S.P.

Evgeny Arhipovitch SHESTAKOFF, Russian was born
in Habarovsk, Siberia, on February 22, 1902.
He is reported to have left the U.S.S.R. for
Manchuria in 1922 and subsequently resided in Harbin. In
1923 he joined the Harbin Law Faculty where he studied until
1927. He arrived in Shanghai in 1927 and in June of the same
year obtained an employment with the Russian Ex-Officers' Club.
He left the club in May 1928 and in November of the same year
joined A. Corrit & Co. as a clerk of works. He left that con-
cern in April 1929 and in December of the same year joined the
Far Eastern Credit Co. as a book keeper. He worked there
until February 1937 when his services were dispensed with due to
a reduction in staff. For the past four years the applicant
has been the owner of a licensed boarding house situated at 925
/3, Avenue Joffre.

Raisa Nikolaevna SHESTAKOVA, nee Mihailova,
Russian, was born in Krasnoyarsk, Siberia, on September 24,
1904.

she was employed as a dancing hostess until 1929 when she met

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by /Signature/

Richard Adolfovitch SEIDEL, Russian of a German
origin, was born in Volynskaya Province, Russia, on October
27, 1906.

According to his own statement, he escaped from
the U.S.S.R. into Manchuria in 1930 and subsequently resided
in Harbin. He arrived in Shanghai in the end of 1930 and
early in 1931 joined as an apprentice the German Beauty
Parlour, 1626 Bubbling Well Road. He left Shanghai for
Peiping in 1931 and returned in 1933. Here he again worked
as a barber until 1934 when he left for Nanking where he
obtained an employment with the Elite Beauty Parlour. He
returned to Shanghai in 1937 and soon afterwards bought over
the German Beauty Parlour, of which he is still a proprietor.

Elena Iurievna SEIDEL, nee Opalinskaya, Russian
of a Lithuanian origin, was born in the Maritime Province,
Russia, on July 23, 1910. She is reported to have left the
U.S.S.R. in 1924 and subsequently resided in Harbin. She
arrived in Shanghai in 1930 together with the applicant and
in December of the same year they were legally married.
They have two sons, one named Robert born on 12-12-35 in
Nanking and the other - Ewald, born on 6-4-38 in Shanghai.

The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, on the strength
of passport No. 15839 issued by the Police Bureau of the
City Government of Shanghai on March 2, 1937.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to the character of Mr. and Mrs. Seidel.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by W. Logan A.S.S.

Lidia Sergeevna ZEPHIROFF, nee JDANOFF, Russian,
Soviet Citizen, was born in Barnaul, Siberia, on June 20,
1899.

According to her own statement, prior and during the
Revolution in Russia she was residing in Omsk, Siberia,
where in 1918 she married N.S. Zephiroff. In 1922 she
together with her husband arrived in Harbin where the latter
was connected with the Chinese Eastern Railway. In 1924
she followed her husband to Shanghai where he was trans-
ferred to organize the Economical Bureau of the Chinese
Eastern Railway.

She separated from her husband in 1931 and soon after-
wards became the common law wife of one named A.L. Roubin,
who is in Australia at present.

The applicant officially divorced her husband on
August 17, 1938 and it seems that her purpose of entering
Australia is to marry A.L. Roubin. She has one daughter
named Elena N. Zephiroff born on September 27, 1923 in Harbin.

The applicant is in possession of a Soviet Passport
No. 76049 issued by the local Soviet Consulate General on
18/8/38.

While in Shanghai the applicant did not come to the
notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any
activities of an undesirable nature.

In order to be
allowed to proceed
to the Australian
Consulate General
if her desire
is to proceed
there.

gone on 6/9/38

Dear Sir

it, if you would verify this from your records,
and send me a letter corroborating the fact.

for troubling you, I am,

J. Ellam.

REPORT
Date Sept. 10, 1938.

Subject B. I. Kahans, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Crawford W.J.

Boris Isakovitch KAHANS, Latvian Jew, was born in Riga,
Latvia, on January 13, 1912. He is reported to have left
Russia in 1920 and subsequently resided in Harbin, Manchuria.
He arrived in Shanghai in the end of 1920 together with his
parents. Here he graduated from the Public School for Boys
in December 1927 and in the beginning of 1928 he left Shanghai
for Belgium, where he entered the University of Ghent,
graduating from the same in May 1932. He returned to Shanghai
in the end of 1932 and in December of the same year joined
Palmer and Turner Civil Engineers as a designer. He left that
concern on his own accord in August 1935 and in September of
the same year joined the staff of Shanghai Jewish School where
at present he holds a position of an Assistant Master of
French and Mathematics.

He is in possession of Latvian passport No. 1061 E,
issued by the Latvian Legation in Belgium on 1.10.32.

Ester Lvovna KAHANS, nee RADOMISHELSKY, Russian Jewess,
Latvian by naturalization, was born in Vladivostok on March 14,
1910. She is reported to have escaped from the U.S.S.R. into
Manchuria in 1931 and in the end of the same year arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin. Here in July 1933 she married the
applicant. From 1933 to 1935 she was employed as manageress
with the Bookstall and Curiosity Shop at 282 - 286 Yu Yuen Rd.
On September 17, 1934 they had a son born to them who was
given the name of Daniel Borisovitch Kahans.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to the character of any member of Mr. B. Kahans
family.

F A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.C. (Special Branch)        I. O. Pavloff.
                                                    D. P. S.

Boris Isakovitch KAHANS，拉脱维亚犹太人，1912年1月13日出生于拉脱维亚里加。据报道，他于1920年离开俄国，随后居住在满洲哈尔滨。他于1920年底与父母一同抵达上海。他于1927年12月毕业于上海公立男校，并于1928年初离开上海前往比利时，进入根特大学就读，于1932年5月毕业。他于1932年底返回上海，并于同年12月加入帕默与特纳土木工程师公司（Palmer and Turner Civil Engineers）担任设计师。他于1935年8月自愿离职，并于同年9月加入上海犹太学校教职员队伍，目前担任法语和数学助理教师。

他持有拉脱维亚驻比利时公使馆于1932年10月1日签发的第1061 E号拉脱维亚护照。

Ester Lvovna KAHANS，婚前姓 RADOMISHELSKY，俄罗斯犹太女性，归化拉脱维亚籍，1910年3月14日出生于海参崴。据报道，她于1931年从苏联逃往满洲，并于同年底从哈尔滨抵达上海。1933年7月，她在此地与申请人结婚。1933年至1935年期间，她在愚园路282-286号的书店古玩店担任经理。1934年9月17日，他们生下一个儿子，取名为 Daniel Borisovitch Kahans。

在工部局警务处的档案中，没有任何不利于 B. Kahans 先生家庭任何成员品行的记录。

F A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.C. (特务科)        I. O. Pavloff.
                                                    D. P. S.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Gouda. S.J.

Mrs Nadejda Iosifovna SPRAVTSOFF nee Mihailoff, Russian,
born on September 14, 1902 at Vladivostok, Russia. According to
her own statement, she left the U.S.S.R. for China in 1925 and
for the following four years resided in Harbin. In 1929 she
went to Tokyo, Japan, where she stayed for over one year. While
in Japan, she married one P.E. Spravtsoff, Soviet citizen, who at
that time was an employee of the Soviet Trade Mission at Tokyo.
In February, 1931 Mr. and Mrs Spravtsoff arrived in Shang-
hai from Japan. Shortly afterwards they renounced their allegi-
ance to the Soviet Government and took out emigrants' papers.
In 1932-1934 Mrs Spravtsoff conducted the "Dual" Milli-
nery Shop at 699 Seymour Road, after which she is reported
to have been working as a dressmaker at her home. Her husband,
a bookkeeper by occupation, left for the United States in Octo-
ber, 1937.
The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and with the S.C.G. Police Bureau
( Reg. No. 8167 of 30-8-34 ). At present she holds passport
No 12160 issued by the same Bureau on 23-7-35 for travelling to
Tsingtao. She resides at 215 Route des Soeurs, Apt. F.
While in Shanghai she did not come to the notice of the
Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an unde-
sirable character.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

娜杰日达·约瑟福夫娜·斯普拉夫佐夫（Nadejda Iosifovna SPRAVTSOFF），婚前姓米哈伊洛夫（Mihailoff），俄国人，1902年9月14日出生于俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克。据其自述，她于1925年离开苏联前往中国，并在随后的四年里居住在哈尔滨。1929年，她前往日本东京，在那里停留了一年多。在日本期间，她嫁给了 P.E. 斯普拉夫佐夫（P.E. Spravtsoff），后者为苏联公民，当时是苏联驻东京贸易代表团的雇员。1931年2月，斯普拉夫佐夫夫妇从日本抵达上海。不久之后，他们放弃了对苏联政府的效忠，并办理了移民证件。1932年至1934年间，斯普拉夫佐夫夫人在西摩路699号经营“Dual”女帽店，此后据报在家从事裁缝工作。其丈夫职业为簿记员，于1937年10月前往美国。
申请人已在莫尔缅路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记，并在上海市政府警察局登记（1934年8月30日登记号8167）。目前她持有该局于1935年7月23日签发的第12160号护照，用于前往青岛旅行。她现居住于姐妹路（Route des Soeurs）215号F公寓。
在上海期间，她未因任何不良性质的活动引起工部局警务处的注意。

Subject A.G. Dostavaloff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Crawford L. S.

Alexey Georgievitch DOSTAVALOFF, Russian, was born in
Novo-Nicolaevsk, Siberia, on March 17, 1899. He is reported
to have left Russia for Manchuria in 1922 and subsequently
resided in Harbin. From October 15, 1927 to March 1933 he
was employed in the capacity of an accountant with Bashkiroff
and Co., Automobile Dealers in Harbin. He left that firm
on his own accord and proceeded to Kirin, where, according
to his own statement, he established a motor car repair
shop. However the venture proved to be a failure. He then
left Kirin for Tientsin and after a short stay in the city
arrived in Shanghai in April 1935. In May of the same year
he was engaged by the China General Omnibus Company as a
ticket Inspector, which position he still holds at present.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee,
118/1 Moulmein Road on the strength of passport No.17826,
issued on 2-7-37, by the Police Bureau of the City Government
of Shanghai.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to the character of the applicant.

（左侧边缘手写批注：）
19/9.

A.G. Pavloff.
D. P. S.

阿列克谢·格奥尔基耶维奇·多斯塔瓦洛夫（Alexey Georgievitch DOSTAVALOFF），俄国人，1899年3月17日出生于西伯利亚新尼古拉耶夫斯克。据报他于1922年离开俄罗斯前往满洲，随后居住在哈尔滨。1927年10月15日至1933年3月，他在哈尔滨的巴什基罗夫公司（Bashkiroff and Co.，汽车经销商）担任会计。他自愿离开该公司并前往吉林，据其自述，他在那里开设了一家汽车修理店。然而该尝试以失败告终。随后他离开吉林前往天津，在该市短暂停留后，于1935年4月抵达上海。同年5月，他被英商中国公共汽车有限公司（China General Omnibus Company）聘为查票员，该职位他一直保持至今。

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C Crawford

Ivan Alexandrovitch GERASSIMOFF, Russian, was born in Moscow, Russia, on March 19, 1904. According to his own statement he graduated from the Moscow Art Academy in 1925. In 1928 he left the U.S.S.R. for Teheran, Iran and resided there until November 1935, working as a painter.

He arrived in Shanghai from Iran in December 1935, travelling on a visa No.56/49, issued by the Teheran Police on September 7, 1935. He is also in possession of a Carte d' Identite for the period 1928-1935 which is issued to all immigrants in Iran. In Shanghai he has been working in his professional capacity, painting portraits, advertisements, etc.

His wife, Mrs. Medina Zakirovna GERASSIMOFF, nee Ish-muhametova, Russian of Tartar origin, was born in Omsk, Siberia, on July 2, 1904. She is reported to have left Russia for Manchuria in 1920 and subsequently resided in Harbin. Upon graduating from a High School in Harbin she entered the Harbin 2nd School for Dentistry, graduating from same in May, 1930.

She arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in 1935 and it is believed that soon afterwards she met and started to cohabit with the applicant. They were legally married on July 9, 1937 in the Union Church. During her stay in Harbin she was a Soviet Citizen, but prior to her leaving Harbin for Shanghai she renounced her allegiance to the Soviet Government and took out emigrant papers from the Bureau for the Affairs of the Russian Emigrants in Manchoukuo. (Certificate No.31761, issued by the above Bureau.)

The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'

Subject A.I. Atkatchoonas, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Casford D.S

Alexandre Iosifovitch ATKATCHOONAS, Russian, was born
in Maritime Province, Russia, on November 11, 1907. He is
reported to have left Russia for Manchuria, together with
his father in 1910 and subsequently resided in Harbin. Upon
graduating from a High School in Harbin, in 1927, he entered
the Harbin Polytechnic Institute. However he did not complete
his studies there, leaving the Institute in 1931. He arrived
in Shanghai from Harbin in November 1931 and at the end of
the same month obtained the position of a mechanic with Lor
and Lomach Co., 100, Great Western Road. He left that firm
in April 1932, owing to its liquidation. In September 1932
he was employed by the China General Omnibus Company as a
ticket Inspector. In February 1935 he was promoted to the
rank of Chief Inspector, his present position in the Company.
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee,
118/1 Moulmein Road, on the strength of passport No.15686,
issued on 4-9-36, by the Police Bureau of the City Government
of Shanghai.
While in Shanghai, the applicant did not come to the
notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any
activities of an undesirable nature.

P.A. to D.C. (S.B.)

亚历山大·约瑟福维奇·ATKATCHOONAS，俄国人，1907年11月11日出生于俄罗斯滨海边疆区。据报他于1910年与其父离开俄罗斯前往满洲，随后居住在哈尔滨。1927年从哈尔滨一所高中毕业后，他进入哈尔滨工业大学就读。然而他并未完成学业，于1931年离开该校。他于1931年11月从哈尔滨抵达上海，并于同月底在大西路100号的 Lor and Lomach 公司获得机械师职位。由于该公司清算，他于1932年4月离职。1932年9月，他被中国公共汽车公司雇佣为查票员。1935年2月，他晋升为总查票员，这是他在该公司的现任职务。他凭上海市政府警察局于1936年9月4日签发的第15686号护照，在茂名南路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记。
在上海期间，申请人未因任何不良性质的活动引起工部局警务处的注意。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. S. R. D/8440/ Date September 22, 1938）

Subject. 1. Braunstein - applicant for a certificate of character/

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Gaspard. D. I.

Enquiries show that Ignaz BRAUNSTEIN is an Austrian citizen of Jewish origin, born on May 7, 1902, at Hadikfalva, Bukowina, Austria. He arrived in Shanghai from Europe on November 5, 1934. Here he was employed with the Pacific Merchandise Co, 133 Yuen Ming Yuen Road as an accountant until the date of his departure for Vancouver on 21-3-38 en-route to the United States. His wife, Mrs Gwendolyn Braunstein nee Bergmann, was born on October 14, 1915 at Kamyshloff, Saratov district, Russia. She joined her husband in Shanghai in October, 1935 and left for the United States together with him, in the s.s. "Empress of Russia".

In Shanghai Braunstein resided at the Palace Hotel from 6/11/34 to 2/12/34 ,after which he removed to the Foreign Y.M.C.A., Bubbling Well Road. From 1-10-35 to 31-7-37 he resided at 31 Rue Massenet and from 1-8-37 until his departure -at 55 Rue Moliere, Apt. 5.

When booking passage to Vancouver Braunstein produced Austrian passport No 871 issued in Paris on 4-10-34 valid for five years. His wife held passport No 563 issued in Shanghai on 25/2/38. It is reported that a few days before their departure from Shanghai these passports were substituted by German passports issued by the local German Consulate-General. However, enquiries show that Mr. and Mrs Braunstein are not registered at the German Consulate-General as German citizens.

On May 5, 1938 Mr. Braunstein applied to the French Police for a certificate of character, giving his address in New York. His request was granted ( No.1490 /a of 28-5-38 ).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records concerning the applicant.

（签名）
D. C. ( Special Branch )

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

主题. 1. Braunstein - 品行证明书申请人/

由特别处副督察 Prokofiev 制作。由督察 C. Gaspard 转呈。

查询显示，Ignaz BRAUNSTEIN 是奥地利公民，犹太裔，1902年5月7日出生于奥地利布科维纳的 Hadikfalva。他于1934年11月5日从欧洲抵达上海。在此地，他在圆明园路133号的太平洋商品公司（Pacific Merchandise Co）担任会计，直至1938年3月21日启程前往温哥华，途中转往美国。他的妻子，Gwendolyn Braunstein 夫人（娘家姓 Bergmann），1915年10月14日出生于俄罗斯萨拉托夫地区的 Kamyshloff。她于1935年10月在沪与丈夫团聚，并与其一同乘坐“俄罗斯皇后”号轮船前往美国。

Braunstein 在上海期间，于1934年11月6日至12月2日居住在礼查饭店，之后搬至静安寺路的青年会国际协会（Foreign Y.M.C.A.）。从1935年10月1日至1937年7月31日，他居住在马思南路31号，从1937年8月1日直至离境，居住在莫利哀路55号5室。

在预订前往温哥华的船票时，Braunstein 出示了1934年10月4日在巴黎签发的奥地利护照，编号871，有效期五年。他的妻子持有1938年2月25日在上海签发的第563号护照。据报，在他们离开上海前几天，这些护照被德国驻当地总领事馆签发的德国护照所取代。然而，查询显示，Braunstein 夫妇并未在德国总领事馆登记为德国公民。

1938年5月5日，Braunstein 先生向法国警察申请品行证明书，提供了他在纽约的地址。他的请求获准（1938年5月28日，编号 1490/a）。

工部局警务处记录中关于申请人的内容无任何不良记录。

（签名）
特别处副总监

A. Prokofiev
特别处副督察

Dear Sir:-

nine months at the Foreign Y.M.C.A. Building at Bubbling well rd.
whence I moved to the French Concession at 31. Rue Massenet.

By way of reference would like to mention that I am
an Austrian and am registered with the Austrian-German Consulate.
I am connected with the Pacific Merchandise Co., Inc., 133. Yuen
Ming Yuen rd. in Shanghai.

I left Shanghai on the 21st of March 1938 per S/S
Empress of Russia for the U.S.A.

For my stay in the French Concession I have already a
certificate from the French Police. I would very much appriciate
if you could also let me have such a statement at your earliest
convenience as I need it urgent for the local authorities.

Yours very truly

Subject A.P. Chernoff and G.P. Chernoff - applicants for certificates of
character.
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Gascoigne D.I.

Alexander Petrovich CHERNOFF, Russian, was born March 14,
1911 at Kazan, Russia. According to his own statement, he left the
U.S.S.R. for China in 1924 together with his younger brother,
G.P. Chernoff, and for the following 11 years resided in Harbin.
In 1929 he graduated from the local Russian High School, after
which he worked casually until his departure to Shanghai in Janu-
ary, 1933. On 1-11-33 he joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C. in
which he is still serving.

Georgy Petrovich CHERNOFF, was born on January 18, 1913 at
Voronej, Russia. He is reported to have graduated from the Chi-
nese Eastern Railway Technical School in Harbin in 1930. In Au-
gust, 1932 he arrived in Shanghai from Harbin and from 14-9-32
has been serving in the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.

Both brothers are registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and with the Shanghai City Govern-
ment Police Bureau ( Reg. Nos 12601 and 13847, respectively ).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records against
either of the applicants.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

22/9.

F. A. to D. C (Sp. Br.)

由副督察普罗科菲耶夫（D.S.I. Prokofiev）撰写。由督察加斯柯因（C. Gascoigne D.I.）转呈。

亚历山大·彼得罗维奇·切尔诺夫（Alexander Petrovich CHERNOFF），俄国人，1911年3月14日出生于俄国喀山。据其自述，他于1924年与其弟 G.P. 切尔诺夫一同离开苏联前往中国，并在随后的11年间居住在哈尔滨。1929年，他从当地的俄罗斯高中毕业，此后从事临时工作，直至1933年1月前往上海。1933年11月1日，他加入上海义勇军（S.V.C.）俄罗斯团，目前仍在该团服役。

格奥尔基·彼得罗维奇·切尔诺夫（Georgy Petrovich CHERNOFF），1913年1月18日出生于俄国沃罗涅日。据报他于1930年毕业于哈尔滨中东铁路技术学校。1932年8月，他从哈尔滨抵达上海，并自1932年9月14日起在上海义勇军（S.V.C.）俄罗斯团服役。

兄弟二人均在莫尔缅路118/1号的俄罗斯移民委员会登记，并在上海市政府警察局登记（注册号分别为12601和13847）。

工部局警务处档案中没有任何针对这两位申请人的不良记录。

Subject A.G. Zenchenkoff and Mrs A.M. Leschinsky - applicants for certificates
of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. [签名，难以辨认] S.D.

I. Alexander Grigorievich ZENCHENKOFF, Russian, born on
April 11, 1893 at Krasnoyarsk, Siberia. He is reported to have ar-
rived in Shanghai from Vladivostok in 1921 together with his
wife, Mrs Anna Mihailovna Zenchenkoff, nee Leschinsky, born on
24-6-1896 at Vladivostok. Zenchenko claims to be a musician by
profession. However, it is well known that ever since their ar-
rival in Shanghai the Zenchenko couple have been conducting hou-
ses of ill fame at various addresses in Chapei and Settlement,
including 42(or 44) Haining Road (1921-1922), 54 Jukong Road
(1922-1928), 432 Dixwell Road (1928-1933), the "Eldorado Bar", 358-
360 Jukong Road ( 1933-1937). Since November, 1937 they have been
conducting a similar business at 16 Soochow Road. At present
they reside at apt. 732, Embankment Building, N-Soochow Road, to-
gether with their adopted son Adolf A. Zenchenkoff, born on 21-4-
1919 at Shanghai, who until September, 1938 attended the St. Fran-
cis Xavier's College.

2. Mrs Antonina Mihailovna LESCHINSKY, Russian, born on
4-6-1894 at Vladivostok. According to her own statement, she left
Russia for Manchuria in 1924 together with her husband, Mr. V.A.
Alexandroff, and resided in Harbin for several years, after which
she proceeded to Shanghai. Here she resided with her sister,
Mrs. A.M. Zenchenkoff, at 54 Jukong Road. Since 1929 she lived
separately from her husband and was formally divorced from him
in 1934 through the 1-st S.S.D. Court. From 1929 to 1934 she co-
habited with a certain Austrian named A.I. Bauer, formerly a musi-
cian in Shanghai, who at present is employed as a cashier with
the Algan branch of the Wostwag, a German Export & Import firm .
Since 1934 she has been residing with her sister and brother-in-
law whom she assists in their business.

一、亚历山大·格里戈里耶维奇·曾琴科夫（Alexander Grigorievich ZENCHENKOFF），俄国人，1893年4月11日出生于西伯利亚克拉斯诺亚尔斯克。据报他于1921年与其妻安娜·米哈伊洛夫娜·曾琴科夫夫人（Anna Mihailovna Zenchenkoff，婚前姓 Leschinsky，1896年6月24日出生于符拉迪沃斯托克）一同从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海。曾琴科声称其职业为音乐家。然而，众所周知，自抵达上海以来，曾琴科夫妇一直在闸北及租界内的多处地址经营妓院，包括海宁路42号（或44号）（1921-1922年）、巨鹿路54号（1922-1928年）、狄思威路432号（1928-1933年）、“埃尔多拉多酒吧”（Eldorado Bar），位于巨鹿路358-360号（1933-1937年）。自1937年11月以来，他们一直在苏州路16号经营类似业务。目前，他们与其养子阿道夫·A·曾琴科夫（Adolf A. Zenchenkoff，1919年4月21日出生于上海，直至1938年9月就读于圣方济各沙勿略学院）共同居住于北苏州路河滨大厦732号公寓。

2. 安东尼娜·米哈伊洛夫娜·列申斯基夫人（Mrs Antonina Mihailovna LESCHINSKY），俄国人，1894年6月4日出生于符拉迪沃斯托克。据其本人陈述，她于1924年与其丈夫 V.A. Alexandroff 先生一同离开俄国前往满洲，在哈尔滨居住数年后，随后前往上海。在此，她与其姐姐 A.M. 曾琴科夫夫人一同居住在巨鹿路54号。自1929年起，她与丈夫分居，并于1934年通过第一特区地方法院正式离婚。从1929年至1934年，她与一名名为 A.I. Bauer 的奥地利人同居，此人此前在上海担任音乐家，目前受雇于德国进出口商行 Wostwag 的阿尔根分行担任出纳。自1934年以来，她一直与其姐姐和姐夫同住，并协助他们经营业务。

SHANGHAI

Shanghai, September 16th, 1938.

Registered.

To the Commissioner of Police Force.
Shanghai Municipal Police.
185, Foochow Road.
Shanghai.

Sir,

May I apply to you on the following subject:-

One of my clients Mr. Alexander Grigorievitch Zenchenkoff, a Russian emigrant, residing at Shanghai, Embankment Building, Apt. No. 732, applied to me with the request to help him to get a permit to enter Australia where he intends to go together with his family consisting of his wife Anna Zenchenkoff, his son Adolf and a sister of his wife Mrs. Antonina M. Leschinsky. According to regulations now in force in order to get a permit it is necessary to file an application with the Australian Authorities and said application is to be supported by a certificate from local Police Office to the effect that neither applicant nor any member of his family who intends to proceed to Australia has ever been in prison or in mental hospital.

Therefore, I have the honour to request you to be so kind as to issue certificates to the above persons to the effect that there are no records against them in the Shanghai Municipal Police.-

I remain, Sir,

Yours respectfully,
N. A. Ivanow.

先生：

谨就以下事项向您提出申请：-

我的客户之一，亚历山大·格里戈里耶维奇·曾琴科夫先生，一位居住在上海河滨大厦732号公寓的俄国移民，向我提出请求，希望帮助他获得进入澳大利亚的许可，他打算与其家人一同前往，其家人包括其妻安娜·曾琴科夫、其子阿道夫以及其妻妹安东尼娜·M·列申斯基夫人。根据现行规定，为了获得许可，必须向澳大利亚当局提交申请，且该申请需附有当地警察局出具的证明，证明申请人及其任何打算前往澳大利亚的家庭成员从未入狱或住进精神病院。

因此，我荣幸地请求您惠予向上述人员出具证明，表明上海公共租界工部局警务处并无关于他们的不良记录。-

此致，

敬礼，
N. A. Ivanow。

CONFIDENTIAL REPORT
Date September 27, 9 38.

Subject (in full) Wilhelm SCHMIDT - application for certificate of character.

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford. A. I.

Wilhelm SCHMIDT, former Austrian, aged 40, has been a resident of Shanghai since April 1937 during which time he has not come to the notice of the police from a criminal or moral point of view. Since 1936, however, he has been connected in Shanghai, Tientsin and Mukden, with the Oriental Trading & Engineering Corporation, an American controlled concern which was strongly suspected of being a semi-official Soviet trading organisation in China and Manchuria.

Apart from this nothing is known to the detriment of the applicant.

D. S. Pitts
