REPORT
File No.__________
Date September 29, 1938

Subject M. A. Kougaevsky, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Gauda. 2. 9.

Nikolai Alexandrovich KOUGAEVSKY, Russian, born on Octo-
ber 17, 1899 at Yakootsk, Siberia. Former student of the Tomsk
Institute of Technology he is reported to have arrived in Shang-
hai from Vladivostok in 1922 and to have since been residing in
this city. From 1923 to June, 1927 he was employed with A.R. Bur-
kill & Sons as a manager of their Fibre Trunk Factory and from
1927 to 1930 -with the China Handkerchief & Hemming Co., Footung,
as a foreign supervisor. His next employment was in the capaci-
ty of a clerk of works with the Imperial Chemical Industries
(China) from February to October, 1931 , and from December, 1931 he
has been employed with the China General Omnibus Co, as a foreman
i/c the night shift ( Bodybuilding Department). He possesses
good testimonials from his previous employers.

Kougaevsky is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Soulmein Road, and resides at 275 Route Tenant
de la Tour together with his wife, Mrs Alexandra Ivanovna Kou-
gaevsky nee Kosloff, born 26-5-1908 at Miass, Orenbourg Province,
Russia, and their children Alexis and Ludmila, aged 8 and 5 years,
respectively. Mrs Kougaevsky is the sister-in-law of Mr. G.E.
Radionoff, formerly a Sub-Inspector in the Shanghai Municipal Po-
lice, who is in Australia at present.

Mr. and Mrs Kougaevsky hold certificates of good charac-
ter issued by the French Police on 28-9-38 ( Nos. 122 and 123,
respectively).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records concern-
ing these persons.

（批：D.R. 29/9.）

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

D. C. ( Special Branch)

尼古拉·亚历山德罗维奇·库加耶夫斯基（Nikolai Alexandrovich KOUGAEVSKY），俄国人，1899年10月17日出生于西伯利亚雅库茨克。据报他曾是托木斯克理工学院的学生，于1922年从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海，并自此居住在该市。1923年至1927年6月，他受雇于 A.R. Burkill & Sons 公司，担任其纤维板箱厂经理；1927年至1930年，受雇于浦东的中国手帕与锁边公司（China Handkerchief & Hemming Co.），担任外籍监工。他的下一份工作是在1931年2月至10月期间，担任帝国化学工业（中国）公司（Imperial Chemical Industries (China)）的工程职员；自1931年12月起，他受雇于中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Co.），担任夜班领班（车身制造部）。他拥有前任雇主出具的良好推荐信。

库加耶夫斯基在苏尔美因路118号的俄国侨民委员会注册，并与妻子亚历山德拉·伊万诺芙娜·库加耶夫斯卡娅夫人（Alexandra Ivanovna Kougaevsky，婚前姓 Kosloff，1908年5月26日出生于俄国奥伦堡省米亚斯）及其子女阿列克谢（8岁）和柳德米拉（5岁）共同居住在唐乃安路275号。库加耶夫斯卡娅夫人是 G.E. Radionoff 先生的妻妹，Radionoff 先生曾任上海公共租界工部局警务处副巡官，目前在澳大利亚。

库加耶夫斯基夫妇持有法国警察于1938年9月28日签发的品行良好证明书（编号分别为122和123）。

工部局警务处记录中关于这些人员没有任何不良记载。

（批：D.R. 9月29日。）

A. Prokofiev
副督察

助理处长（特务科）

Subject U.S. Gertsenstein, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev.    Forwarded by C. Crawford. S.J.

Ury Solomonovich GERTSENSTEIN, Russian of Jewish origin, born on February 17, 1907 at Herson, South Russia. According to his own statement, he left Russia for Manchuria in 1915 and for the following 8 years resided in Harbin where he graduated from the 1st Public School in 1923.

He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in 1923. Here he is reported to have been employed with the P.A.T. Motion Picture Studio, Hankao Road, from 1923 to 1925, after which he joined Zais, Steinman & Co., 110 Szechuen Road, as an office clerk. In 1933, in partnership with another Russian of Jewish extraction named K. Pomus, he established his own business known as the North China Import Co., importers of Piece Goods, 320 Szechuen Road. In May, 1938 he severed his connections with this firm, after which he has been working as Manufacturers' representative in connection with A.G. Macpherson, a London firm.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and with the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau ( Reg. No. 3011) and at present resides at 86 Rue Llasenet, together with his wife, Mrs Frida Iosifovna Gertsenstein nee Polonetsky, born 30-5-1910 at Vilna, Russia, and their daughter Rosa, 7 years of age.

Mr. and Mrs Gertsenstein hold certificates of good character issued by the French Police on 28-9-38 ( Nos 126 and 125, respectively).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records concerning these persons.

Ury Solomonovich GERTSENSTEIN，俄籍犹太人，1907年2月17日出生于俄罗斯南部赫尔松。据其自述，他于1915年离开俄罗斯前往满洲，并在随后的8年里居住在哈尔滨，于1923年毕业于第一公立学校。

他于1923年从哈尔滨抵达上海。据报道，他于1923年至1925年间受雇于汉口路的 P.A.T. 电影制片厂，之后加入四川北路110号的 Zais, Steinman & Co. 公司担任办公室职员。1933年，他与另一位名为 K. Pomus 的俄籍犹太人合伙，创立了自己的企业，即华北进口公司（North China Import Co.），经营匹头进口业务，地址为四川北路320号。1938年5月，他断绝了与该公司的联系，此后一直作为伦敦 A.G. Macpherson 公司的厂商代表工作。

他在莫尔尼路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会以及上海市政府警察局（注册号 3011）登记，目前与妻子 Frida Iosifovna Gertsenstein（婚前姓 Polonetsky，1910年5月30日出生于俄罗斯维尔纳）及7岁的女儿 Rosa 居住在马思南路86号（原文 Llasenet 疑为 Massenet 之误）。

Subject M.D. Yastreboff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Garsia. D.I.

Mihail Dimitrievich YASTREBOFF, Russian, born on April 19,
1911 at Harbin. Son of a former employee of the Chinese Eastern
Railway, he is reported to have graduated from the Harbin Poly-
technic Institute ( Electro-Mechanical Department) in October,
1933. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in March, 1934. Here he
was employed with the Radio Protection Co., 337 Avenue Haig, from
1-4-34 to 1-4-35 when the company was closed, after which he was
without a fixed employment for a period. In June, 1936 he joined
the General Electric Company and is still employed at their engi-
neering works, 285 Hochien Road.

While in Harbin, Yastreboff became a naturalized Chinese
citizen in 1927. However, in 1938 he applied to the Russian Emi-
grants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, for registration as a Rus-
sian emigrant and at present holds passport No 1288 issued on
29-7-38 by the Police Bureau of the Shanghai Municipal Administra-
tion Office ( Reg. No. 1804 ).

He resides at 57 Rue Paul Henry together with his wife, Mrs.
Nathalie Nikolaevna Yastreboff nee Nikitin, born on 4-2-1905 at
Petrograd. Mrs Yastreboff is reported to have been residing in
Shanghai for the past seven years, during which period she has
been working as a ballet dancer under stage names Makovsky and
Lolita Manon.

Mr.&Mrs Yastreboff hold certificates of good character is-
sued by the French Police in September, 1938 ( Nos 124 and 117,
respectively).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records concerning
these persons.

Mihail Dimitrievich YASTREBOFF，俄国人，1911年4月19日出生于哈尔滨。他是前中东铁路员工的儿子，据报道于1933年10月毕业于哈尔滨工业大学（机电系）。他于1934年3月从哈尔滨抵达上海。在此，他于1934年4月1日至1935年4月1日期间受雇于海格路337号的无线电保护公司（Radio Protection Co.），该公司关闭后，他曾有一段时间没有固定工作。1936年6月，他加入通用电气公司，目前仍受雇于其在霍肯路285号的工程车间。

Yastreboff 在哈尔滨期间，于1927年归化为中国公民。然而，1938年他向莫尔尼路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会申请注册为俄国侨民，目前持有上海市政厅警察局于1938年7月29日签发的第1288号护照（注册号 1804）。

他与妻子 Nathalie Nikolaevna Yastreboff（婚前姓 Nikitin，1905年2月4日出生于彼得格勒）居住在保罗亨利路57号。据报道，Yastreboff 夫人在过去七年里一直居住在上海，在此期间，她以 Makovsky 和 Lolita Manon 为艺名从事芭蕾舞演员工作。

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

Leonid Zarnovsky, Polish citizen of Karaim-Jewish
origin, born on 22.3.1903 at Troki, Vilno District, Poland.
He is reported to have arrived in China from Esthonia via
the U.S.S.R. in March, 1931. According to his own state-
ment he was employed in the "MARS" Sweet, Chocolate and
Biscuit Factory in that city as a candy maker from October 27,
1931 to October 26, 1933, after which he left for Shanghai.
Here he has been employed in the same capacity with the
Bakerite Company, 1134 Sinza Road, from November, 1933.
Applicant holds passport No. 20/36 issued by the
Polish Consulate-General on 12.2.36, valid until 11.2.39.
His wife, Mrs. Zinaida Zarnovsky nee Lavrinovich, born on
25.7.1909 at Troki, Vilno District, holds passport 63/37,
valid for three years, issued by the same Consulate on
16.4.37. She is reported to have been residing in Shanghai
for about five years.
Mr. and Mrs. Zarnovsky hold certificate of character
No. 2554/A issued by the French Police on 29.9.38.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
concerning these persons.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

P. A. to D. C.

REPORT
Date October 2, 1938

Subject O. L. Ivanoff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Gascoigne. D. I.

Oleg Leonidovich IVANOFF, naturalized Chinese citizen
of Russian origin, born on February 2, 1907 at Irkutsk, Siberia.
Son of an employee of the Chinese Eastern Railway he is reported
to have been residing in Manchuria from 1921 to 1933. In 1932
he graduated from the Harbin Polytechnic Institute with a civil
engineer's degree.

He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in September, 1933.
Here he was employed with the China United Engineering Corpora-
tion, 209 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, from 20-10-33 to 1-5-37 during
which period he worked mostly at various construction works in
Nanchang and Hangchow. He holds a good testimonial from the cor-
poration. From 1-5-37 he has been employed with the General
Electric Co., 27 Ningpo Road.

Ivanoff holds naturalization certificate No 12136 is-
sued on October 1, 1927 by the Ministry of Interior. Upon arrival
in Shanghai he also registered with the Russian Emigrants Com-
mittee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

The applicant at present resides at 125 Avenue du Roi
Albert, House 33. On 29-9-38 he obtained from the French Police
a certificate of good character ( No. 2555/A )

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records con-
cerning this individual.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

D.B.R.
3/10.

D. C. ( Special Branch ).

P. A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.)

由副督察普罗科菲耶夫（Prokofiev）呈报。经 Gascoigne 督察转发。

Oleg Leonidovich IVANOFF，俄裔归化中国公民，1907年2月2日出生于西伯利亚伊尔库茨克。据报其为中东铁路雇员之子，1921年至1933年间居住于满洲。1932年毕业于哈尔滨工业大学，获土木工程学位。

他于1933年9月从哈尔滨抵达上海。在此期间，他受雇于圆明园路209号的中国联合工程公司（China United Engineering Corporation），任期从1933年10月20日至1937年5月1日，期间主要在南昌和杭州的各项建筑工程中工作。他持有该公司出具的优良推荐信。自1937年5月1日起，他受雇于宁波路27号的通用电气公司（General Electric Co.）。

Ivanoff 持有内政部于1927年10月1日签发的第12136号归化证书。抵达上海后，他也在莫利哀路（Moulmein Road）118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记。

申请人目前居住于阿尔伯特王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）125号33室。他于1938年9月29日从法国警察机关获得品行良好证明书（第2555/A号）。

工部局警务处档案中无关于此人的记录。

ged by the Shanghai Municipal Orchestra. He left this position

sian Public Organization (SORO), 8 Avenue Dubail, and with the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau and at present resides
at 19 Rue Paul Henry together with his wife, Mrs V.B. Shevtzoff,
born 22-10-1899 at Irkutsk and their daughter, Miss Nina I. Shev-
tzoff, born On 3-7-1918 at Irkutsk.

They hold certificates of good character issued by the
French Police on August 19, 1938 ( Nos. 82, 81 and 80, respecti-
vely).

ing these individuals.

Subject D. B. RABINOVICH - applicant for Certificate of Character.

Made by D. S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. S.

David B. RABINOVICH ( or RABINOVITCH ), Russian of
Jewish extraction, has been a resident of Shanghai from
1921, since when he has not been convicted of any criminal
charge or committed to any mental institution. The same
remarks apply to his wife and three daughters.

The applicant, however, first came to the notice of
the Municipal Police in July 1924 when he became joint
editor of "New Shanghai Life," a Soviet publication which
was closed down on the orders of the Mixed Court at the
end of 1926. In September 1924, Rabinovich's name was
included in a list of persons who were at that time known
to have been engaged in propagating Bolshevism in Shanghai.
Since 1930, when he was unconfirmedly reported to have
been active in local communistic affairs, he has not come
to the notice of this office.

D. S. Pitts
D. S.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. 374/14 Date 7/10/38）
Date October 6, 1938

Subject Miss S.D. Rebena ( Rybina ), applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. I.

Miss Seraphima Dimitrievna REBENA ( or Rybina),
Russian, born on July 8, 1902, at Vladimir, Russia. According to
her own statement, she arrived in Tientsin from Russia in 1919
and resided in that city for the following four or five years,
after which she proceeded to Shanghai. Here she is reported to
have been working as a dancing partner for a period. In 1930
she worked in the "Iris" Dressmaking Shop, Route Cardinal Mer-
cier, as an apprentice. In 1935-1936 she was a partner in a si-
milar enterprise known as the "Muguette" Dressmaking Shop, 227
Route Cardinal Mercier, and in 1937 conducted the "Chanel"
Hat & Dress Making Shop in Avenue Petain. At present she is un-
employed. She claims to have certain independent means. It is
rumoured, however, that for the past several years she has been
supported by a male friend.

Miss Rebena is registered with the Council of United
Russian Organization, (SORO ), 8 Avenue Dubail, and with the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau ( Reg. 3172). On Sep-
tember 9, 1938 she obtained from the French Police a certificate
of good character ( No.113 ).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
concerning this person.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

（手写批注：23/2. 6/10.）

D. C. ( Special Branch ).

事由：S.D. Rebena ( Rybina ) 小姐，品行证明书申请人。

由副督察普罗科菲耶夫呈报。经 Crawford 警督转发。

Seraphima Dimitrievna REBENA（或 Rybina）小姐，俄国人，1902年7月8日生于俄国弗拉基米尔。据其自述，她于1919年从俄国抵达天津，在该市居住了四五年，随后前往上海。据报她在此曾做过一段时间的舞伴。1930年，她在麦神父路（Route Cardinal Mercier）的“Iris”服装店做学徒。1935-1936年，她是位于麦神父路227号的类似企业“Muguette”服装店的合伙人，1937年在贝当路经营“Chanel”帽饰及服装店。目前她失业。她声称有一定的独立经济来源。然而，有谣言称过去几年她一直由一位男性朋友供养。

Rebena 小姐已在联合俄国组织委员会（SORO，地址：杜拜尔路8号）以及上海市政府警察局登记（注册号3172）。1938年9月9日，她从法国警察机关获得了一份品行良好证明书（编号113）。

工部局警务处档案中无关于此人的记录。

A. Prokofiev

pages.en:
30th September, 1938

George Enoch Sistonan (spelt in Finnish - Sistonen)

I am 44 years of age, Christian and married (no children); I
am Finnish by nationality (father) and former Russian subject.

Save for the occasional business trips to Nanking, Hangchow
and up the Yangtzse river, the usual short Summer leaves spent in Tsingtao,
Kuling etc., or in Japan, and an absence from Shanghai of a few months'
duration in 1934/1935, while on furlough in Europe, I (we) have been
residing permanently in Shanghai since 1923 - i.e. for 16 years. We
came here from Vladivostock (Siberia) after that city had been occupied
by the forces of the Soviet.

Very shortly upon arriving here I obtained a temporary
position with Messrs. Hall & Holtz, Ltd; then, with Messrs. Moutrie &
Co., Ltd. From the 1st December, 1923 and till the 1st February, 1936
(i.e. for over 12 years) I was connected with The Office Appliance Co.,
Nanking Road - dealing in all kinds of machines and equipment for
offices, shops, etc. From the 1st February, 1936 and till the 1st July,
1937 I was associated with Messrs. Scharpf, Guenter & Co., then in
Canton Road, and on the 1st July, 1937 I joined the firm of Reiss,
Bradley & Co., Ltd., 88 Museum Road. At present I am on the staff
of this firm taking charge of the Accounting machines & Typewriter Dept.

As to my social and other activities, I may say that outside
of having been interested in sports, Volunteering and similar harmless
pastimes , I have not taken part in any other activities here, political
or otherwise. I feel certain that I am not expected in this curriculum
to expound my political credo, etc. Suffice it to say that by birth,
education and my former associations I could be classed as conservative,
belonging to the old school of thought, etc. However - so much for that.
Some time ago (when not so old yet ) I was actively interested in local
sports and for several years played Football (old "Engineers' Club; Sh'ai
Football Club; International Cup matches, etc.), rowed (Henli; Interport
regatta at Kobe, etc.) and ran (Harriers; Sh'ai Amateur Athletic Club
under Inspector McKenna, SMP ). In conclusion I may add that I am a proud
holder of the Long Service Medal of the Shanghai Volunteer Corps, for
12 years of Efficient Service, and of the last 1937 Emergency Medal of SMC.

Should you require any additional information I would be pleased
to give you same. For obvious reasons I would prefer, of course, that you
apply at my residence rather than at the office of my firm - so as not
to jeopardize my position or reputation. My present address and telephone
are given hereunder.

George E. Sistonan.
651, Wei Hai Wei Road
Apt. D01; Telephone 36201
Usually at home before 8.30 in the morning and after 6 o'clock in the eve.
pages.zh:
1938年9月30日

George Enoch Sistonan（芬兰语拼写为 Sistonen）

我现年44岁，基督徒，已婚（无子女）；国籍为芬兰（父系），前俄罗斯帝国臣民。

除了偶尔去南京、杭州及长江上游出差，通常在青岛、牯岭等地或日本度过短暂的暑假，以及1934/1935年间在欧洲休假离开上海数月外，我（们）自1923年以来一直定居上海——即已16年。我们在该城被苏维埃军队占领后从符拉迪沃斯托克（西伯利亚）来到此处。

抵达此处后不久，我即在 Hall & Holtz, Ltd. 公司获得一个临时职位；随后在 Moutrie & Co., Ltd. 公司任职。从1923年12月1日至1936年2月1日（即超过12年），我就职于南京路的 The Office Appliance Co.，经营各类办公室、商店等用的机器和设备。从1936年2月1日至1937年7月1日，我与位于广东路的 Scharpf, Guenter & Co. 公司有合作关系，并于1937年7月1日加入位于博物馆路88号的 Reiss, Bradley & Co., Ltd. 公司。目前我是该公司职员，负责会计机器和打字机部门。

至于我的社交和其他活动，可以说除了对体育、志愿服务及类似的无害消遣感兴趣外，我没有参与这里的任何其他活动，无论是政治性的还是其他性质的。我相信在此履历中无需阐述我的政治信条等。 suffice it to say（ suffice it to say 意为“ suffice it to say”），出于出身、教育和以往的联系，我可以被归类为保守派，属于旧式思想流派等。然而——就此打住。不久前（当时还没这么老）我曾积极参与本地体育活动，踢了几年足球（老“工程师俱乐部”；Sh'ai 足球俱乐部；国际杯比赛等），划船（Henli；神户港际赛船会等），以及跑步（Harriers；在工部局警务处 McKenna 巡官领导下的 Sh'ai 业余田径俱乐部）。最后补充一点，我是上海万国商团长期服务奖章的自豪持有者，表彰12年的高效服务，以及1937年工部局紧急状态奖章。

如需更多信息，我很乐意提供。出于显而易见的原因，我当然希望您到我的住所而非我公司办公室查询——以免危及我的职位或声誉。我目前的地址和电话如下。

George E. Sistonan.
威海卫路651号
D01室；电话 36201
通常早上8:30之前和晚上6点之后在家。

Subject M. T. Mironoff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Gasford. D.S.

Mihail Terentievich MIRONOFF, Soviet citizen, born on
September 21, 1884 in Viatka Province, Russia. A graduate of the
Imperial Technical School in Moscow ( 1910), he is reported to
have arrived in Harbin from the U.S.S.R. in 1925 to serve with
the Chinese Eastern Railway. He left this service in March, 1935
when that concern was taken over by the Japanese. In September,
1936 he arrived in Shanghai. Here he is reported to have been
working independently as a specialist in installation of "dust
eliminators".

He holds passport No 128980/760521 issued on 20-9-27
at Vladivostok, which was renewed in Shanghai on 3-12-37.

Applicant's wife, Mrs Vera Georgievna Mironoff, 50, also
a Soviet citizen, holds passport No 19824/436340 issued on
18-4-1924 at Vladivostok. She arrived in Shanghai from Harbin
together with her husband and, being a qualified dental surgeon,
has since been practising dentistry with an office at 479 Route
Cardinal Mercier.

They have two sons of whom one, Valentin M. Mironoff,
is reported to have graduated from a polytechnic institute in
Belgium in 1933 and to be in Hongkong at present, and the other,
George Mironoff, 26, a graduate of the University of Liege (1935)
has been employed with the French Municipal Police in Shanghai
for the past two years.

The Mironoff family reside at 479 Route Cardinal Mer-
cier. While in Shanghai they did not come to the notice of the
Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an unde-
sirable character.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

Mihail Terentievich MIRONOFF，苏联公民，1884年9月21日出生于俄罗斯维亚特卡省。他是莫斯科帝国技术学校（1910年）的毕业生，据报于1925年从苏联抵达哈尔滨，在中东铁路服役。1935年3月，当该企业被日本人接管时，他离开了该职务。1936年9月他抵达上海。据报在此地他作为“除尘器”安装专家独立工作。

他持有1927年9月20日在符拉迪沃斯托克签发的第128980/760521号护照，该护照于1937年12月3日在上海续期。

申请人的妻子 Vera Georgievna Mironoff 夫人，50岁，也是苏联公民，持有1924年4月18日在符拉迪沃斯托克签发的第19824/436340号护照。她与丈夫一同从哈尔滨抵达上海，作为一名合格的牙科医生，此后一直在麦神父路479号的诊所从事牙科诊疗工作。

他们有两个儿子，其中一人 Valentin M. Mironoff，据报于1933年毕业于比利时的一所理工学院，目前在香港；另一人 George Mironoff，26岁，列日大学（1935年）毕业生，过去两年受雇于上海法租界警务处。

Mironoff 一家居住在麦神父路479号。在上海期间，他们未因任何不良性质的活动引起工部局警务处的注意。

A. Prokofiev

Subject M.D. Gleboff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

Mihail Dimitrievich GLEBOFF, Russian, born on November 2, 1886 in Smolensk Province, Russia. An agricultural engineer by profession he is reported to have arrived in Harbin from Russia in 1920 together with his family and subsequently was employed with the Chinese Eastern Railway from 1923 to March, 1935, when that concern was taken over by the Japanese. In September, 1937 he arrived in Shanghai from Harbin and has since been residing in this city without a fixed employment.

While in Harbin he became a Soviet citizen in 1925 and at present holds passport No 010830 issued on 30-10-35 by the Soviet Consulate-General at Harbin valid until 22-3-39.

Applicant's wife, Mrs Ludmila Ivanovna Gleboff, 43, and their son and daughter, aged 17 and 12 years, respectively, are registered with the French Police as Russian emigrants ( Reg.Nos 794 and 795 ). The son, Evgeny Gleboff, is reported to be a student of the St. John's University.

In connection with his intention to proceed to Australia Gleboff applied to the French Police recently for a certificate of character. He was told that a letter from the local Soviet authorities was required to the effect that they had no objection to his departure to Australia. The applicant stated that it would hardly be possible to obtain such letter.

While in Shanghai Gleboff did not come to the notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an undesirable nature.

[签名]
A. Prokofiev

米哈伊尔·德米特里耶维奇·格列博夫，俄国人，1886年11月2日出生于俄罗斯斯摩棱斯克省。职业为农业工程师，据报他于1920年与家人一起从俄罗斯抵达哈尔滨，随后于1923年至1935年3月受雇于中东铁路公司，直至该公司被日本人接管。1937年9月，他从哈尔滨抵达上海，此后一直居住在本市，无固定职业。

他在哈尔滨期间，于1925年成为苏联公民，目前持有苏联驻哈尔滨总领事馆于1935年10月30日签发的第010830号护照，有效期至1939年3月22日。

申请人的妻子，43岁的柳德米拉·伊万诺芙娜·格列博娃夫人，以及他们分别为17岁和12岁的儿子和女儿，已在法国巡捕房登记为俄国侨民（登记号794和795）。据报，儿子叶夫根尼·格列博夫是圣约翰大学的学生。

鉴于其打算前往澳大利亚，格列博夫最近向法国巡捕房申请品行证明书。他被告知，需要当地苏联当局出具一封不反对他前往澳大利亚的信函。申请人表示，几乎不可能获得此类信函。

格列博夫在上海期间，未因任何不良活动引起工部局警务处的注意。

Subject E.M. Dorfman, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by Wogan A.P.I.

Mihail Efraimovich DORFMAN, Russian of Jewish extraction, born on October 25, 1891, in Vilno Province, Russia. According to his own statement, he left the U.S.S.R. for Manchuria in 1926 and for the following five years resided in Harbin where he was engaged in commercial activities on a small scale. He arrived in Shanghai in 1930. Here he is reported to have been working independently as a salesman on a commission basis. Among other things he has been selling various fashion magazines etc. The "Fashion Books", 732 Avenue Joffre, which he gives as his business address was visited in connection with the present enquiries. It is just a corner which he rents in a small Chinese shop situated at the above address, and at present Mr. Dorfman's entire property there consists of several boxes of soap.

Applicant resides at 833 Avenue Joffre, House 19, Room 12 ( Linda Terrace ) together with his common-law wife, a certain Mrs A.I. Jack, Russian Jewess, a divorcee, who claims to be practising manicure and pedicure.

Dorfman is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records concerning this individual.

It appears that Mr. Dorfman called at the Australian Trade Commissioner's Office in order to obtain information and that he does not possess the necessary funds.

米哈伊尔·叶夫赖莫维奇·多尔夫曼，犹太裔俄国人，1891年10月25日出生于俄罗斯维尔诺省。据其自称，他于1926年离开苏联前往满洲，并在随后的五年里居住在哈尔滨，从事小规模商业活动。他于1930年抵达上海。据报，他在此独立工作，担任佣金制推销员。除其他物品外，他还销售各种时尚杂志等。作为其营业地址提供的“时尚书籍”（Fashion Books），位于霞飞路732号，已就本次调查进行了走访。那只是他在上述地址的一家中国小店里租的一个角落，目前多尔夫曼先生在那里的全部财产仅为几箱肥皂。

申请人与其事实婚姻妻子A.I. 杰克夫人同住于霞飞路833号，林达台（Linda Terrace）19号12室。杰克夫人是俄籍犹太女子，离异，自称从事修甲和修脚业务。

多尔夫曼已在穆勒路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记。

工部局警务处档案中关于此人没有任何记录。

看来多尔夫曼先生曾前往澳大利亚商务专员办公室获取信息，且他并不具备必要的资金。

Grigory Vladimirovich LVOFF, Russian, was born on January
7, 1908, at Moscow. He is reported to have left Russia for
China in 1920 and to have subsequently resided in Harbin, where
upon completing his education in a local school, he worked as
a salesman with Shriro Bros., Import & Export Co. Towards the
end of 1929 he resigned from this firm and was for a period employed
as a clerk with the Harbin branch of the National City Bank of
New York. In 1928, shortly after he had left this position,
he and two other employees of the same bank (Choolkoff and
Melgunoff) were implicated in defrauding the bank in question
by drawing out money on false cheques, for which offence Lvoff
was sentenced to 1 year imprisonment.

In August, 1930 he came to Shanghai and soon afterwards
secured employment with the Shanghai Telephone Co. His services
with the company terminated in December, 1931 due to his bank
affairs in Harbin reaching the ears of the management.

His next employment was in the Advertising Department of
Russian newspaper "Slovo", 238 Avenue du Roi Albert, where he
worked until September, 1932 when he left on his own accord.

In 1933-1934 he worked at various places as a tailor and
ladies hair-dresser apprentice, respectively. In 1935-1936
he conducted the Shanghai-Tsingtao Line, a travel agency which
was located at No. 538 Avenue Joffre. This agency worked in
conjunction with Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd., whose four
freighters were converted into passenger boats with the general
idea of conveying Russians on low tariff during the summer season.
During the same period he also claims to have been engaged in
commercial pursuits importing silk materials in Shanghai. In

格里戈里·弗拉基米罗维奇·利沃夫（Grigory Vladimirovich LVOFF），俄国人，1908年1月7日出生于莫斯科。据报他于1920年离开俄国前往中国，随后居住在哈尔滨，在当地学校完成学业后，他在 Shriro Bros. 进出口公司担任推销员。1929年底，他从该公司辞职，并在一段时间内受雇于纽约国家城市银行（National City Bank of New York）哈尔滨分行，担任职员。1928年，在他离开该职位后不久，他与同一家银行的两名其他雇员（Choolkoff 和 Melgunoff）被牵连进一起通过开具空头支票诈骗银行的案件，利沃夫因此罪行被判处一年监禁。

1930年8月，他来到上海，并很快在上海电话公司找到工作。由于他在哈尔滨的银行事务传到了管理层的耳中，他于1931年12月终止了在该公司的服务。

他的下一份工作是在阿尔伯特王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）238号的俄文报纸《言论报》（Slovo）广告部，他在那里工作直到1932年9月自行离职。

1933-1934年间，他先后在多处分别担任裁缝和女士美发师学徒。1935-1936年间，他经营“上海-青岛线”旅行社，该社位于霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）538号。该机构与怡和洋行有限公司（Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd.）合作运营，怡和的四艘货轮被改装为客船，总体构想是在夏季以低费率运送俄国人。在此期间，他还声称在上海从事进口丝绸材料的商业活动。在

1937 he made a couple of trips to Canton, allegedly on commercial business. From February, 1937 to September, 1937 he worked as a salesman on a commission basis for Messrs. In 1937-1938 he came under suspicion of the Narcotic Section, S.M.P. of being engaged in narcotic smuggling operations in association with a local Persian firm whose activities in connection with drug smuggling are well known.

Lvoff resides at 9 Route de Grouchy, Apt. 5.

Subject V.P. Kuznetsoff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by （签名）

Vladimir Petrovich KUZNETSOV, Russian, was born on Ju-
ly 9, 1909 in Simbirsk Province, Russia. According to his own
statement, he came to Harbin from the U.S.S.R. in 1931 and short-
ly afterwards proceeded to Shanghai, arriving in this city in
July of the same year. Here he was employed at "Volta" Electric
Company, 654 Avenue Joffre, for about one year, after which he has
been working independently as an electrical mechanic and at pre-
sent has a small workshop at 215 Route des Soeurs. Some time ago
he was a partner in a barber shop situated at the same address.
For the past several months he also has been operating a few motor
trucks in company with another Russian named S.I. Poroshin. It
is reported that during this period there has been a marked
change for the better in his material circumstances. Apparently,
he is one of those who have profited of the business in connec-
tion with transportation of goods from the Japanese occupied area
of Shanghai.

He resides at the above address together with his wife,
Mrs Tamara Vassilievna Kuznetsov nee Kalkey, 29, and their daugh-
ter Margaret, aged 6 years. Mrs. Kuznetsov is at present employed
with Aureole Beauty Parlour, 936 Bubbling Well Road, as a ladies'
hair-dresser.

Applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Com-
mittee, 118/1 Moulmein Road ( Reg. No 1610 ). On 29-12-37 he ob-
tained from the French Police a certificate of good character
(No. 3393/A ).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records con-
cerning this individual.

（批：C 13/10.）

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

D. C. ( Special Branch )

Subject V.P. Kosmenko, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by W. Logan A.S.I.

Victor Fanteleimonovich KOSMENKO, Russian, born on December 23, 1913 at Onuchina, Maritime Province, Russia. He is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok in 1920 together with his parents. In 1929 he graduated from the Thomas Hanbury School and for the following five years studied in the Aurora University ( electro-mechanical faculty). Upon graduating from the university in 1935 he was employed with Moller's Engineering Works, 259 Conservancy Road, for about three months. Leaving this position owing to a reduction in staff, he worked in the Installation Department of the Shanghai Telephone Co., from September, 1937 to April, 1938, when he joined the Shanghai Power Company as an apprentice engineer. He is still working in this capacity.

His father, Mr. P. Kosmenko, was formerly employed as a mechanic on board the various vessels of the Russian Mercantile Fleet. Later he served in the same capacity with the China Merchants Steam Navigation Co., in Shanghai and since 1931 has been employed with the Shanghai Telephone Company.

The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and at present resides at 57 Route Pichon together with his parents.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records concerning the applicant.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

（批：C. 13/10）

D. C. ( Special Branch )

Subject M.V. Maslow , applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by [Signature] A.S.P.

Mihail Vladimirovich MASLOW, Russian, was born on December 25, 1896 at Moscow. Former student of the Imperial Technical Institute at Moscow ( Chemical Engineering Department ), he is reported to have seen active service during the Great War in 1915-1918 and later to have served in Admiral Kolchak's White Army in Siberia for a period.

He first came to Shanghai from Vladivostok in February, 1919 and soon afterwards secured employment at the Liulin Estate at Kuling as a custodian, in which capacity he worked until the end of 1919.

In 1920 he left for the Philippine Islands, where he worked as a chemist with the New Life Bazaar, Import Company, up to 1921, when he resigned from his position and proceeded to Harbin. For the following two years he worked in the "Niva" Printing & Publishing Co., as manager of the printing department and also in the "Russian Daily News", a Russian newspaper published in English.

Returning to Shanghai in 1923, he worked casually until 1925, when in company with a Mr. Cooper he established the Cooper & Co., Distillery & Perfumery Works, 301 Avenue Joffre. This establishment closed down in 1927 owing to poor business.

In 1929 Maslow again proceeded to the Philippine Islands where at Manapla, Negros, he joined a Sugar Refinery Factory as a chemist. After about six months stay in that place he returned to Shanghai. In 1930 -1933 he conducted the St. George's Pharmacy at No. 1559 Bubbling Well Road. Selling out the business he went to Tsingtao where until the end of 1935 he was a shareholder and manager of the Tsingtao United Industrial & Trading Co.,

由警探长 Prokofiev 制作。由 [签名] A.S.P. 转呈

Mihail Vladimirovich MASLOW，俄国人，1896年12月25日出生于莫斯科。据报他曾是莫斯科帝国技术学院（化学工程系）的学生，在1915-1918年大战期间服过现役，后来在西伯利亚的 Kolchak 海军上将白军中服役一段时间。

他于1919年2月首次从海参崴来到上海，不久后在牯岭 Liulin 地产公司谋得看守一职，并在此职位上工作至1919年底。

1920年他前往菲律宾群岛，在那里作为化学师受雇于 New Life Bazaar, Import Company，直至1921年辞职前往哈尔滨。在接下来的两年里，他在“Niva”印刷出版公司担任印刷部经理，并在一家以英文出版的俄文报纸《Russian Daily News》工作。

1923年回到上海后，他打零工直到1925年，当时他与一位 Cooper 先生合作建立了 Cooper & Co., Distillery & Perfumery Works（酿酒与香水厂），地址霞飞路301号。该机构因生意不佳于1927年关闭。

1929年 Maslow 再次前往菲律宾群岛，在内格罗斯岛 Manapla 加入一家糖精炼厂担任化学师。在该地停留约六个月后，他返回上海。1930-1933年间，他经营位于静安寺路1559号的圣乔治药房。卖出业务后，他前往青岛，直到1935年底，他是青岛联合工贸公司的股东兼经理，

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff    Forwarded by [签名]

Iosif Grigorievitch PATENT, Russian Jew, was born in
Irkutsk, Siberia on October 22, 1911. He arrived in Harbin
from the U.S.S.R. together with his father in 1924. In
Harbin his father, a tailor by occupation, was employed with
Bent Brothers (Furriers, Woollen Merchants & Outfitters)
until 1932, after which he was employed in Shanghai first
with U.J. Soskin, No.1141 Bubbling Well Road, and later with
the Shanghai Branch of Bent Brothers and Co. The last named
firm, the owner of which Y.M. Bent, was formerly a contractor
of the Red Army, was known to be financed by the Moscow
Narodny Bank.

The applicant was educated in a commercial school in
Harbin. In 1929 he left for Hongkong where for 8 months he
attended the St. Joseph's College. Upon returning to Harbin
he was employed as a clerk with Netherlands Insurance Co.
He left this firm on his own accord some time towards the end
of 1932 and proceeded to Shanghai. Here he was employed as a
cashier with the "Cosmos" Provision Store, Avenue Joffre,
owned by R.B. Bitker of the American Asiatic Trading Co.,
No.320 Szechuen Road. Upon the liquidation of the "Cosmos"
Store in 1934, he joined the R.C.A. Victor Co. of China, No356,
Peking Road, his present place of employment. The applicant
has been a member of the S.M.P. (Specials) since January 1937.

He is registered with the Public Safety Bureau as a
Russian Emigrant. Mabel PATENT, nee ISAAC, Arabian Jewess,
was born in Hilla, Iraq, on February 21, 1917. She left Iraq
for Hongkong together with her mother in 1920 and in 1923

由副总巡 Pavloff 制作    由 [签名] 转呈

Iosif Grigorievitch PATENT，俄国犹太人，1911年10月22日出生于西伯利亚伊尔库茨克。1924年他与父亲一起从苏联抵达哈尔滨。在哈尔滨，他的父亲是一名裁缝，受雇于 Bent Brothers（皮货商、羊毛商及服饰商），直至1932年，之后他先在上海受雇于静安寺路1141号的 U.J. Soskin，后来受雇于 Bent Brothers and Co. 上海分公司。后者公司的老板 Y.M. Bent 曾是红军承包商，众所周知由莫斯科 Narodny 银行提供资金。

申请人在哈尔滨的一所商业学校受教育。1929年他前往香港，在圣约瑟夫书院就读8个月。回到哈尔滨后，他受雇于荷兰保险公司担任职员。1932年底左右，他自愿离开该公司前往上海。在这里，他受雇于美亚贸易公司（地址四川路320号）的 R.B. Bitker 所拥有的霞飞路“Cosmos”食品店担任出纳。1934年“Cosmos”商店清算后，他加入中国 RCA Victor 公司（地址南京路356号），即其目前的工作单位。申请人自1937年1月以来一直是上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别辅警队）的成员。

他在公共安全局登记为俄国侨民。Mabel PATENT，娘家姓 ISAAC，阿拉伯犹太人，1917年2月21日出生于伊拉克 Hilla。1920年她与母亲一起离开伊拉克前往香港，1923年

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff    Forwarded by W.A.igan A.S.M.

Gavryil Kuzmitch PIANKOFF, Russian, was born in
Nerchinsk, Transbaikal Province, Siberia, on July 12, 1898.
He is reported to have left Russia for Korea in 1922 and later
proceeded to Chang-Chun, Manchuria. In April 1923 he obtained
employment with the Chinese Eastern Railway and worked with
that concern until the end of 1931. He arrived in Shanghai
from Harbin in the beginning of 1932 and soon afterwards
operated a boarding house in the Joffre Terrace, Avenue Joffre.
In June 1934 he obtained employment with International Saving
Society first as a watchman and later as a supervisor of
building repairs. He left that concern in June 1938 owing to
a reduction in staff. In July 1938 he was engaged by the
Barco Gauze, Bandage & Cotton Co., 392-3-4, Route de Zikawei,
as a supervisor of works, where he is still employed. In
1927, while in Harbin the applicant became a Soviet citizen
but in Shanghai he renounced his allegiance to the Soviet
Government and registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee.
He holds passport No.8759, issued by the Police Bureau of the
City Government of Shanghai on 21-8-35.

Faina Prokofievna PIANKOFF, nee USHAKOFF, was born in
Transbaikal Province, Siberia, on June 12, 1897. She married
the applicant in 1916 and ever since has been living together
with him. They have two children: - daughter Tatiana, born
in Chang-Chun on January 19, 1923 and at present studying in
St. Sophies' School on Route de Soeurs, and son Vitaly born
in Harbin on January 19, 1931 and at present studying in the
Peter Pan School on Route Bourgeat.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records

加夫里尔·库兹米奇·皮扬科夫（Gavryil Kuzmitch PIANKOFF），俄国人，1898年7月12日出生于西伯利亚外贝加尔省涅尔琴斯克。据报他于1922年离开俄国前往朝鲜，随后前往满洲长春。1923年4月，他在中东铁路公司受雇，并一直为该机构工作至1931年底。他于1932年初从哈尔滨抵达上海，不久后在霞飞路霞飞坊经营一家寄宿公寓。1934年6月，他受雇于万国储蓄会，初任看守，后任建筑维修主管。由于裁员，他于1938年6月离开该机构。1938年7月，他被霞飞路392-3-4号的巴科纱布绷带棉花公司（Barco Gauze, Bandage & Cotton Co.）聘为工程主管，目前仍在此任职。1927年在哈尔滨期间，申请人成为苏联公民，但在上海他放弃了对苏联政府的效忠，并在俄国侨民委员会登记。他持有上海市政府警察局于1935年8月21日签发的第8759号护照。

法伊娜·普罗科菲耶夫娜·皮扬科夫（Faina Prokofievna PIANKOFF），娘家姓乌沙科夫（USHAKOFF），1897年6月12日出生于西伯利亚外贝加尔省。她于1916年与申请人结婚，此后一直与其共同生活。他们有两个孩子：女儿塔季扬娜（Tatiana），1923年1月19日出生于长春，目前在修女路圣索菲亚学校就读；儿子维塔利（Vitaly），1931年1月19日出生于哈尔滨，目前在蒲石路彼得潘学校就读。

Subject A.I. Shilo, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by Adgan

Andrey Ivanovich SHILO, Russian, was born on September 25, 1876 in Poltava Province, South Russia. Formerly a farmer in the Maritime Province, he is reported to have left Russia for Manchuria in 1922 and for the following three years to have resided in Harbin and other places along the Chinese Eastern Railway.
In 1925 he arrived in Shanghai from Harbin and has since been residing in this city. He worked casually as a carpenter etc. until 1927 and for the following six years was employed in the same capacity with Russian newspaper "Slovo". In 1931 he became a member of the "Patronage for the relief to Very Aged Emigrants" of which he is now the secretary. This organization is constituted of a small group of old and destitute Russians depending mainly on charity. Shilo himself is an old man and for the past several years has been unable to work. He lives in the direst poverty, being supported by charity and, according to his own statement, by his step-son, Mr. J.G. Makagon, who is reported to have been residing in Australia since 1928 and whose address he gives as " 8 Mile Plains, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia". Shilo states that his step-son has made on his behalf an application for an immigration visa to Australia.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and at present resides at 330 Route Cardinal Mercier, where he occupies a small room in a Chinese house. He holds certificate of good character issued by the French Police on 11-10-38 ( No.136 ).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records against this person.

D. C. ( Special Branch)

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

安德烈·伊万诺维奇·希洛（Andrey Ivanovich SHILO），俄国人，1876年9月25日出生于俄罗斯南部波尔塔瓦省。他曾是滨海省的农民，据报于1922年离开俄国前往满洲，并在随后的三年里居住在哈尔滨及中东铁路沿线的其他地方。
1925年他从哈尔滨抵达上海，此后一直居住在该市。直到1927年，他零星从事木匠等工作，随后的六年里，他以同样的身份受雇于俄文报纸《言论报》（Slovo）。1931年，他成为“高龄贫困侨民救济促进会”的成员，目前担任该会秘书。该组织由一小群主要依靠慈善救济的老弱贫困俄国人组成。希洛本人已年迈，过去几年无法工作。他生活在极度贫困中，依靠慈善救济以及据他自己称由其继子 J.G. Makagon 先生供养，据报该继子自1928年起居住在澳大利亚，其地址为“澳大利亚昆士兰州布里斯班 8 Mile Plains”。希洛称其继子已代表他申请澳大利亚移民签证。

他在莫尔缅路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记，目前居住在卡迪尼尔·梅尔西埃路330号，在一栋中式房屋内占用一个小房间。他持有法国警察局于1938年10月11日签发的良好品行证明书（编号136）。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ____
S.1, Special Branch ____
REPORT
Date Oct. 21, 1938.

Subject B.A. Medvedsky, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by W. Logan A.S.I.

Boris Alexandrovich MEDVEDSKY, Russian, born on June
19, 1904 at Warsaw, Poland (formerly a part of Russian Empire).
Former cadet of the Habarovsk Military School, he arrived in
Shanghai from Vladivostok via Genzan (Korea) in 1923, together
with the school. Upon completing his education in 1924 he
proceeded to Canton where he was employed as a guard for about
six months, after which he returned to Shanghai. In 1925-1926
he was without a fixed employment. In 1927, after about three
months' service in the Russian Detachment, S.V.C., he was engaged
by Jardine, Matheson & Co. as a watchman, in which capacity he
worked until the middle of 1929. He left this position on his
own accord and from 1930 has been employed as a foreman with the
Shanghai Telephone Company. He states that it is his intention
to proceed to Australia in 1940, when he has completed 10 years
service with the company and may draw his superannuation fund.

Applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and at present resides at 153
Rue Amiral Courbet together with his wife, Mrs. Valentina
Gavrilovna Medvedsky nee Domratsky, born 19/9/1913, and their
child born in 1938. Mrs. Medvedsky is reported to have been
residing in Shanghai since 1931. She is reported to be a
graduated nurse, having received her training at Shanghai
Sanitarium & Hospital, 150 Rabicon Road.

Mr. and Mrs. Medvedsky hold certificates of good character
issued by the French Police on 18/10/38 (Nos. 146 and 147,
respectively).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records against
these persons.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

鲍里斯·亚历山德罗维奇·梅德韦茨基（Boris Alexandrovich MEDVEDSKY），俄国人，1904年6月19日出生于波兰华沙（前俄罗斯帝国的一部分）。他曾是哈巴罗夫斯克军事学校的学员，1923年随该校师生经元山（朝鲜）从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海。1924年完成学业后，他前往广州，在那里担任警卫约六个月，之后返回上海。1925-1926年间，他没有固定工作。1927年，在上海义勇队（S.V.C.）俄国分队服役约三个月后，他被怡和洋行（Jardine, Matheson & Co.）聘为看守，在此职位上工作至1929年中。他自愿离职，自1930年起受雇于上海电话公司，担任领班。他表示打算在1940年前往澳大利亚，届时他在该公司服务满10年，可以领取养老金。

申请人在莫尔缅路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记，目前与妻子瓦伦蒂娜·加夫里洛夫娜·梅德韦茨基（Valentina Gavrilovna Medvedsky，娘家姓 Domratsky，1913年9月19日出生）及1938年出生的孩子居住在库尔贝海军上将路153号。据报梅德韦茨基夫人自1931年起居住在上海。据报她是一名注册护士，曾在拉比孔路150号的上海疗养院及医院接受培训。

梅德韦茨基夫妇持有法国警察局于1938年10月18日签发的良好品行证明书（编号分别为146和147）。

工部局警务处档案中没有任何对这些人不利的记录。

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

D.C.（特科）

Subject J. M. Mironoff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by [Signature]

Jury ( George) Mihailovich MIRONOFF, Russian, born
on May 10, 1912 at Samara, Russia. He is reported to have left
Russia for Manchuria in 1924 and subsequently resided in Harbin.
In 1929 he graduated from the Harbin Commercial School and du-
ring the same year left for Belgium where for the following five
years he studied in the University of Liege ( Civil Engineering
Department), graduating in October, 1935. In March, 1936 he ar-
rived in Shanghai from Belgium and shortly afterwards proceeded
to Chefoo to join his parents. He returned to this city in Sep-
tember of the same year and on 15-10-36 joined the French Po-
lice as a garde auxiliaire . He is still employed with the Po-
lice.

Applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, on the strength of Certificate
of Identity No 5490/1571 issued on 30-12-35 at Brussels. He
resides at 479 Route Cardinal Mercier together with his parents.
Mr. M.T. Mironoff, his father, an engineer by profession, is a
Soviet citizen. He was issued a certificate of character on
18-10-38 in connection with his application for immigration vi-
sa to Australia.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
against this person.

A. Prokofiew
D. S. I.

D. C. ( Special Branch )

Subject L.Ya. Baranovsky and J.L. Baranovsky, applicants for certificates

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford.

Leonty Yakovlevich BARANOVSKY, Russian Jew, born on
April 10, 1888 at Krasnoyarsk, Siberia. According to his own sta-
tement, he left Russia for Manchuria in 1919 and after a short
stay in Harbin proceeded to Shanghai arriving in this city du-
ring the same year. While in Shanghai he is known to have been
engaged in commercial activities. From 1922 to 1927 he conduct-
ed the "Universal Store" at 777 East Broadway (Haberdashery and
Millinery Store) with branches in N-Szechuen Road ( closed in
1926 ) and Bubbling Well Road ( closed in 1930 ). From 1927 he
has been conducting a similar business at 850 Avenue Joffre.
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Commit-
tee, 118/1 Moumein Road, and with the S.C.U. Police Bureau and
at present resides at 818-A Avenue Joffre, together with his
wife, Mrs Esther Isayevna Baranovsky nee Lapshin. On 24-8-36 a
notice appeared in the "Sin Wan Pao" to the effect that Baranov-
sky had acquired the status of a Chinese citizen. Interviewed
in connection with the present enquiries Baranovsky stated that
the notice in question referred to his wife.

Jack L. Baranovsky, son of the above, was born on
June 5, 1911 at Achinsk, Siberia. Upon completion of his education
in one of the Shanghai schools he left for Belgium in 1930 and
for the following six years studied in the Institute for Tex-
tile Industry at Tournai, graduating in 1936. He then left for
Buenos Ayres, Argentine, where he stayed for about 6 months,
after which he proceeded to Shanghai. He arrived here in July,
1937 and has since been living with his parents without a fixed
employment. He holds certificate of identity No 5169/1909 is-
sued on 14-7-36 at Brussels.

The Baranovsky family are reputed to be fairly pros-

Leonty Yakovlevich BARANOVSKY，俄罗斯犹太人，1888年4月10日出生于西伯利亚克拉斯诺亚尔斯克。据其自称，他于1919年离开俄罗斯前往满洲，在哈尔滨短暂停留后前往上海，于同年抵达本市。在上海期间，已知其从事商业活动。1922年至1927年，他在百老汇路（今东大名路）777号经营“环球商店”（百货及女帽店），并在北四川路（1926年关闭）和静安寺路（1930年关闭）设有分店。自1927年起，他在霞飞路850号经营类似业务。
他在莫利哀路118/1号的俄罗斯侨民委员会以及工部局警务处登记，目前与妻子 Esther Isayevna Baranovsky 太太（娘家姓 Lapshin）同住于霞飞路818-A号。1936年8月24日，《新闻报》刊登一则公告，称 Baranovsky 已取得中国公民身份。就本次调查进行面谈时，Baranovsky 称该公告指的是其妻子。

Jack L. Baranovsky，上述人士之子，1911年6月5日出生于西伯利亚阿钦斯克。在上海一所学校完成学业后，他于1930年前往比利时，在接下来的六年里就读于图尔奈纺织工业学院，于1936年毕业。随后他前往阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯，在那里停留了约6个月，之后前往上海。他于1937年7月抵达此地，此后一直与父母同住，无固定职业。他持有1936年7月14日在布鲁塞尔签发的第5169/1909号身份证明书。

opinions differ on this point and he cannot boast of having a

    He first came to the notice of the Municipal Police
in July, 1919 when a letter was received from Mr. V.A. Grosse,
who was then Russian Consul-General at Shanghai, in which Bara-

    An extract from police report dated January 12, 1931
reads as follows:-
    " L. Baranovsky, owner of a cloth shop at 750 Avenue
Joffre. He is well known to the police as a smuggler of narco-
tics and swindler. He often receives by post from Paris various
parcels containing clothing and perfume, which were sent to him
by Leontieff, his agent in Paris".
    Mr. Baranovsky and his son were issued by the French

and 1156/A, respectively) in connection with their application
for immigration visae to Australia.

1931年1月12日的一份警务报告摘录如下：
“L. Baranovsky，霞飞路750号一家布店店主。警方熟知其为毒品走私者和诈骗犯。他经常通过邮政从巴黎收到各种包裹，内含衣物和香水，这些包裹由其巴黎代理人 Leontieff 寄给他”。
Baranovsky 先生及其子因申请澳大利亚移民签证，于1938年4月22日获法租界巡捕房签发了品行良好证明书（编号分别为 1135/A 和 1156/A）。

means.

118/1 Moulmein Road, and holds passport No.18265, issued on
July 14, 1937, by the Police Bureau of the City Government
of Shanghai.

Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by C. Crawford. 26.9.

Rudolf OPPENHEIM, German (former Austrian), was born
in Vienna on October 20, 1907. He left Austria in 1927
and for a period of five years approximately was employed
in various capacities with Messrs. Simon ARZT, Port Said.
He left Egypt in 1933 and from June of that year
until January 1936 was engaged in the shipping business
in a lucrative position in both Majorca and Barcelona.
He left Barcelona in April 1936 and arrived in Shanghai
in June, 1936 since when he has been Head Porter of the
Cathay and Metropole Hotels.
During his sojourn here he has not come to the notice
of this Police Force in any way and nothing to his detriment
is on record. Further he has never been committed to any
institution in this city for mental incompetence.
He is at present in possession of a valid German
passport issued in Shanghai on April 20, 1938, No. 641/38.
This is due to expire on January 19, 1939.
The applicant needs the attached forms to be duly
signed in connection with his application to the South
African authorities to settle down in that country in order
to acquire British naturalization.

Rudolf OPPENHEIM，德国人（前奥地利人），1907年10月20日出生于维也纳。他于1927年离开奥地利，在大约五年的时间里，以各种身份受雇于塞得港的 Simon ARZT 公司。他于1933年离开埃及，从当年6月至1936年1月，在马略卡岛和巴塞罗那从事航运业务，职位优厚。他于1936年4月离开巴塞罗那，1936年6月抵达上海，此后一直担任华懋饭店和大都会饭店的首席门童。
在此逗留期间，他未以任何方式引起本警务处的注意，档案中亦无对其不利的记录。此外，他从未因精神失常而被送入本市的任何机构。
他目前持有一本有效的德国护照，于1938年4月20日在上海签发，编号 641/38。该护照将于1939年1月19日到期。

Date October 25, 1938

Subject A.I. Efimoff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

Commander F.H.M. Skyrme, Indo China S.N. Co., was communicated in connection with this application. He stated that he only wanted to ascertain that Efimoff had no police record in Shanghai, before placing him on the list of candidates for employment as a guard.

Brief particulars of the applicant as far as known to the police, are as follows:-

Alexander Ivanovich EFIMOFF, Russian, born on 21-8-96 in Samara Province, Russia. Former junior war time officer of the Russian Army, he is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in 1922 and, with the exception of several periods when he was absent to Canton or Tientsin, to have since been residing in this city. During this period he was variously employed as a watchman, guard etc.

In 1926 he was the editor of a small Russian magazine entitled "UKRAI". Following the publication in this magazine of several articles of an insulting character, a private criminal prosecution case was brought against him by the aggrieved party. In connection with this matter a warrant for his arrest was issued by the old Mixed Court on 25-9-26. However, the warrant was not executed owing to the fact that Efimoff was absent to Tientsin. A despatch warrant was issued against him by the same Court on application of the complainant, but as the latter was unable to defray the expenses involved by the extradition of Efimoff from Tientsin to Shanghai, the matter was dropped. Upon Efimoff's returning to Shanghai in 1930, the complainant had a chance to take up the case before the 1-st S.S.D. Court, but failed to do so.

In connection with this case Efimoff was refused regi-

就此申请事宜与印度支那轮船公司（Indo China S.N. Co.）的 F.H.M. Skyrme 指挥官进行了沟通。他表示，在将 Efimoff 列入警卫职位候选人名单之前，他只想确认 Efimoff 在上海没有警方记录。

据警方所知，申请人的简要情况如下：

Alexander Ivanovich EFIMOFF，俄罗斯人，1896年8月21日出生于俄罗斯萨马拉省。前俄罗斯军队低级战时军官，据报他于1922年从哈尔滨抵达上海，除几次前往广州或天津外，此后一直居住在本市。在此期间，他从事过看守、警卫等各种工作。

1926年，他是一家名为“UKRAI”的小型俄文杂志的编辑。因在该杂志上发表了几篇具有侮辱性质的文章，受害方对他提起了私人刑事起诉。为此，旧混合法院于1926年9月25日签发了对他的逮捕令。然而，由于 Efimoff 当时去了天津，逮捕令未能执行。应原告申请，同一法院对他签发了通缉令，但由于原告无力承担将 Efimoff 从天津引渡到上海所涉及的费用，此事不了了之。1930年 Efimoff 回到上海后，原告有机会在第一特区地方法院重新提起此案，但未这样做。

与此案有关，Efimoff 被拒绝登

Mr. P. A. Ballod,
764 Rue Bourgeat, apt. 13,
Shanghai, 13-th December 1938.

To Commissioner of
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

Sir,
    I, Peter Ballod, Latvian citizen leaving Shanghai for Australia,
hereby beg you to issue a clean record about me from Shanghai Muni-
cipal Police as such certificate is required by Australian authorities.
    Almost two years ago, being in financial difficulties after a
loss of Sh.$ 25.000.- in my newspaper enterprise, which I tried to
lead absolutely independently and honestly, I was once attacked by
my Chinese workmen on ground of money matters.
    The case was taken before the Chinese Court where the judge
openly took the side of Chinese workmen and was challenged and dis-
missed from this particular case, but though the second judge was
in appearance less prejudiced, he took also the side of Chinese
workmen and fined me Sh. $ 60.-
    Thinking that such misconduct as the fight in selfdefence in
general is not a very serious offence, and that such thing might
happen to anybody and taking into consideration the prejudice of
Chinese court I would greatly appreciate and would be much obliged
to you for considering the case for my benefit providing me with a
certificate that I have a clean record and enable me to leave China
for good.
    Thanking you in anticipation,

                                    I have the honour to be,
                                                Sir,
                                    Your obedient servant,
                                    P. Ballod
                                    P. A. Ballod.
pages.zh:
P. A. Ballod 先生，
上海布尔热瓦路764号13室，1938年12月13日。

致 上海公共租界工部局
警务总监，
上海。

先生：
    本人 Peter Ballod，拉脱维亚公民，即将离开上海前往澳大利亚，特此恳请阁下出具一份上海公共租界工部局警务处关于本人的无犯罪记录证明，因为澳大利亚当局需要此类证书。
    大约两年前，在我的报业企业中损失了25,000上海元之后，我陷入了财务困境，当时我试图完全独立且诚实地经营该企业，我曾因金钱问题遭到中国工人的袭击。
    该案提交至中国法院，法官公然偏袒中国工人，该法官受到质疑并被免除审理此案，尽管第二位法官表面上偏见较少，但也偏袒中国工人，并罚款我60上海元。
    考虑到这种一般性的自卫斗殴行为并非非常严重的罪行，且此类事情可能发生在任何人身上，并考虑到中国法院的偏见，如蒙阁下出于对我的利益考虑，提供一份我有无犯罪记录的证明，使我能永远离开中国，本人将不胜感激并深表谢意。
    预先致谢，

                                    谨此，
                                                先生，
                                    您顺从的仆人，
                                    P. Ballod
                                    P. A. Ballod.

Date October 31, 1938

Subject P.A.Ballod, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

Peter Alexandrovich BALLOD, Latvian citizen, born on November 24,1910 at Harbin. Son of a former employee of the Customs in Harbin, he is reported to have graduated from the Commercial School of the Chinese Eastern Railway at Harbin in 1928 and for the following 5 years to have attended the Institute of Oriental and Commercial Sciences in that city.

He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in January,1936 and in March of the same year became editor and publisher of Russian daily newspaper entitled "NOVY PUT" ( New Trail ), "organ of defence of Russian interests in the Far East". This newspaper,which at one time was prominent in Shanghai on account of its criticism of the Japanese administration methods in Manchuria and harmful to the interests of Russian population, went out of existence in March,1937 owing to financial difficulties. In connection with the payment of wages Ballod had a series of troubles with Chinese workers in his employ which culminated in a street fight between him and three foreign members of his staff on one hand and his Chinese workers on the other. In connection with this affair Ballod was charged with Assault and on 31-3-37 was sentenced by the 2-nd S.S.D.Court to 60 days detention or $ 60.00 fine.

He came to the notice of the Municipal Police in June,1936,when he and one Gridneff,assistant editor of the "Novy Put", were brought to Chengtu Road Station on a complaint of one Miss V.GORSKAYA alias Viola Smith,Japanese subject,proprietress of a "massage establishment" at 52 Love Lane. 彼得·亚历山德罗维奇·巴洛德（Peter Alexandrovich BALLOD），拉脱维亚公民，1910年11月24日出生于哈尔滨。据称其父曾任哈尔滨海关职员，他于1928年毕业于哈尔滨中东铁路商业学校，并在随后的5年间就读于该市的东方与商业科学学院。

他于1936年1月从哈尔滨抵达上海，同年3月成为俄文日报《新路》（NOVY PUT，New Trail）的编辑兼出版人，该报自称是“远东俄罗斯利益保卫机构”。这份报纸曾因批评日本在满洲的行政手段并损害俄罗斯居民利益而在上海一度颇具影响力，后因财务困难于1937年3月停刊。在支付工资问题上，巴洛德与其雇佣的中国工人发生了一系列纠纷，最终导致他与三名外籍员工一方同其中国工人另一方之间发生街头斗殴。就此事件，巴洛德被控殴打罪，并于1937年3月31日被第二特区地方法院判处拘留60天或罚款60美元。

他于1936年6月引起工部局警务处的注意，当时他与《新路》助理编辑格里德涅夫（Gridneff）因一名名为V.戈尔斯卡娅小姐（Miss V.GORSKAYA，又名维奥拉·史密斯 Viola Smith，日本籍，爱多亚路52号一家“按摩院”的业主）的投诉而被带至成都路捕房。看来戈尔斯卡娅小姐以为〔此处转录不清〕去她家，意图

Igor Mihailovich TORNOVSKY, Russian, born on April
21, 1908 at Verhneudinsk, Siberia. According to his own
statement, he left Russia together with his parents in 1919
for Urga, Mongolia, where he remained until 1921 when he
proceeded to Harbin. After graduating from a local middle
school in 1925 he studied in the Harbin Polytechnical
Institute (Electro-Mechanical Department), graduating in
1931. In April, 1932 he proceeded to Tientsin where he was
employed as a service engineer with Theatre Equipment Co.
for about five months, after which he was transferred to
Shanghai branch of the concern (Theatre Supply Co.,
Embankment Building). Leaving this firm in September, 1934,
shortly prior to its liquidation, he joined the R.C.A.
Victor Company of China, 356 Peking Road, his present place
of employment.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee,
118/1 Moulmein Road, and with the Shanghai City Government
Police Bureau (Reg. 13390) and at present resides at 1920
Avenue Joffre, Apt. 302, together with his wife, Mrs. Evgenia
Porfirievna Tornovsky nee Gladysheff, born 8-4-1913 at
Harbin, and their daughter Helene, aged 1 year. His father,
M.G. Tornovsky, formerly an officer in the Russian Army,
also resides in Shanghai. Mrs. Tornovsky has been residing
in Shanghai since 1934 and from December, 1934 to June, 1937
is reported to have been employed with Cosmos Paper Company,
Hamilton House, as a steno-typist.

Mr. and Mrs. Tornovsky hold certificates of good
character issued by the French Police on 22-10-38 (Nos. 150

伊戈尔·米哈伊洛维奇·托尔诺夫斯基（Igor Mihailovich TORNOVSKY），俄罗斯人，1908年4月21日出生于西伯利亚上乌丁斯克。据其自述，他于1919年随父母离开俄罗斯前往蒙古乌兰巴托，在那里停留至1921年，随后前往哈尔滨。1925年从当地一所中学毕业后，他在哈尔滨工业大学（机电系）学习，于1931年毕业。1932年4月，他前往天津，在剧院设备公司（Theatre Equipment Co.）担任维修工程师约五个月，之后被调往该公司上海分公司（剧院供应公司，位于外滩大楼）。1934年9月，在该公司清算前夕，他离职加入目前就职的中国无线电公司胜利牌留声机分公司（R.C.A. Victor Company of China，北京路356号）。

他在莫利哀路118/1号的俄罗斯侨民委员会以及上海市政府警察局（注册号13390）登记，目前与妻子叶夫根尼娅·波菲里耶芙娜·托尔诺夫斯基夫人（娘家姓格拉迪舍夫 Gladysheff，1913年4月8日出生于哈尔滨）及一岁的女儿海伦同住于霞飞路1920号302室。其父M.G.托尔诺夫斯基，前俄国军官，也居住在上海。据报道，托尔诺夫斯基夫人自1934年起居住在上海，并于1934年12月至1937年6月期间受雇于汉密尔顿大厦的宇宙造纸公司（Cosmos Paper Company），担任速记打字员。

列昂尼德·帕夫洛维奇·罗文斯基（Leonid Pavlovitch ROVENSKY），俄罗斯人，1896年11月26日出生于西伯利亚托木斯克省。据其自述，他自1898年起与在中东铁路任职的父亲一同居住在哈尔滨。1923年他前往天津，在那里从事各种工作，直到1931年创立了自己的企业，名为“L.P. 罗文斯基公司”，运输公司，北四川路179号，B.C.区。

他于1937年10月从天津抵达上海。据信，由于在与天津新当局打交道时遇到一些困难，他被迫离开该城市。

其妻玛丽亚·季莫费耶芙娜·罗文斯基（Maria Timofeevna ROVENSKY），娘家姓费多罗娃（Fedorova），俄罗斯人，1895年6月21日出生于俄罗斯萨马拉。据报道，她自幼居住在满洲哈尔滨，并于1923年3月与申请人结婚。

申请人在莫利哀路118/1号的俄罗斯侨民委员会登记。

工部局警务处档案中关于这些人没有任何记录。

Boris Fedorovitch ZENZINOFF, Russian, was born
on October 4, 1898, in Transbaikal Province, Siberia.
He is reported to have left Russia for Harbin in 1921 and
during the same year entered the Harbin Polytechnical
Institute. Upon graduating from same in December 1926
with the diploma of Electro-Mechanical Engineer, in September
1927 he obtained a position of an Assistant Manager in the
Technical Department of I.I. Tchurin & Co., a well known
firm in Harbin. He left that concern in March 1932 owing
to the closure of the above department. He arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin in April of the same year and soon after-
wards obtained an employment with Elliot Hazzard, Architect,
33 Szechuen Road. He left that concern in July 1933
owing to a reduction in staff. From 1934 to 1936 he was
engaged by Mr. Lehonos, Architect, on construction of the
Russian Orthodox Cathedral, Route Paul Henry. On com-
pletion of this work he left for Canton. Having failed
to obtain any employment there he returned to Shanghai and
in February 1937 secured his present position of designer,
with Andersen, Mayer & Company.

The applicant holds passport No. 15742 issued on
September 23, 1937 by the Police Bureau of the City Govern-
ment of Shanghai.

1906. She is reported to have left Russia together with
her family in 1919 and subsequently resided in Harbin, where

Georgy Alexeyevitch MISHIN, Russian, was born in Moscow,
Russia on May 13, 1908. He is reported to have left Russia
together with his parents in 1922 and subsequently resided in
Harbin. Upon graduating from a local high school he studied
in the Harbin Polytechnical Institute graduating in March
1933 with the diploma of Civil and Railway Engineer.

He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in April 1933 and in
May of the same year obtained employment as designer of rein-
forced concrete constructions with Davis, Brooke and Gran,
81 Jinkee Road. He left that concern in March 1935, owing
to reduction in staff. From April to October of the same
year he worked in the same capacity with L.E. Hudec, B.A.,
209 Yuen Ming Yuen Road. In the beginning of 1936 he establish-
ed his own business as a woodwork contractor and at present
has his work shops at 23, Rue Corneille.

He holds passport No. 15697 issued on September 24, 1937,
by the Police Bureau of the City Government of Shanghai.

While in Shanghai, the applicant did not come to the
notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any
activities of an undesirable nature.

Date November 3, 19 38.

Subject T.A. Baranoff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff        Forwarded by C. Cantoni

Theodore Alexandrovitch BARANOFF, Russian, was born on
December 12, 1896, at Tiflis, Russia. He is reported to
have left Russia in 1925. A musician by occupation, he worked
in this capacity for various periods in Harbin, Mukden and
Tsingtao and arrived in Shanghai from the latter city towards
the end of 1926. Here he worked in various cabarets, res-
taurants and hotels playing violin and Hawaiian guitar.
Later he was employed by Robinson Piano Company as a piano
tuner from 1930 to 1935, when he had to leave that concern
owing to reduction in staff. From July 1933 to September
1935, while in the employ of Robinson Piano Co., he also
played violin in the orchestra of the Circle Sportif Francais .
Leaving this place of employment owing to a change of the
orchestra he worked as a musician at the "Arcadia" Restaurant
until October 4, 1938, after which he was engaged by "Ciro's"
Cabaret, his present place of employment.

The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road. He holds passport No. 18560
issued on July 27, 1937 by the Police Bureau of the City
Government of Shanghai.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to his character.

The reference to Mrs. BARANOFF in the attached communica-
tion from the Australian Trade Commissioner's Office is
apparently due to some misunderstanding, as the applicant
states that he is a bachelor.

D.C. (Special Branch)                                N. S. Pavloff
                                                     D. P. S.

西奥多·亚历山德罗维奇·巴拉诺夫，俄国人，1896年12月12日出生于俄国第比利斯。据报他于1925年离开俄国。作为一名音乐家，他曾在哈尔滨、沈阳和青岛断续工作，并于1926年底从青岛抵达上海。在此地，他在各种歌舞厅、餐馆和酒店演奏小提琴和夏威夷吉他。后来，他于1930年至1935年间受雇于罗宾逊钢琴公司（Robinson Piano Company）担任调琴师，后因裁员不得不离开该公司。1933年7月至1935年9月期间，在受雇于罗宾逊钢琴公司的同时，他还在法国总会（Circle Sportif Francais）的乐队中演奏小提琴。后因乐队变动离开该职，他在“阿卡迪亚”（Arcadia）餐馆担任乐师，直至1938年10月4日，之后受雇于“西罗”（Ciro's）歌舞厅，即其现任职位。

申请人已在穆尔门路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记。他持有上海市政府警察局于1937年7月27日签发的第18560号护照。

Subject Mr. G. Stepanoff, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by J.S.I. Prokofiev.    Forwarded by C. Clausen

George Alexeyevitch STEPANOFF, Russian, born on January 8, 1895 at Odessa, South Russia. According to his own statement, he left Russia for Manchuria in 1923 and after a short stay in Harbin proceeded to Shanghai. In July, 1925 he left for Australia where he was employed for over one year with Sanders, Jewellers, George Street, Sydney, as an engraver. Returning to Shanghai in 1927, he established his own business at 800 Avenue Joffre ( G.Stepanoff, Jewellers, Watchmakers & Engravers ), which he is still conducting.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and the S.C.G. Police Bureau ( Reg. No. 6271 ) and at present resides at 800 Avenue Joffre together with his wife, Mrs Olga Mihailovna Stepanoff nee Tischenko, born 17-4-1902 at Vladivostok, and their son, Evgeny, 11 years of age.

Mr. and Mrs Stepanoff hold certificates of good character issued by the French Police on 15-10-38 (Nos 142 and 141, respectively ).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records against these persons.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

D. C. ( Special Branch ).

J.R.

他在莫尔尼姆路118/1号的俄罗斯侨民委员会以及工部局警务处（注册号 6271）登记，目前与妻子 Olga Mihailovna Stepanoff 夫人（婚前姓 Tischenko，1902年4月17日出生于符拉迪沃斯托克）及11岁的儿子 Evgeny 居住在霞飞路800号。

Date November 11, 19 38.

Subject S.P. Rogovoy, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff    Forwarded by [签名: C. Gaspar ...]

Savely Petrovitch ROGOVOY, Russian, was born on June
30, 1900 in Kiev Province, Russia. He is reported to have
escaped from the U.S.S.R. to Manchuria in 1925 and subse-
quently resided in Harbin. A musician by occupation he
worked in this capacity for various periods in Tsingtao,
Hankow, Tientsin and Shanghai. He first arrived in Shanghai
in 1929 and worked in "Tkachenko Cafe" 405, Avenue Joffre.
Later he proceeded to Hankow and then to Tientsin, where,
it is reported, he worked in the same capacity. He returned
to Shanghai from Tientsin in May 1937 and soon afterwards
established his own business under the style of "Rogovoy
& Co., Music House", 723, Avenue Joffre, which he is still
conducting. From June 1938 Rogovoy has also been employed
as a cello and saxaphone player in the orchestra of the
Cercle Sportif Francais.

Ekaterina Nicolaevna Rogovoy nee Izgorodin, Russian,
was born on November 2, 1902 in Tomsk, Siberia. She
married the applicant in Vladivostok in 1921 and has since
been residing together with him.

Mr. and Mrs. Rogovoy are registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee and hold passport No.4236 issued on
May 23, 1935 by the Police Bureau of the City Government
of Shanghai.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to the characters of these persons.

[左侧签名/缩写]
D.C. (Special Branch)

[右侧签名: N.A. Pavloff]
D. P. S.

Savely Petrovitch ROGOVOY，俄罗斯人，1900年6月30日出生于俄罗斯基辅省。据报他于1925年从苏联逃往满洲，随后居住在哈尔滨。作为一名音乐家，他曾在青岛、汉口、天津和上海等地断续从事该职业。他于1929年首次抵达上海，在霞飞路405号的“Tkachenko Cafe”工作。后来他前往汉口，随后又去天津，据报在那里也从事同样的工作。他于1937年5月从天津返回上海，不久后以“Rogovoy & Co., Music House”的名义在霞飞路723号创办了自己的商行，目前仍在经营。自1938年6月起，Rogovoy 还在法国总会（Cercle Sportif Francais）的管弦乐队中担任大提琴和萨克斯管演奏员。

Ekaterina Nicolaevna Rogovoy，婚前姓 Izgorodin，俄罗斯人，1902年11月2日出生于西伯利亚托木斯克。她于1921年在符拉迪沃斯托克与申请人结婚，此后一直与其共同居住。

Rogovoy 夫妇已在俄罗斯侨民委员会登记，并持有上海市政府警务处于1935年5月23日签发的第4236号护照。

Nicolai Ivanovitch POPOFF, Russian, was born on
February 18, 1908 at Yaomin Station, Chinese Eastern
Railway. Upon graduating from a high school in Harbin he
entered the Harbin Polythecnic Institute and subsequently
graduated from same in March, 1934 with a diploma of
Electro-Technical Engineer. He first arrived in Shanghai
from Harbin in April 1935 and resided here together with
his brother V.I. Popoff, who at that time was employed
with Mr. Chibunovsky & Co., A.G. Heating and Sanitary
Engineers. In June 1935 he returned to Harbin and resided
there until November 1936, when he left for Tsingtao. He
worked casually in that city until October 9, 1938, when
he proceeded to Shanghai.

The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee 118/1 Moulmein Road and holds passport

Pavel Fedorovich ORLOW ( Orloff),Russian,born on December 7,1887,in Tver Province,Russia. According to his own statement, he left the U.S.S.R. for Manchuria in 1929 and subsequently resided in Harbin until November,1936, when he left for Peking. After a short stay in that city he proceeded to Shanghai arriving in this city in February,1937. A graduate of the Medical Faculty of the Imp. Nicolas University, Saratov.( 1916 ) he established himself in Shanghai as a medical practitioner with an office at 153 Route des Soeurs,Apt.6.

His wife,Mrs Olga Ivanovna ORLOW nee Penkin, born 4-7-1894 at Nijny-Novgorod, Russia, arrived in Shanghai together with her husband. A dentist by profession she has been working in this capacity with an office at the above address.

Mr. and Mrs Orlow are registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee.118/1 Moulmein Road and with the S.C. C. Police Bureau ( R.887 ). On 15-11-38 they were issued by the French Police certificates of good character ( Nos 172 and 173,respectively ).

Raissa Mihailovna HOTIMSKY nee Solomin, Russian, born
on March 10, 1899 at Tomsk, Siberia. According to her own
statement, she left Russia for China in 1923 and until 1934
resided in Tientsin where she conducted a boarding house.
She is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Tientsin in
September, 1934 together with her daughter, Miss Lydia M.
Hotimsky, born 22-2-1918 at Tomsk.

While in Shanghai Mrs. Hotimeky is not known to have
any employment. Her daughter who is reported to have
graduated from the St. Joseph School, Tientsin, in 1933,
has been employed for the past two years as a stenographer
with Siemens China Co., 233 Nanking Road. The applicant's
son, C.J. Hotimsky, 22, has been employed with R.C.A. Victor
Co. of China, 356 Peking Road, as an accountant for over
three years.

Mrs. and Miss Hotimsky are registered with the Council
of United Russian Organization (SORO), 8 Avenue Dubail, and
with the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau. They hold
certificates of good character issued by the French Police
on 7-11-38 (No.167) and 15-11-38 (No.171) respectively.
Their present address is 66-A Route de Grouchy.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
regarding these persons.

D.C. (Special Branch)

Date November 21, 1938.

Subject V.I. Mariepolsky, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Cassidy

Victor Iosifovitch MARIEPOLSKY, Russian Jew, was born on December 12, 1913, in Tomsk Province, Siberia. He arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok in 1921 together with his two brothers. Here he studied in the Jewish School and later in the St. Francis College until 1930 when he proceeded to Germany. Returning to Shanghai in 1932, he joined the Texas Oil Company in May of the same year as a claims clerk. He resigned from this position on his own accord in December 1934. In January 1935 he obtained employment with Pasche Motor Service as a salesman of second hand cars in which capacity he worked until December 1935. Upon leaving this employment he worked casually until the end of 1936 when he secured a position with the "Red Seal" Dairy Farm, in Kating. He remained with that concern until the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1937 when the above farm was destroyed. During hostilities he joined Marden and Company where he worked until August 8, 1938, the date of his departure to Hongkong.

While in Shanghai, Mariepolsky was a member of the American Company, S.V.C. from September 1932 to February 1936.

In September 1936 he applied for a position in the S.M.C. Gaol. His application was turned down owing to some incorrect statements made by him in the application form regarding his age and religion.

V.I. Mariepolsky is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records detrimental to his character.

D.C. (Special Branch)
D. P. S.

维克多·约瑟福维奇·马里波尔斯基（MARIEPOLSKY），犹太裔俄国人，1913年12月12日出生于西伯利亚托木斯克省。他于1921年与两个兄弟一同从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海。在此他就读于犹太学校，后就读于圣方济各书院，直至1930年前往德国。1932年返回上海后，他于同年5月加入德士古石油公司，担任理赔职员。1934年12月，他自愿辞去该职位。1935年1月，他在帕施汽车服务公司受雇，担任二手车销售员，在此职位工作至1935年12月。离职后，他打零工直至1936年底，当时他在嘉定“红印”奶牛场谋得职位。他一直在那家公司工作，直到1937年中日敌对行动爆发，上述农场被毁。在敌对行动期间，他加入马登公司，工作至1938年8月8日，即他启程前往香港之日。

在上海期间，马里波尔斯基于1932年9月至1936年2月是美国公司S.V.C.的成员。

1936年9月，他申请在上海公共租界工部局监狱任职。由于他在申请表中关于年龄和宗教的一些陈述不实，其申请被驳回。

V.I. 马里波尔斯基已在莫尔缅路118/1号俄国侨民委员会登记。

工部局警务处档案中没有任何不利于其品行的记录。

特务科督察长

family have ever been in prison or in a mental hospital.

the following particulars regarding myself.

I arrived in Shanghai in 1918 and have been in China since
that date. During this period I have been employed by the following
concerns.

Shanghai Municipal Electricity Dept.      1918- 1921 √
Dowdall & Read          Architects.       1921- 1923 √

and I am now in business on my own account as a consulting

Judge N. E. Lurton and Mr. A. Petersen of the U.S. Court
for China. Mr. Manley C. Jensen of the P. W. D.
Mr. H. E. Arnhold, Mr. E. S. Barraclough and Inspector
W. H. Widdowson of the S. M. Police.

A. Levenspiel .

Andreyan Mihailovich VDOVIN, Russian, born on April 28,
1903 in Simbirsk Province, Russia. He is reported to have ar-
rived in Shanghai from Harbin some time during the summer of
1930. He served in the Russian Regiment, S.V.C. from 21-9-30
to 31-12-30 when he was discharged owing to sickness. Since
that time he has been casually working as a carpenter, painter,
watchman, teller, longshore-man etc. apparently earning just
enough to keep his body and soul together.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee,
118/1 Moulmein Road, and with the S.C.G. Police Bureau ( Reg.
5430 ). According to his own statement, he escaped from the
U.S.S.R. to China in 1930. However, he admits that in 1932 or
1933 he made an unsuccessful application at the Soviet consu-
late in Dairen for permission to return to the U.S.S.R. and
later applied for Soviet passport in Shanghai. In 1937 he joi-
ned the "Repatriation Union" in this city, a pro-Soviet organi-
zation, the professed aim of which is to obtain for their mem-
bers permission to return to the U.S.S.R.

In December, 1937 Vdovin came to the notice of the Mu-
nicipal Police in connection with investigations of a bomb
outrage at the offices of Russian pro-Soviet newspaper "Novo-
sti Dnia", 620 Avenue Foch. On that occasion he volunteered a
statement to the effect that a casual acquaintance of his, a
certain Russian named N.N. Ermolyeff, approached him suggest-
ing that he should place a time-bomb at the offices of the lo-
cal Soviet consulate during one of his visits there.

When interviewed in connection with his present appli-
cation Vdovin gave information about himself which conflicted

Nicolas Fedorovich ORLOFF, Russian, born on Novem-
ber 3,1885 in Tver Province,Russia. A graduate of the Impe-
rial Military Medical Academy in St.Petersburg ( 1914 ),he is
reported to have arrived in Harbin from the U.S.S.R. in 1927
and to have served in the Chinese Eastern Railway Hospital for
Mental Diseases until 1930, after which he worked independent-
ly as a medical practitioner until his departure to Shanghai.
He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in October,1935 and estab-
lished himself as medical practitioner with an office at 610
Avenue Joffre,Apt. 5.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee.
118/1 Moulmein Road,and the S.C.G. Police Bureau ( Reg.16984 )
According to his own statement, he was divorced from his wife
on 1-1-37 and at present resides at the above address together
with his son Lev Nikolaevich Orloff, born 9-11-1915 at Petro-
grad,Russia, who arrived in Shanghai together with his father
and is now a student of the St. John's University. Another
son of Dr. Orloff. Igor, aged 24, is reported to be in Hong-
kong at present where he studies medicine at the university of
Hongkong.

Mr. N.F. Orloff and his son,L.N. Orloff, hold certi-
ficates of good character issued by the French Police on No-
vember 21,1936 ( Nos 182 and 183,respectively ).

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records con-
cerning these persons.

1885年11月3日出生于俄罗斯特维尔省。他是圣彼得堡帝国军事医学院
（1914年）的毕业生，据报他于1927年从苏联抵达哈尔滨，并在中东铁路

奥尔洛夫博士的另一子伊戈尔，24岁，据报目前在香港，

Made by...D.P.S. Pavloff ........ Forwarded by C Crawford

Sergey Semenovitch PAPANOFF, Russian, was born
on July 1, 1911 in Harbin, Manchuria. His father S. Papanoff
was employed as a Police Officer with the Chinese Eastern
Railway since 1906. The applicant arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin in 1929 and soon afterwards obtained a position as a
driver with the China General Omnibus Company. In January
1931 he was engaged by the Shanghai Telephone Company where
he worked until September 15, 1932 when he resigned on his
own accord in order to open a second-hand store which he
operated until October 1933 when he obtained his present
position as a clerk with the Shanghai Power Company.

Zinaida Prohorovna PAPANOFF, nee Koloshnaya, wife
of the applicant, was born on August 11, 1911 in Harbin,
Manchuria. She married the applicant in Harbin in June
1929 and has since been residing together with him.

They have a daughter Elena born in Shanghai on
October 23, 1933.

Evdokia Stepanovna PAPANOFF, nee Dougaeff, mother
of the applicant, was born on March 1, 1886 in Maritime
Province, Siberia. She married applicant's father in 1904
and since had been residing together with him, first in
Harbin and then since 1930 in Shanghai. After the death of
the applicant's father in October 1936 she has been living
together with him.

All above mentioned persons are registered with the
Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to the characters of any member of Papanoff's
family.

D.C. (Special Branch).

谢尔盖·谢苗诺维奇·帕帕诺夫（Sergey Semenovitch PAPANOFF），俄罗斯人，1911年7月1日出生于满洲哈尔滨。其父 S. 帕帕诺夫自1906年起受雇于中东铁路担任警官。申请人于1929年从哈尔滨抵达上海，不久后在中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）获得司机职位。1931年1月，他受雇于上海电话公司，工作至1932年9月15日，随后自愿辞职以开设一家二手商店，经营至1933年10月，此后获得现任职位，在上海电力公司（Shanghai Power Company）担任职员。

济娜伊达·普罗霍罗芙娜·帕帕诺娃（Zinaida Prohorovna PAPANOFF），娘家姓科洛什纳亚（Koloshnaya），系申请人之妻，1911年8月11日出生于满洲哈尔滨。她于1929年6月在哈尔滨与申请人结婚，此后一直与申请人共同居住。

他们育有一女埃琳娜（Elena），1933年10月23日出生于上海。

叶夫多基娅·斯捷潘诺芙娜·帕帕诺娃（Evdokia Stepanovna PAPANOFF），娘家姓杜加耶夫（Dougaeff），系申请人之母，1886年3月1日出生于西伯利亚滨海省。她于1904年与申请人之父结婚，此后一直与其共同生活，先是在哈尔滨，自1930年起在上海。1936年10月申请人之父去世后，她便与申请人共同生活。

上述所有人员均在莫尔尼姆路118/1号的俄罗斯侨民委员会登记注册。

在工部局警务处的档案中，没有任何不利于帕帕诺夫家族任何成员品行的记录。

D.C.（特务科）。

弗雷德里克·尼基普罗维茨基（Frederic NIKIPROWIECKI），埃及籍，立陶宛裔，1904年4月4日出生于立陶宛奥什米亚内（Oshmiani）。他于1924年2月从法国抵达埃及开罗，并在那里居住，在各家公司担任职员，直至1933年6月。他于1933年7月从埃及抵达上海，不久后在位于中央商场12-14B室的阿尔方索·马里纳罗裁缝店（Alfonso Marinaro, Tailors）获得会计师职位。他在该商号工作至1936年初，随后获得现任职位，在圆明园路133号的 W. Koreska 文具制造商处担任销售员。

申请人持有1933年3月24日由开罗警方签发的第30315号通行证（Laissez-Passer）。

在工部局警务处的档案中，没有任何不利于其品行的记录。

Date November 25, 19 38

Subject M.L. Roubin, applicant for a certificate of character.

Made by J.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by C. Coates D.S.

Mihail Lazarevich ROUBIN ( Rubin ), Russian of Jewish origin, born on December 1, 1899 in Ekaterinoslav Province, South Russia. He is reported to have graduated from the Petrograd Polytechnic Institute in 1914 with the diploma of a Civil Engineer and to have served in the Russian army during the Great War. According to his own statement, he left Russia for China in 1920 and for the following three years resided in Harbin. He then left for the U.S.A., reportedly, on a mission on behalf of the Chinese Eastern Railway. In 1924 he arrived in Shanghai from America and soon afterwards established a business under the style " M.L. Roubin & Co, Engineers and Contractors ", 10 Canton Road, which he conducted until 1932, when he became a partner in the Far Eastern Salvage Company. In 1935 this company was amalgamated with the Far Eastern Salvage Association, 2 French Bund. According to Roubin, he severed his connections with the latter firm in November, 1938 in view of his intention to depart to Australia.

He is registered with the Russian Migrants' Committee, 118/1 Boulmein Road and the S.C.D. Police Bureau ( Reg. No 330 ) and at present resides at 816 Embankment Building, together with his wife, Mrs Evstolia Ivanovna Roubin nee Umshanoff, born 9-11-1911 at Suchedu, Chinese Eastern Railway, and their daughter and son born in Shanghai in 1935 and 1937, respectively.

He had two brothers in Shanghai, one of whom, J.M. Roubin, was killed in an explosion which took place during the course of salvage operations in the Yangtsze river near Nanking on 9-5-1932, and the other, A.L. Roubin, is reported to have left for Australia recently.

米哈伊尔·拉扎列维奇·鲁宾（Mihail Lazarevich ROUBIN，即 Rubin），俄籍犹太人，1899年12月1日出生于俄罗斯南部的叶卡捷琳诺斯拉夫省（Ekaterinoslav Province）。据报，他于1914年毕业于彼得格勒理工学院，获得土木工程师文凭，并在大战期间服役于俄国军队。据其自称，他于1920年离开俄国前往中国，随后三年居住在哈尔滨。此后，据称他代表中东铁路执行任务前往美国。1924年，他从美国抵达上海，不久后在广东路10号以“M.L. Roubin & Co, Engineers and Contractors”（M.L. 鲁宾工程承包商公司）的名义开展业务，一直经营至1932年，当时他成为远东打捞公司（Far Eastern Salvage Company）的合伙人。1935年，该公司与位于法租界外滩2号的远东打捞协会（Far Eastern Salvage Association）合并。据鲁宾称，鉴于其打算前往澳大利亚，他已于1938年11月断绝了与该公司的联系。

他在俄国移民委员会（地址：蒲石路118/1号）和工部局警务处（注册号 330）均有登记，目前与其妻子叶夫斯托利娅·伊万诺芙娜·鲁宾（Evstolia Ivanovna Roubin，娘家姓 Umshanoff，1911年11月9日出生于中东铁路苏家屯站）以及分别于1935年和1937年在上海出生的女儿和儿子，共同居住在外滩大厦816号。

他在上海有两个兄弟，其中一人 J.M. 鲁宾，于1932年5月9日在南京附近的长江打捞作业过程中发生的爆炸事故中丧生；另一人 A.L. 鲁宾，据报最近已前往澳大利亚。

Dear Sir,

I, the undersigned, Michael. L. Rubin, residing
at 516 Embankment Bldg. has applied to the Consulate General
for permit to enter Australia.
In accordance with the requirements of the application
Such is to be supported by a certificate from the Police
that neither myself nor any member of my family has
ever been in prison or in a mental hospital
I therefore beg to apply to you for such a certi-
ficate and hope that it will be issued to me.
I am pleased to give you the following particulars:
I have arrived in Shanghai on the 15th Aug 1924 from
U. S. of America and has been engaged in Engineering and
contracting work since. I have married second time in
July 1934 and have two children. My family will proceed
with me to Australia if permit is granted.
During the last four years, I am a director and partner
in a British firm "The Far Eastern Salvage Co."; % Wheelock
& Co. Ltd., 3 French Bund.
Hoping for your kind attitude with regard
to my application, I beg to remain, Dear Sir,

Yours faithfully,
M. L. Rubin.
